sops.title: Declare, coordinate and hand off an incident
sops.trigger: A critical alert, confirmed isolation/integrity failure or user-blocking critical journey.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Confirm alert freshness, affected environment/cell and source version. Determine control, execution, identity, financial, evidence and delivery impacts independently.
Establish incident commander, technical lead, communications lead and financial/security lead when relevant. Use an external channel if Aperture is affected.
Classify P1 immediately for verified disclosure, unauthorized authority, ledger mismatch or widespread unavailable critical tasks. P2 is bounded degradation without integrity loss.
sops.containment: Use the smallest reversible restriction consistent with current authority. Do not broaden access, bypass budget reservation or disable TLS to restore a green dashboard.
procedure: Open an incident record with initial blast radius and an explicit unknowns list.
Attach safe metric/query references; preserve original timestamps and hashes. Declare who can approve expansive recovery.
Give an initial impact statement and update cadence. Proposed targets are P1 acknowledgement within 5 minutes and updates every 15 minutes, subject to accepted staffing.
Delegate one hypothesis per investigator. Keep a shared UTC timeline of observations and actions, not an unreviewed command stream.
Handoff explicitly includes current mode, queued/dispatching/unknown counts, holds, active silences, pending changes and receiver uncertainty.
sops.verification: Incoming owner repeats the outstanding risks and next safe actions; monitoring and communication channels both work.
sops.rollback: Withdraw a mistaken incident severity only with recorded rationale; preserve events and state changes.
sops.escalation: Page security for suspected disclosure or compromised identity, FinOps for financial uncertainty, and storage owner for state corruption. Never rely only on R14 webhook delivery.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Recover monitoring and detect missing evidence
sops.applicability: Proposed telemetry plane plus current health/SQL
sops.trigger: AL-01/02/39/40 or a stale dashboard despite reported traffic.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Check independent expected-target inventory and scrape status. Missing series is not a value of zero.
Compare collection time, source time and query availability; verify clock offset before concluding export delay.
Inspect collector/export queue capacity, dropped-record counters and destination authentication without exporting payloads.
sops.containment: Preserve authoritative audit/financial state. Do not make critical decisions from stale charts. Use health probes and a bounded protected snapshot as a documented fallback.
procedure: Distinguish collection failure, exporter failure, storage/query failure and dashboard filter error.
Restore the affected pipeline with pinned configuration and narrowly scoped credentials. Increase buffers only within measured disk/memory limits.
Run a unique synthetic safe event through collection and query; record source/observed/query timestamps.
Recover queued telemetry with event deduplication. Replay evidence, never execution commands.
Reconcile blind-spot start/end against durable source tables and disclose permanent gaps.
sops.verification: Expected components are present, source timestamps advance, test events are queryable and zero drops persist for two observation windows.
sops.rollback: Revert the collector/configuration change through its deployment path. Retain buffered data securely and do not silently truncate queues.
sops.escalation: Incident commander if visibility over authorization, financial safety or multiple cells is lost; security if loss might conceal disclosure.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Investigate control-plane unavailability
sops.trigger: /health/control fails or sign-in and investigation are unavailable.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Check /health/live separately from /health/control and execution readiness. A Paused installation may have healthy control.
Verify one process owns the SQLite file, correct local disk mount, permissions, journal mode and versioned extensions.
Read safe ASGI errors for STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, invariant rejection or identity failure. Do not expose raw SQL/exception context.
sops.containment: If execution remains active but control cannot establish safe authority, use approved operating restriction or supervisor shutdown. Account for already dispatched work before restart.
procedure: Capture protected diagnostics and supervised process logs. Confirm exact origin and configured transport rather than switching to browser demo.
Use SOP-17/18 for lock or integrity conditions, SOP-15 for identity-only failure.
Restore access using the unchanged approved artifact and storage branch. Serving never runs migrations automatically.
After recovery validate current membership, service revision and command-receipt retrieval using a low-risk fixture account.
sops.verification: Control probe succeeds and authorized reads/negative tenant tests behave correctly; one successful /health/live is insufficient.
sops.rollback: Revert only compatible configuration changes. Do not launch an older binary against an upgraded schema or restore old authority in place.
sops.escalation: P1 if incident investigation/containment is unavailable or multiple tenants are blocked.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Recover a stuck execution queue or worker
sops.trigger: Old queued work, Serving without healthy execution worker or AL-04/05/13.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Compare Queued, Dispatching and Unknown inventories with current operating mode. Paused is intentionally frozen.
Inspect complete queue age and job/request correspondence, not recent 200-row UI lists.
Check worker loop evidence, SQLite lock waits and current service/workload/tenant restrictions. An alive loop does not prove progress.
sops.containment: Drain to stop new admissions while allowing eligible queued work to finish, or pause when existing queued dispatch itself is unsafe. Do not add a second server process.
procedure: Record current source counts and oldest request IDs.
Resolve underlying configuration/storage issue without changing queued request payloads or current grants.
For work no longer wanted, use explicit cancellation before durable dispatch intent (SOP-06).
If controlled restart is necessary, record Dispatching work first; recovery can classify it Unknown. Do not turn it back into Queued manually.
Use fresh exact-state resume plan only after current authority and balances verify.
sops.verification: Eligible queue age decreases, no duplicate attempt appears and financial holds match source requests; unrelated tenants remain isolated.
sops.rollback: Pause again if progress or invariants regress. Keep Unknown reservations rather than retrying upstream.
sops.escalation: Execution and storage owners; FinOps when interrupted work carries unresolved exposure.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Drain, pause and resume safely
sops.trigger: Planned maintenance or containment requiring installation-wide execution restriction.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Use ops-status to establish mode, counts and held exposure. Draining permits eligible queued dispatch; Paused does not.
Understand that notification sender and case observer continue outside Recovery. Disable approved notification routes separately when egress must stop.
sops.containment: Prefer Draining for planned shutdown. Use Paused for unsafe queued execution. Both preserve existing liabilities.
procedure: Create a protected change record naming the scope, reason, reviewer and maintenance expiry.
Apply drain or pause with explicit reference and inspect current counts. Do not infer a reconciled ledger from empty Queued work.
Complete maintenance under the appropriate storage/identity/release SOP.
Generate a fresh five-minute resume plan only after no durable Dispatching work remains and verify passes. Inspect its full effect, digest and unknown exposure.
Apply the plan with external acceptance reference. Add --acknowledge-unknown only after actual review; the option does not settle anything.
sops.verification: Operating revision advances, eligible control remains accessible, current authority remains unchanged, and a permitted fixture request reaches the expected outcome.
sops.rollback: Apply restrictive pause immediately if recovery fails. A state change, cancellation or settlement can make the previous resume plan stale; regenerate, never edit it.
sops.escalation: Incident commander must approve expansion of authority; operator reference is an attestation, not authenticated dual approval.
sops.commands:
python server.py --db "$DB" ops-status
python server.py --db "$DB" ops-drain --reason "Planned controlled maintenance" --reference "$CHANGE_REF"
# Use pause instead when queued dispatch is unsafe.
python server.py --db "$DB" ops-pause --reason "Contain uncertain execution" --reference "$CHANGE_REF"
python server.py --db "$DB" verify
python server.py --db "$DB" ops-resume-plan --out "$EVIDENCE/resume-plan.json"
# After independent inspection, while the plan is current:
python server.py --db "$DB" ops-resume --plan "$EVIDENCE/resume-plan.json" --reference "$ACCEPTANCE_REF"
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Cancel queued inference without fabricating upstream cancellation
sops.trigger: User withdraws a request or queued work should not dispatch.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Inspect current request state and source version. Ensure the request belongs to the authorized workspace.
Distinguish Queued from Dispatching. Browser disconnect and response loss do not prove that no provider work occurred.
sops.containment: Pause admission if broader scope is unsafe, but do not assume that pause cancels outstanding work.
procedure: Open Request Inspector, review state and use Cancel queued request with explicit reason through authenticated API/console.
Keep the same idempotency key if acknowledgement is lost. Retrieve existing receipt after reauthorization.
If dispatch won the transaction race, accept too-late rejection. Move to uncertain-dispatch procedure, not a manual refund.
Inspect request Not dispatched state, closed job, one release journal effect and absence of an attempt.
sops.verification: Exactly one release, no new attempt, liability preserved for any already dispatched request and current authorization enforced on replay.
sops.rollback: Cancellation is not undone by editing the record. New desired work requires a new explicit authorized intent.
sops.escalation: Execution owner for inconsistent state; ledger owner for unexpected release amount.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Investigate provider degradation and SLO burn
sops.applicability: Future real integration; R14 fixture only
sops.trigger: AL-07/08/09, elevated provider errors, latency or incorrect output behavior.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Confirm real versus synthetic environment, logical outcome denominator and time window. Replays/attempts must not inflate successful requests.

Verify healthy tenants receive defined fairness and no cross-scope cached/receipt data.
Measure label series count, log bytes/second, histogram series growth and query CPU.
Publish sustainable envelope, assumptions and exact artifact rather than a universal requests-per-second claim.
sops.verification: Performance objective and invariants hold within measured envelope; telemetry loss and cost remain within accepted budget.
sops.rollback: Restore previous admission cap and monitoring configuration after test; preserve results as nonproduction evidence.
sops.escalation: Platform/FinOps/product owners when cost, fairness or UX objectives conflict.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Recover a lost command acknowledgement
sops.trigger: Browser or network cannot establish whether a submitted command committed.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Keep exact original intent and logical key. Do not infer failure from a timeout or empty browser panel.
Reauthenticate or refresh scope when needed; current authority is checked before replay.
sops.containment: Disable accidental new submissions while explaining uncertainty. Do not switch to standalone demo.
procedure: Use Retry same command or fetch existing receipt through supported client path with unchanged content/key.
If receipt exists, present committed result and refresh dependent views; no second financial/execution action.
If same key with changed content conflicts, inspect original intent and create a new key only for a genuinely new reviewed command.
If authority revoked, accept denial and request authorized investigation; receipt existence is not access permission.
If one-time credential disclosure cannot safely be replayed, use supported rotation rather than exposing persisted secret material.
sops.verification: One committed effect, one logical execution/hold, accurate UI state and retained current authorization.
sops.rollback: No destructive rollback based only on missing response. Follow domain-specific reversal procedure after committed state is known.
sops.escalation: Platform owner for repeated receipt-loss defects, security for authorization discrepancy.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.
sops.closure: Incident owner confirms outcome against fresh source evidence and updates customer-facing status. A cleared alarm, successful probe or HTTP acknowledgement alone does not close the incident.
sops.review: Before production enablement, after source/contract change, and at least quarterly. Run on fixtures first.

sops.title: Investigate cost per accepted outcome without misleading savings
sops.trigger: Optimization recommendation, provider switch or cost anomaly.
sops.preconditions: Confirm environment, cell, source revision and incident/change reference. Use the least-privileged current identity. Do not paste secrets, prompts or private notes into a ticket. Use a protected evidence directory and UTC timestamps. Read-only SQL is for a trusted operator on a consistent snapshot, not a tenant-access API.
diagnose: Define a fixed workload cohort, business acceptance criterion, quality baseline, currency and accounting cutoff.
Separate known costs, outstanding liability, cache effects, retries, tools, reserved capacity and operator effort.
sops.containment: No automatic routing change from token price or synthetic quality score. Mandatory geography/privacy/capability constraints remain filters, not weighted preferences.
procedure: Join request/attempt/settlement to independently assessed outcome using authorized references.
Keep rejected/unknown outcomes in denominator policy explicitly; never treat all HTTP 2xx as accepted business results.
Compare alternatives on the same input/output workload and qualified capability; report uncertainty intervals and unallocated fees.
Prepare a proposal with exact evidence, expected savings and rollback trigger; independent review and activation remain required.
After rollout compare measured realized outcomes to forecast before claiming savings.
sops.verification: Cost reduction is reproducible at comparable accepted quality, latency and policy compliance, with residual financial uncertainty disclosed.
sops.rollback: Revert through a reviewed contract change when outcome quality or cost assumptions fail.
sops.escalation: Product/service owner and finance for disputed acceptance or accounting basis.
sops.evidence: Record incident/change reference, scope, exact artifact and configuration revisions, observation time, diagnostic result hashes, actors, commands/actions taken, before/after state and unresolved liabilities. Never attach raw credentials or unrestricted database files.

opsGates.title: Telemetry inventory
opsGates.criterion: Actual /metrics or collector capture records family/type/labels for each enabled metric; absence is not filled with fabricated values.

opsGates.title: Source agreement
opsGates.criterion: Each derived gauge equals a complete consistent source query; each event counter has one event/one increment semantics.

opsGates.title: Cardinality
opsGates.criterion: Producer denylist/allowlist and worst-case series budget tested before all-tenant rollout.

opsGates.title: Scope
opsGates.criterion: API, export, drill-down and direct diagnostic privileges are separately verified with negative tenant/workspace cases.

opsGates.title: Log schema
opsGates.criterion: Positive and negative schema cases, safe fields, source vs observed time and bounded reason enums pass.

opsGates.title: Sensitive data
opsGates.criterion: Seeded secrets and prompt markers never reach logs, labels, exemplars, audit summaries or external payloads.

opsGates.title: Correlation
opsGates.criterion: Edge/logical/attempt/provider/command IDs remain distinct; trace parentage and asynchronous links tested.

opsGates.title: SLI denominator
opsGates.criterion: Accepted intent, replay, denied request, timeout, Unknown, late completion and no-traffic behavior are agreed and tested.

opsGates.title: Rule parsing
opsGates.criterion: Exact Prometheus binary passes check rules and expression fixtures; no unobserved alarm dependency.

opsGates.title: Alert routing
opsGates.criterion: Exact Alertmanager binary validates configuration and approved out-of-band receivers receive a synthetic alert and recovery.

opsGates.title: Missing telemetry
opsGates.criterion: Scrape disappearance, stalled snapshots and future timestamps trigger independent detection.

opsGates.title: Burn rate
opsGates.criterion: Fast, slow, low-traffic, maintenance and no-traffic fixtures have expected outputs; thresholds tied to approved SLO.

opsGates.title: Unknown exposure
opsGates.criterion: Disconnect/worker crash/recovery retains held liability and opens actionable evidence without invented zero cost.

opsGates.title: Ledger
opsGates.criterion: Multi-request/multi-tenant independent aggregates detect a single introduced discrepancy; no join fanout or hierarchical double counting.

opsGates.title: SQLite contention
opsGates.criterion: Read diagnostics meet bounded timeout and do not write; competing queries cannot starve authorized writes beyond approved envelope.

opsGates.title: Recovery
opsGates.criterion: Protected backup restores in quarantine; source remains unchanged; post-backup exposure and independent-host recovery separately assessed.

opsGates.title: Signals
opsGates.criterion: Observer failure, recurrence, suppressed condition and stale evidence remain distinct from case ownership/closure.

opsGates.title: Notification
opsGates.criterion: DNS/TLS/signature failures, drops, duplicate receipt and expiry have safe bounded outcomes; pause and egress controls are separate.

opsGates.title: Identity
opsGates.criterion: Expired/revoked bindings and credentials fail before replay and dispatch; verification never automatically retries sensitive commands.

opsGates.title: Governed change
opsGates.criterion: Full reviewed content and current base checked, including rollback/restoration; deployment markers match actual runtime.

opsGates.title: External components
opsGates.criterion: Optional LiteLLM/PostgreSQL/Redis contracts verified on exact deployed versions; no inherited acceptance from R14.

opsGates.title: User experience
opsGates.criterion: Representative users complete J1/J2/J3 and explain pending authority and uncertainty; accessibility checked in supported native browsers.

opsGates.title: Retention and deletion
opsGates.criterion: Owners approve TTLs, legal holds, subject withdrawal, backups and receiver custody; exported evidence handling tested.

opsGates.title: Operational ownership
opsGates.criterion: Named on-call, security, finance, integration and product owners rehearse escalation, handoff and exit criteria before pilot sign-off.

findings.title: No unified metrics emission in R14
findings.risk: Published metric names could be mistaken for actual scrapeable series.
findings.recommendation: Build a bounded exporter/instrumentation layer and prove source-to-sample accounting; retain separate health probes.
findings.acceptance: Every enabled alert has emitted, type-checked, bounded labels and fresh expected-inventory coverage.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Development and ASGI access logs differ
findings.risk: A collector expecting ASGI JSON may miss development-server requests.
findings.recommendation: Declare the transport baseline and instrument the selected serving path; do not synthesize nonexistent request logs.
findings.acceptance: One accepted and one denied request visible in the actual selected transport with no sensitive fields.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: No native source timestamp or trace binding in access event
findings.risk: Misleading temporal order and failed joins between edge and durable work.
findings.recommendation: Preserve collector observed_at, leave source time null when absent, implement separate edge/request/attempt/trace mapping.
findings.acceptance: Out-of-order and missing-origin-time cases remain explicit; request_id not blindly treated as trace_id.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Administrative snapshot is not complete telemetry
findings.risk: Two hundred recent rows can undercount exposure and incidents.
findings.recommendation: Use complete authoritative aggregates and paginated authorized drill-down; never aggregate a truncated snapshot.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with over 200 requests yields full totals and a visible row limit on detail.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Health is not an inference or UX SLO
findings.risk: Successful process/worker probe can hide provider failure or broken sign-in.
findings.recommendation: Add non-sensitive, approved canaries and a deadline-based logical-request completion contract.
findings.acceptance: Controlled dependency failure violates the correct SLI while liveness may remain green.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Financial amounts are synthetic and units are not tokens
findings.risk: Mock micro-dollar records could be presented as a real invoice or model token measurement.
findings.recommendation: Keep synthetic/version dimensions visible and qualify actual provider usage/price/cost separately.
findings.acceptance: No fixture series included in real billing, savings or accepted-outcome dashboards.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Observer and sender need independent external alerts
findings.risk: A broken in-application detector or sender cannot reliably notify about itself.
findings.recommendation: Deploy external freshness/scrape monitors and an independent pager route.
findings.acceptance: Stop observer/sender and demonstrate out-of-band detection without using its failed pipeline.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Pause does not contain egress
findings.risk: Operators may pause inference while webhook metadata continues leaving.
findings.recommendation: Expose separate execution and notification containment actions and evidence.
findings.acceptance: A maintenance drill demonstrates pause, route disable and recovery quarantine distinctly.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Signal history has bounded run retention
findings.risk: Retained 256 runs are not durable compliance history or a monotonic lifetime sweep counter.
findings.recommendation: Export needed evidence under a reviewed retention policy and count completed sweeps at transition time.
findings.acceptance: Counter survives controlled exporter restart via checkpoint; historical gaps are not backfilled as observations.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Unknown outcome needs durable financial ownership
findings.risk: Expired counters or restored snapshots can obscure open liabilities.
findings.recommendation: Retain Unknown exposure and reconcile with independent evidence; compare post-backup dispatches before resumption.
findings.acceptance: Uncertain execution is never refunded just because a timer or incident closes.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Query access is privileged, not tenant authentication
findings.risk: Direct file access bypasses API scope checks; a SQL WHERE clause is not RLS.
findings.recommendation: Use protected snapshots and operator custody; offer tenant dashboards only through authorized services.
findings.acceptance: Cross-scope API/export tests and diagnostic custody review pass before user exposure.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Global metrics labels can expose identifiers
findings.risk: Unbounded or sensitive labels persist even when dashboards hide them.
findings.recommendation: Restrict producer labels, split secure financial views and inspect actual exposition without exporting label values.
findings.acceptance: No raw keys, email, IP, user agent, arbitrary paths or prompts in collected labels.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: No live LiteLLM/PG/Redis integration evidence
findings.risk: A collection of proposed queries can be mistaken for a qualified live stack.
findings.recommendation: Pin exact runtime/configuration and qualify all components together before enabling optional alarms.
findings.acceptance: Actual proxy and data-store failure cases with source-to-observation evidence, not mocks alone.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Resumption references are not verified dual approval
findings.risk: Trusted local operator reference can be misrepresented as authenticated organizational sign-off.
findings.recommendation: Record it as attestation; design enterprise two-person controls separately where required.
findings.acceptance: UI, runbooks and evidence never promote a local reference to signed approval.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: UX measures need genuine participants and coherent cohorts
findings.risk: Synthetic completion or cross-window counts can manufacture usability improvement.
findings.recommendation: Measure matched journey cohorts, assistance, comprehension and accessibility with representative participants.
findings.acceptance: Observe eligible denominator, abandoned cases and missing data; no statistical sufficiency claim from minimum sample alone.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

findings.title: Capacity and recovery targets remain unmeasured
findings.risk: One-process tests do not establish production concurrency, RPO or RTO.
findings.recommendation: Select capacity envelope, measure realistic contention and demonstrate independent-host restoration before deployment approval.
findings.acceptance: Approved workload limits and restoration evidence with acknowledged unresolved exposure.
findings.state: Open design/qualification work; no runtime patch applied by C2.

alignment.consolidated_resolution: Reader points current evidence to R14; R9 and earlier counts are labeled historical.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Historical originals remain unchanged.

alignment.issue: R14 receiver-first roadmap predates the LiteLLM integration candidate.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: One roadmap prioritizes patch/native qualification and durable integration; receiver acceptance remains a separate egress gate.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No promotion or customer approval is recorded.

alignment.issue: AP-ADR-004 proposes a Go execution kernel while RV-02 and the candidate favor qualified reuse.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Preserve the original Proposed ADR and add a reconsideration disposition rather than pretend Go is built or selected permanently.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Runtime selection needs accepted integration/performance evidence.

alignment.issue: Four proposed independently deployable roles can be mistaken for the single-node reference.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Architecture reader and handbook explicitly distinguish target roles from R14 modules/workers.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No independent production services are delivered.

alignment.issue: Proposed PostgreSQL/RLS and historical WAL references conflict with the actual R14 SQLite DELETE mode.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Current store and deployment matrix govern implementation; PostgreSQL and RLS remain proposed.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No database adapter or financial storage is changed.

alignment.issue: R9 mock core includes provisioning/qualification/hierarchical admission features not exposed by R14 persistent API.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Capability matrix identifies each surface; fifteen mock views are not nine server views with all features.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Missing server capabilities remain explicit.

alignment.issue: Target sketches, mock command catalogs, persistent OpenAPI and candidate Authority are distinct contracts.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Separate authoritative locators and complete 37-operation R14 index prevent interface conflation.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No new public candidate HTTP endpoint is invented.

alignment.issue: Transport tests can sound like an actual Aperture/LiteLLM integration.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Current baseline says the candidate is unconnected and durable Authority is unimplemented.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Real proxy, PostgreSQL/Redis and provider integration remain unrun.

alignment.issue: A PR mergeability result or source version could be misread as merge/release qualification.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Rechecked main/head, draft/unmerged state, check runs and reviews; source declaration is not stable image provenance.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No repository mutation or merge.

alignment.issue: Cumulative market report includes early-October “current/latest” statements.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Every comparison reader is prominently dated; later source review supersedes only pinned LiteLLM claims.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Market-wide re-research not performed.

alignment.issue: Successive reports repeat full ADR bodies and could inflate the decision inventory.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: 352 canonical records indexed once, with ten scopes and unchanged full text.
alignment.remaining_boundary: All remain Proposed, not accepted by test counts.

alignment.issue: Historical mock storage retains Released while current server uses Activated.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Use Activated as current prose while preserving legacy serialized values in their source scope.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No browser/server data migration is performed.

alignment.issue: Delivery has Cancelled; inference cancellation does not necessarily use a state of that name.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Preserve each schema’s distinct states; queued-only inference cancellation is not provider cancellation after dispatch.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Upstream cancellation remains unqualified.

alignment.issue: Local reservations or strict LiteLLM flags can be mistaken for universal invoice ceilings.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Separate estimator coverage, durable unknown exposure, local ledger, distributed rights and invoice reconciliation.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Actual provider pricing and distributed Authority remain unqualified.

alignment.issue: Local fingerprints and operator references can be mistaken for signatures or authenticated dual approvals.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Distinguish exact-content comparison, authenticated service review and trusted local-operator attestations.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Signed bundles and production approval assurance remain proposed.

alignment.issue: Webhook public-only destinations and candidate numeric internal gateways look inconsistent without context.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Define separate threat/route contracts; neither weakens the other.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No common permissive destination bypass is introduced.

alignment.issue: Paused execution can be read as stopping every background process or all egress.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Document independent inference, observer and notification controls; restore quarantine disables stale egress.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Installation pause is not a universal network kill switch.

alignment.issue: HTTP acceptance, acknowledgement and resolution can be conflated.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Keep receiver acceptance, human case ownership and source-rechecked resolution independent.
alignment.remaining_boundary: No exactly-once processing or guaranteed delivery claim.

alignment.issue: Repeated release suites and different units invite misleading cumulative totals.
alignment.consolidated_resolution: Retain version-bound results separately; C1 checks are new document/provenance checks only.
alignment.remaining_boundary: Historical product suites are not rerun or added together.

alignment.issue: Injected HTML, HTTP bridges and local TLS fixtures are useful but limited.

alignment.remaining_boundary: No conformance certificate or production security claim.

alignment.remaining_boundary: Real owners, participant results and external approvals remain absent.

decisions.title: Make the AI Service Contract the primary product object
decisions.disposition: Retained product direction. R14 models a narrow service contract; complete enterprise capability catalogs remain unqualified.
decisions.body:
Area Product & experienceSuggested owner Platform product architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

Provider-centric administration makes users coordinate model names, policy attachments, keys and budgets without a single statement of what an application is allowed to rely on. The product needs a stable unit of ownership and change.

Alternatives considered

Expose provider endpoints directly; use loosely related gateway entities; or introduce a versioned service contract. Direct endpoints are simplest for one provider but transfer governance coordination to every application.

Proposed decision

Use a tenant-scoped, versioned AI Service Contract containing protocol, capability, quality, processing, financial and lifecycle requirements. Resolve qualified implementations behind it. Make the same object visible in the console, APIs, delivery tools, request evidence and cost attribution. Do not advertise cross-provider interchangeability beyond its tested contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This reduces configuration ambiguity but adds catalog and contract maintenance. Specialized provider APIs remain separate qualified contracts. A small single-provider application may correctly choose direct native access instead.

Required validation

Test whether users can identify owner, permissions, destinations and cost envelope from one service view. Run the same contract fixtures against each eligible target.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when the service abstraction loses required native semantics or creates more application exceptions than it removes.

Related decisions AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-020 AP-ADR-036

Evidence [R08]

decisions.title: Separate administrative hierarchy from physical placement
decisions.disposition: Partial local scope model. Tenant/workspace membership exists, but dedicated placement is not implied.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Tenant platform leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Teams often confuse billing labels, workspaces and isolation boundaries. That confusion permits accidental cross-tenant joins and creates misleading promises about dedicated infrastructure.

Alternatives considered

Flat API keys; tenant equals namespace; or explicit organization/tenant/workspace/service resources with independent cell placement. A namespace alone cannot describe all security and recovery boundaries.

Proposed decision

Treat tenant as an authorization and financial boundary, workspace as organization/environment, and cell assignment as a placement and failure-isolation decision. Include verified scope in every resource aggregate, job and evidence record. Expose the isolation manifest rather than infer exclusivity from a product label.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More explicit identifiers and migrations are required. Tenant movement must reconcile state, keys, jobs and financial grants. A workspace cannot be moved across tenants by editing a billing tag.

Required validation

Enumerate cross-tenant negative tests for every API family and export. Verify cell assignment independently of labels, queue names and cost centers.

Revisit trigger

Revisit if business tenancy changes or a customer requires an additional legal or sovereign trust boundary.

Related decisions AP-ADR-006 AP-ADR-007 AP-ADR-008 AP-ADR-016

decisions.title: Start with a modular control plane and four deployable roles
decisions.disposition: Target only as independently deployed roles. R14 is a single-node Python application with local workers.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Platform engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A large microservice architecture would add network failure modes before domain boundaries are proven. A single process for all functions would instead mix administrative authority, content handling and financial correctness.

Alternatives considered

One all-purpose binary; many small network services; or a modular control plane with separate execution and admission roles. Choose service boundaries for authority and recovery, not repository aesthetics.

Proposed decision

Package Control API and Control Worker from one modular Go codebase. Deploy Execution Kernel and Admission Service separately in each cell with narrowly scoped credentials. Keep catalog, tenant, compiler and change modules inside the control application until measured load or independent ownership justifies extraction.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Transactional control workflows stay simple, but module boundaries require discipline and independent tests. Execution and admission introduce a deliberate network dependency whose latency and availability must be qualified.

Required validation

Exercise each role with only its declared credentials. Verify an execution compromise cannot alter approvals and a control outage does not become an unbounded request-path dependency.

Revisit trigger

Revisit extraction when a module has independently measured scaling, security or release requirements.

Related decisions AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-031

Evidence Original design decision; evaluate against the stated acceptance gates.

decisions.title: Use a small Go execution kernel with build-time adapters
decisions.disposition: RECONSIDER alongside RV-02. Go is a proposed runtime choice, not implemented or accepted. Qualify reuse of LiteLLM before selecting a replacement kernel.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Runtime leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Repeated parsing across proxy scripts, callback layers and sidecars can produce conflicting semantics and retry ownership. A language rewrite alone does not prove an architectural improvement.

Alternatives considered

Extend an incumbent proxy; build a Rust kernel; or implement one typed Go kernel with constrained adapters. Existing ingress remains useful for transport without owning AI semantics.

Proposed decision

Use Go initially for kernel and control implementation. Parse each approved protocol once, retain a typed request view and execute one explicit plan. Ship reviewed adapters at build time. Use existing ingress for transport limits but disable independent provider retries. Optimize native hot paths only after profiling a qualified workload.

Consequences and tradeoffs

A common language lowers integration overhead but introduces garbage-collection and allocation considerations. Owning adapters creates a maintenance commitment; the capability matrix limits that commitment to supported combinations.

Required validation

Measure allocation, active streams, cancellation, serialization, connection reuse and p99 admission overhead under the reference load. Compare with an incumbent under identical policy settings.

Revisit trigger

Revisit the runtime language or adapter boundary only when reproducible measurements show a material bottleneck.

Related decisions AP-ADR-003 AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-021 AP-ADR-039

decisions.title: Qualify normalized and native APIs independently
decisions.disposition: Candidate covers only plain-text nonstreaming Chat Completions. Other normalized/native protocols are not qualified.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner API architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Common request syntax does not establish common tool behavior, structured output, reasoning, resource ownership or billing semantics. Lossy translation can appear successful while breaking the application.

Alternatives considered

Universal normalization; unrestricted passthrough; or a small normalized contract plus explicitly approved native contracts. Both extremes obscure important constraints.

Proposed decision

Publish conformance per provider/account/model/version/endpoint/geography/capability tuple. Reject unsupported fields. Preserve approved provider-specific extensions without allowing endpoint or credential overrides. Native APIs use the same tenant and governance boundaries but have independent lifecycle and acceptance evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The catalog becomes larger and support is deliberately bounded. Applications gain explicit incompatibility errors rather than silently degraded behavior. Some advanced features remain provider-bound.

Required validation

Test schemas, error details, streaming events, tools, context limits, usage and provider-owned IDs. Negative tests must prove that native routes do not bypass mandatory controls.

Revisit trigger

Revisit an abstraction when upstream protocol changes or an application needs a capability outside the existing contract.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-020 AP-ADR-021 AP-ADR-023

decisions.title: Derive identity and scope from verified authority
decisions.disposition: Partial local implementation plus optional OIDC. Enterprise IdP, workload identity and browser deployment still need qualification.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Identity and security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Client-supplied tenant labels, cost metadata and tool descriptions are not proof of authority. Human administration, application workloads and delegated end users need distinct lifecycles.

Alternatives considered

Shared API keys; caller-selected tenant headers; or short-lived verified identity with explicit scoped grants. Long-lived emergency keys remain an exception with recovery controls.

Proposed decision

Use OIDC for human access through a BFF and short-lived audience-bound workload credentials. Resolve tenant and grants server-side. Authenticate internal services with approved workload identity. Keep original end-user authorization distinct from gateway identity when calling retrieval or business tools.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Identity-provider and key-rotation integration are required. Cached verification material has bounded age. The platform must explain access failures without disclosing foreign resource existence.

Required validation

Test wrong issuer/audience, expiration, revoked grants, forged tenant metadata, provider-token reuse and cross-object access. Verify support access has an independent expiry and audit trail.

Revisit trigger

Revisit for new federation, delegated-user or sovereign trust requirements.

Related decisions AP-ADR-002 AP-ADR-008 AP-ADR-014 AP-ADR-025

decisions.title: Offer pooled, dedicated and sovereign isolation explicitly
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. Pooled/dedicated/sovereign product editions are not delivered.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Infrastructure security architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

A tenant may need stronger isolation than row filtering, while smaller tenants benefit from shared infrastructure. Calling every topology dedicated obscures real exposure.

Alternatives considered

Only shared infrastructure; one complete installation per tenant; or graduated isolation using the same contract/API model. The choice should match risk and operations capacity.

Proposed decision

Define manifests for pooled cells, exclusive tenant cells and separate sovereign installations. State exclusivity for processes, nodes, networks, ledgers, keys, evidence and administrator access. Keep the service API consistent. Add dedicated cells only when requirements justify their cost.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Dedicated operation increases infrastructure and upgrade overhead. A dedicated runtime does not remove a shared management administrator from the threat model. Tenant movement becomes a controlled state migration.

Required validation

Inspect the actual infrastructure and credential boundary against the declared manifest. Run noisy-neighbor and cross-tenant tests on pooled operation and recovery drills on dedicated stores.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when threat classification, performance isolation or contractual geography changes.

Related decisions AP-ADR-002 AP-ADR-006 AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-031

decisions.title: Use object authorization plus database row-security defense
decisions.disposition: Object-level checks are locally implemented. PostgreSQL/RLS is not implemented or qualified.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Data security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Correct API scoping is essential but can regress in exports, joins or background tasks. Database protections provide a second boundary only when roles and pooling behavior are configured correctly.

Alternatives considered

Application filters only; per-tenant database everywhere; or object checks plus row security for pooled stores and separate databases for stronger isolation.

Proposed decision

Apply action/object authorization before queries and tenant-aware primary/foreign keys. Use non-owner application database roles without BYPASSRLS, enforce row policies where appropriate and set verified scope transaction-locally. Separate migration/owner credentials. Treat background jobs and exports as ordinary authorized callers.

Consequences and tradeoffs

RLS complicates administration and migrations, and it does not constrain privileged database owners. Pool leakage and unsafe session-setting interfaces must be tested explicitly. Dedicated databases remain available for stronger boundaries.

Required validation

Test foreign rows through every query family, transaction rollback, prepared statements, connection reuse and restore. Verify runtime roles cannot alter scope or policies through exposed SQL.

Revisit trigger

Revisit if a data store cannot express reliable scoped constraints or a tenant requires independent restoration.

Related decisions AP-ADR-002 AP-ADR-006 AP-ADR-027 AP-ADR-033

decisions.title: Compose mandatory policy by intersection and explicit deny
decisions.disposition: Narrow local rules exist. General mandatory-policy compilation/intersection remains proposed.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Policy architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Last-writer configuration precedence permits a convenient child or request setting to weaken a parent control. Operators need one understandable effective policy.

Alternatives considered

Last setting wins; arbitrary plugin ordering; or a typed deny-preserving composition model. Flexibility that changes authority must be explicit rather than implicit precedence.

Proposed decision

Define policy fields with typed composition: intersect allowed sets, union denies, minimize maxima and maximize required floors. Requests can choose only within the result. Reject conflicting, unbounded or unsupported policies at compilation. Include provenance for every effective value and safe reason codes at evaluation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some provider options become unavailable until a contract explicitly delegates them. The compiler is security-critical and requires generated negative tests. Arbitrary policies are not exposed as an unrestricted UI editor.

Required validation

Property-test monotonicity over generated parent/child/request combinations, including absent, empty, wildcard and alternate-protocol cases.

Revisit trigger

Revisit only with a formal rule for new policy types that preserves mandatory authority.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-036

decisions.title: Distribute immutable signed contract bundles with bounded validity
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. Local reviewed-content fingerprints are not signed distributed policy bundles.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Release security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Hot configuration reloads are useful but can expose partial objects, untrusted updates or indefinitely stale grants. Request handling needs a consistent approved view.

Alternatives considered

Read the control database per request; permit direct runtime edits; or distribute signed immutable snapshots with explicit activation and expiry.

Proposed decision

Compile a complete artifact containing contracts, eligibility, policy, grant epoch, price references, validity and kernel compatibility. Verify signer, digest, schema, epoch and age before atomic activation. Retain one revision per in-flight admission and emit a cell receipt. Invalid updates never produce a permissive empty state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Artifact distribution and trust-root rotation become operational responsibilities. Signed does not imply fresh or correct; expiry and authorization age can reduce outage availability.

Required validation

Inject altered, unsigned, expired, incompatible and downgraded artifacts. Test cold starts, clock skew, partial download and request concurrency during activation.

Revisit trigger

Revisit bundle granularity when cell size or update rates create measurable distribution cost.

Related decisions AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-013 AP-ADR-014

decisions.title: Give configuration one declared owner across UI, Git and IaC
decisions.disposition: Target ownership contract. LiteLLM settings ownership must be exposed and reconciled; no Git/IaC reconciler is implemented.
decisions.body:
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Developer experience leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Multiple configuration surfaces can overwrite each other and make incidents impossible to reconstruct. A familiar declarative tool must not bypass review.

Alternatives considered

File wins; database wins; last write wins; or explicit resource ownership with all writers using the same domain commands.

Proposed decision

Mark resources as Git-managed or API-managed and reject conflicting writes with an actionable source reference. Console, CLI, Terraform and Kubernetes integrations submit typed ChangeSets with base versions. Ownership transfer and emergency exceptions are themselves reviewed, expiring changes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Users cannot freely edit every field in every interface. The product must explain the ownership source clearly and provide a legitimate transfer workflow. Drift becomes a first-class state.

Required validation

Submit conflicting writes through every interface, including emergency tooling. Verify no path mutates a runtime or database field outside the change protocol.

Revisit trigger

Revisit ownership granularity when teams need delegated field-level management with a provable conflict model.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-013 AP-ADR-029

decisions.title: Require independent approval of an exact immutable proposal
decisions.disposition: Locally exercised independent service/workload/budget review. Local-operator egress/maintenance attestations are a different, weaker authority path.
decisions.body:
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Governance ownerDate 8 October 2026

Context

A generic approval label does not show what was reviewed or whether the author could self-approve. Editing after review invalidates the meaning of approval.

Alternatives considered

Immediate updates; external ticket references; or approvals tied to a typed proposal digest and exact base resource versions.

Proposed decision

Freeze the ChangeSet at review, require a distinct authorized reviewer, and bind approval to its digest, scope, tests and expiry. Recheck authority and versions at release. Material edits create a new version. Financial expansion requires a permitted financial approver; higher-risk changes can require multiple disciplines.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Review adds friction for meaningful changes. Safe delegated actions must have explicit pre-approved envelopes rather than informal bypasses. Emergency authority is a separate time-limited protocol.

Required validation

Test self-approval, withdrawn grants, edited proposals, expired approvals, stale base versions and releases through alternate APIs.

Revisit trigger

Revisit review thresholds using measured operator burden and incident data, without removing digest binding.

decisions.title: Distinguish desired, approved, active and healthy state
decisions.disposition: Distinct states are retained. Synthetic/local observation is not proof of a healthy live model deployment.
decisions.body:
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Release engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

An API save or orchestration acknowledgement does not prove that the intended configuration runs in every target cell. Green deployment labels can conceal partial application.

Alternatives considered

Treat save as success; display deployment tool status only; or model release distribution and runtime receipts independently.

Proposed decision

Record a release operation with target cells, approved digest, canary plan and observed receipts. Expose partial activation and health gates. Rollback constructs a new approved release against current mandatory policy; it does not rewrite history or revive revoked grants.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The UI needs more states and correlation identifiers, but they correspond to real distinctions. Old/new revisions may coexist during a canary, so each request records its exact contract.

Required validation

Partition a target cell, delay receipts, fail health checks and change policy during a rollback. Verify the console never labels incomplete activation as fully healthy.

Revisit trigger

Revisit rollout strategy as deployment scale and workload blast radius change.

decisions.title: Make revocation freshness an explicit availability tradeoff
decisions.disposition: Local grant/binding rechecks exist. Distributed epoch propagation and offline revocation bounds remain unproved.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Security operations leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Last-known configuration can preserve availability during an outage but may continue authorizing access after revocation. The acceptable window depends on data sensitivity.

Alternatives considered

Online authorization for every request; indefinite cached grants; or bounded locally evaluated authorization with epochs and explicit stale behavior.

Proposed decision

Use monotonic authorization epochs and short-lived grants. Distribute revocations with high priority and report acknowledgement coverage. Restricted services stop new admission when the approved age bound expires; public services may use separately approved longer bounds. Existing work follows an explicit cancellation/exposure policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Partitions can intentionally deny otherwise valid requests. Shorter windows require more reliable distribution and clock management. Revocation cannot retroactively erase output or guarantee upstream cancellation.

Required validation

Test partitions, delayed updates, expired grants, clock skew, persisted snapshots and key rotation. Measure the actual worst-case continued-admission window.

Revisit trigger

Revisit freshness bounds through accountable data-owner approval and tested reliability tradeoffs.

Related decisions AP-ADR-006 AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-013 AP-ADR-030

decisions.title: Separate strict financial admission from analytics and rate limits
decisions.disposition: SQLite local financial admission exists for synthetic requests. Candidate has an external Authority port; distributed strict guarantees are not proved.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Financial systems leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Completed-usage counters and dashboards cannot prevent every concurrent dispatch that creates economic exposure. Capacity and provider token limits answer different questions from spending authorization.

Alternatives considered

Retrospective counters only; approximate local reservations; or an authoritative regional transactional admission service for strict workloads.

Proposed decision

Require a durable reservation before any bounded billable attempt. Maintain integer-currency account balances, idempotent identities, known settlement and unresolved exposure. Financial unavailability denies strict new work. Optional advisory-only budgets must be a separately labeled contract, never an automatic fallback.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Transactions add latency and can reduce availability or utilization. Unknown pricing requires rejection or an explicitly accepted risk envelope. The guarantee concerns admitted modeled exposure, not all possible provider invoice charges.

Required validation

Run synchronized near-limit admissions, duplicate requests, database failover, rollback and missing-usage tests. Verify conservation and absence of provider attempts without admission IDs.

Revisit trigger

Revisit implementation only with evidence that the replacement preserves authority under concurrency and failure.

Related decisions AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-017 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-019

decisions.title: Partition regional spending rights and never reclaim by timeout alone
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. No implemented regional spending-right allocation or multi-node reclamation.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Distributed systems leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A global financial ceiling is difficult to enforce with independently writable regional counters. Lease expiry does not prove that an isolated old spender stopped using its rights.

Alternatives considered

One synchronous global ledger; eventually consistent totals; or bounded regional grants with explicit transfer and fencing.

Proposed decision

Start with one writer region per financial account. Delegate nonoverlapping grants to cells only through a durable allocator. Reclaim rights after sealing, fencing and reconciling consumption and unknown attempts, not merely after elapsed lease time. Quarantine restored grants until current authority is established.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Rights may be stranded during a partition and regional recovery may require a write-off or additional separately approved funding. This deliberately favors conservation over perfect utilization.

Required validation

Model grant conservation and test split connectivity, stale writers, delayed settlement, duplicate transfer and snapshots restored after reallocation.

Revisit trigger

Revisit regional mobility only after formal and fault-injection evidence proves safe transfers.

Related decisions AP-ADR-007 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-033

decisions.title: Track logical intent, individual attempts and uncertain dispatch
decisions.disposition: Locally exercised durable intent and uncertainty. Live upstream attempt/idempotency behavior remains unqualified.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Runtime reliability leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

One user request can generate several provider executions. Retrying after a timeout can duplicate both cost and side effects without the client knowing.

Alternatives considered

Untracked retries; global request IDs only; or a logical-request/attempt state machine with scoped idempotency.

Proposed decision

Use a tenant/service-scoped client intent key and material request hash. Assign an ID to each provider attempt. Durably mark possible dispatch before sending and distinguish known rejection, completed usage and unknown outcome. Do not claim provider idempotency unless the exact provider contract supplies it.

Consequences and tradeoffs

A crash around external dispatch can leave unresolved records. That is honest uncertainty, not an implementation failure to conceal. Recovery may be slower than blind retry.

Required validation

Crash before and after local commit, send, provider acceptance, first output and settlement. Replay same and changed payloads with one key.

Revisit trigger

Revisit attempt granularity when new tool, batch or stateful provider contracts are introduced.

Related decisions AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-021

decisions.title: Preserve unknown cost and reconcile with explicit adjustments
decisions.disposition: Local unknown/settlement semantics exist. No provider billing join or external invoice reconciliation is implemented.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner FinOps ownerDate 8 October 2026

Context

Late usage, missing trailers, external account activity and invoice aggregation prevent perfect request-level billing in every integration. Zero is an incorrect representation of unknown.

Alternatives considered

Estimate and overwrite; release after timeout; or retain unresolved authority and maintain separate estimate, usage and invoice facts.

Proposed decision

Keep unknown outcomes reserved until reconciled or covered by an approved write-off. Record price/usage corrections as adjustments, not silent history edits. Match invoices at the provider-supported granularity and expose remaining differences and confidence. Require accountable review above delegated write-off thresholds.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Financial views are more complex than a single spend total. Some accounts can remain unresolved for a long period, and conservative exposure reduces usable allowance.

Required validation

Exercise missing usage, invoice-only charges, actual cost above estimate, zero-cost confirmed outcomes, duplicate settlement and account-level unmatched differences.

Revisit trigger

Revisit matching adapters and risk allowances when provider billing identifiers or contracts improve.

Related decisions AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-017 AP-ADR-019

decisions.title: Version prices and qualify the reservation estimator
decisions.disposition: Synthetic price revisions exist. A qualified real-provider worst-case estimator is still required.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner FinOps engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Rates, token categories, service tiers and ancillary charges can change independently of model names. An unversioned price lookup cannot explain a historic admission decision.

Alternatives considered

Hardcoded current prices; runtime web lookup; or approved versioned price books with estimator conformance.

Proposed decision

Include provenance, currency, effective dates and covered billing dimensions in the price book. Record its revision in every admission. Bound input, output, recovery and auxiliary service exposure. Reject strict routes with unknown upper-bound semantics unless an explicit risk allowance covers the uncertainty.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Price administration is a release responsibility. Conservative estimation can strand funds and dynamic provider behavior may prevent a complete bound. The system must surface exclusions plainly.

Required validation

Test integer arithmetic, currency rounding, token categories, cache rates, media units, tool charges, price transitions and missing catalog entries.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after provider billing changes or observed estimation error exceeds the accepted envelope.

Related decisions AP-ADR-004 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-020

decisions.title: Optimize only inside qualified capability and quality constraints
decisions.disposition: Prototype/advisory only. Synthetic comparisons do not demonstrate production quality-adjusted savings.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Model quality leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

The cheapest response is not necessarily the cheapest successful task. Behavioral, privacy and context differences can make a syntactically compatible fallback unsafe.

Alternatives considered

Lowest price; latency-only routing; or constrained eligibility followed by a measured cost/quality objective.

Proposed decision

First filter targets by authorization, processing geography, protocol/features, context and task-quality gates. Optimize only among eligible candidates. Store evaluation-set version and confidence. Produce reviewable recommendations; measure realized cost per accepted outcome after a controlled release.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Fewer targets may remain during an incident, reducing availability. Evaluation requires maintained application datasets and can itself incur cost. Synthetic scores in the prototype are not qualification evidence.

Required validation

Use held-out workload tests, excluded-destination tests and fallback checks. Compare actual task acceptance, total attempts and economics under the same workload.

Revisit trigger

Revisit thresholds when task requirements, drift or new models materially change the decision boundary.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-038

decisions.title: Make streaming completion and output enforcement explicit
decisions.disposition: Target only for live streaming. The candidate explicitly excludes streaming.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Streaming runtime leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Once content is sent to a user, a later inspection cannot retract it. HTTP success can precede an incomplete stream or missing usage.

Alternatives considered

Always incremental output; always buffer; or per-contract incremental/buffered modes with a truthful enforcement guarantee.

Proposed decision

Use explicit streaming modes and one response state machine. Mandatory preventive output checks require buffering unless a proven safe segmentation contract exists. Stop transparent model fallback after user-visible output. Record incomplete outcomes and cancellation uncertainty separately from HTTP status.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Buffering increases memory and first-byte latency. Incremental mode may support detection/intervention rather than complete prevention. Some endpoints will remain unsupported under strict content requirements.

Required validation

Test split markers, malformed/partial tool arguments, slow readers, disconnects, missing trailers and inspector failures before and after first output.

Revisit trigger

Revisit segmented streaming only with a demonstrable safety boundary for the specific content and inspector.

decisions.title: Default response reuse off and partition eligible caches by authority
decisions.disposition: Response reuse is not qualified. LiteLLM namespace mechanisms require identity-derived partition tests.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Application data architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

Response reuse can leak tenant data or return an answer valid for a different authorization context. Similar wording does not establish equivalent business meaning.

Alternatives considered

Global exact/semantic caching; no cache ever; or opt-in contract-qualified reuse with explicit partitioning.

Proposed decision

Disable response caching initially. Enable exact reuse only for proven eligible tasks with tenant/principal authorization, contract/model/policy revision, request semantics and retrieval snapshot in the protected key. Keep stateful and side-effecting work out. Qualify semantic reuse separately with false-hit limits.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Lower cache-hit rates are acceptable when they preserve correctness. Invalidation and retention are real operating obligations. Provider prompt caching remains a different feature with its own data contract.

Required validation

Test foreign tenants and principals, changed retrieval grants, policy/model changes, stale entries, revoked callers and semantically misleading near-duplicates.

Revisit trigger

Revisit eligibility only after workload-specific quality and privacy evidence supports broader reuse.

decisions.disposition: Proposed only. Stateful provider resources are outside the candidate.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Stateful services leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Files, response IDs, sessions and asynchronous jobs may belong to a specific provider account. An alias cannot safely migrate those objects by changing its target.

Alternatives considered

Forward arbitrary provider IDs; expose raw provider state without registry; or maintain a scoped resource registry and explicit affinity.

Proposed decision

Register creation owner, authorized workload/user scope, provider/account binding, lifecycle, expiry and deletion obligations for each stateful object. Reauthorize every retrieval, poll, cancellation and deletion. Require explicit reconstruction or completion before changing provider ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Additional registry state and cleanup jobs are necessary. Portability is intentionally limited where upstream state is not transferable. The initial release can exclude protocols whose lifecycle is not qualified.

Required validation

Test cross-tenant IDs, key rotation, creator removal, alias changes, delayed job completion, duplicate cancellation and provider deletion failure.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when providers expose safe export/import or interoperable state contracts.

decisions.title: Preserve original user authorization through retrieval
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. No implemented qualified retrieval-authorization path.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Enterprise data leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A retrieval service using a broad gateway identity can return documents the end user is not allowed to see. Cache and embedding systems can magnify that error.

Alternatives considered

Gateway-wide retrieval credentials; application-managed retrieval only; or a separate approved broker preserving end-user scope and source ACLs.

Proposed decision

Keep business authorization at the retrieval/source system. A broker uses verified delegated identity, approved sources and explicit query/resource scope. Required validation

Test document ACL changes, removed group membership, source deletion, cross-tenant index queries, cache hits and wrong-audience delegation.

Revisit trigger

Revisit each connector when its authorization model or supported delegation changes.
