decisions.title: Isolate tool execution and authorize business actions separately
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. No production tool executor or delegated business-object authority.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Agent security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Model-generated tool calls can create side effects. Discovery rights, tool-server authentication and business-resource authorization are different decisions.

Alternatives considered

Execute tools in the model proxy; trust tool annotations; or use a separate execution boundary with explicit grants.

Proposed decision

Place MCP/tool execution in a separate runtime and credential domain. Validate server/tool/operation grants, token audience, delegated identity, arguments and transaction idempotency. Require human approval for specified high-impact actions. The business service remains authoritative for the actual transaction.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Tool integration needs more setup and some workflows require an additional user decision. This is preferable to letting the model convert descriptive text into execution authority.

Required validation

Test discovery-only principals, removed grants, injected arguments, token passthrough, replayed side effects and sessions crossing tenants or identities.

Revisit trigger

Revisit with each new protocol version or high-impact tool category; do not inherit chat qualification.

decisions.title: Classify safety checks by enforcement time and data egress
decisions.disposition: Proposed only for a general safety pipeline. Local transport and policy restrictions do not implement all safety checks.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner AI safety and privacy leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A configured guardrail can be preventive, detective or ineffective for a particular endpoint. Remote checks also create data destinations and sometimes billable work.

Alternatives considered

Global guardrail toggle; application-only inspection; or explicit contract-level placement, failure and egress semantics.

Proposed decision

Include each inspector in the processing graph with payload scope, destination, retention, cost and fail behavior. Preventive input checks complete before protected dispatch. Preventive output checks complete before delivery. Do not describe sampled or post-delivery checks as complete prevention.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Required inspectors can add latency and lower availability. Their service agreements and data policies become part of the AI service. Some combinations must fail compilation rather than quietly skip checks.

Required validation

Inject known markers through every supported endpoint and error path, including streaming boundaries, cache hits, tools and inspector timeouts.

Revisit trigger

Revisit enforcement modes only after endpoint-specific evidence supports the stronger claim.

Related decisions AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-021

decisions.title: Keep financial, operational and audit evidence distinct but linked
decisions.disposition: Local operational/financial/audit records are linked. External evidence collection and immutable retention remain pending.
decisions.body:
Area Observability & UXSuggested owner Observability architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

One universal log store mixes incompatible retention, cardinality, privacy and accounting responsibilities. An analytics delay must not change spending authority.

Alternatives considered

Everything in request logs; one shared event stream as authority; or separate data products linked by stable identities.

Proposed decision

Use the transactional ledger for finance, operational projections for diagnosis and independently retained audit evidence for authority changes. Connect them with tenant, request, attempt, contract and event IDs. Export via transactional outboxes with deduplication and gap detection; projections never authorize requests.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Operators need clear source and freshness labels when joining views. At-least-once export means consumers must handle duplicates. Retained evidence needs separate access and recovery ownership.

Required validation

Delay and duplicate exports, rebuild projections, detect sequence gaps and verify financial outcomes do not depend on analytics availability.

Revisit trigger

Revisit projection technology when query scale warrants specialized analytics, preserving authority boundaries.

Related decisions AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-028 AP-ADR-035

decisions.title: Collect no prompt, response or tool content by default
decisions.disposition: R14 uses metadata-only synthetic execution. The candidate may handle actual text in memory; host logging/retention must be qualified before live use.
decisions.body:
Area Observability & UXSuggested owner Privacy engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Content-rich tracing is useful for debugging but can create an uncontrolled secondary data store with different access and deletion requirements.

Alternatives considered

Capture all payloads; disable observability entirely; or metadata-first evidence with controlled purpose-bound capture exceptions.

Proposed decision

Instrument identities, versions, decisions, cost and timing without content. Any production content capture requires approved purpose, scope, retention, region, access and expiry. Use separate storage and entitlements. Audit exports and support bundles remain content-minimized.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some debugging requires explicitly authorized reproduction or temporary capture. The UI must distinguish missing content by design from missing telemetry due to failure. Redaction alone is not a substitute for minimization.

Required validation

Scan success, error, retry, adapter, tool and tracing paths with sensitive markers. Test exception expiry and deletion across active stores and restored backups.

Revisit trigger

Revisit collection only for a documented diagnostic need with privacy-owner acceptance.

decisions.title: Run bounded durable automations with proposal-only authority by default
decisions.disposition: Three fixed observers and a durable notification sender exist. General authorable automation and autonomous remediation are not delivered.
decisions.body:
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Automation platform leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Automation should remove repetitive work without becoming an unreviewed superuser. Crash/retry behavior must not duplicate side effects or approvals.

Alternatives considered

Arbitrary scripts in the gateway; broad model-driven administration; or predefined durable state machines with narrow envelopes.

Proposed decision

Use the Control Worker for idempotent provisioning, validation, release, export and reconciliation steps. Store job state and outbox effects transactionally. Rules normally create evidence or ChangeSets. Automatic intervention is limited to a separately pre-approved reversible containment envelope.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The initial product is not a general workflow engine. New workflows require explicit state, failure and authority contracts. An existing enterprise orchestrator may host the same protocol without widening permissions.

Required validation

Test crashed workers, duplicate triggers, stale leases, deadline expiry, cancelled jobs and attempts by automation to approve or increase its own authority.

Revisit trigger

Revisit a general engine only when demonstrated workflow complexity exceeds the bounded worker model.

decisions.title: Operate without the control plane only inside declared bounds
decisions.disposition: Proposed distributed operation. R14 depends on its local control store; no offline signed-bundle execution cell is implemented.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Reliability architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

Control-plane independence improves availability, but unlimited stale execution conflicts with revocation, capability retirement and financial authority.

Alternatives considered

Require online control for all calls; allow indefinite stale operation; or permit bounded local execution under explicit policy.

Proposed decision

Keep configuration APIs off the normal request path. Permit only verified local contracts, sufficiently fresh authorization and valid financial grants during control outages. Reject new grants, relaxed policy and expired artifacts. Document cold-start behavior separately from warm runtime behavior.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Availability is intentionally lower once freshness bounds expire. Operators need an exposure/freshness view and recovery instructions rather than a generic uptime badge.

Required validation

Disconnect control at warm and cold start, revoke access during partition, exhaust grants and advance beyond validity bounds. Verify no new authority appears locally.

Revisit trigger

Revisit allowed stale intervals only through accountable risk acceptance and outage evidence.

Related decisions AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-014 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-016

decisions.title: Keep deployment semantics portable without promising identical operations
decisions.disposition: Reference local deployment plus optional ASGI, not deployment-mode portability certification.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Deployment architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Enterprises differ in network, control-plane and sovereignty requirements. Separate product-specific configuration models would multiply qualification and migration risk.

Alternatives considered

Managed-only platform; fully self-managed-only platform; or common artifacts and APIs across staged deployment targets.

Proposed decision

Design one resource/contract/bundle model for managed, customer-execution and self-managed deployments. Initially qualify one production model. Add dedicated/disconnected variants with explicit dependency, key, update and support contracts. Do not imply that the same API removes different operating responsibilities.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Portability adds packaging and support work. Disconnected installations cannot rely on remote licensing, catalog or secret calls unless explicitly permitted and documented.

Required validation

Install and restore the selected topology from pinned artifacts. Inspect every outbound connection, trust-root dependency and data placement against the declared model.

Revisit trigger

Revisit supported deployment breadth only when the team can own its full lifecycle and assurance burden.

Related decisions AP-ADR-003 AP-ADR-007 AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-034

decisions.title: Scale active work and fairness rather than CPU alone
decisions.disposition: Proposed only. No measured multi-node fairness/capacity or autoscaling guarantee.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Performance and capacity leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Long-lived streams, slow readers and large contexts consume resources that a simple request-rate or CPU metric does not capture. Financial limits cannot guarantee latency fairness.

Alternatives considered

CPU-only autoscaling; unlimited queues; or bounded active-work capacity with tenant fairness and provider-aware scaling.

Proposed decision

Limit body size, active streams, queue wait, output, deadlines and per-tenant concurrency. Use weighted fair scheduling and scale on measured active work, saturation and admission latency. Couple scale plans to provider quotas and available financial grants, not assumed capacity created by replicas.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Traffic can be rejected earlier to preserve useful service for other tenants. Dedicated cells cost more but provide stronger resource isolation where required.

Required validation

Load-test skewed tenants, slow consumers, long generation, connection exhaustion and unavailable providers. Measure per-cell rather than only estate averages.

Revisit trigger

Revisit scheduling weights and limits from observed workload distributions and service objectives.

Related decisions AP-ADR-007 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-020 AP-ADR-021

decisions.title: Quarantine restored authority and rehearse whole-system recovery
decisions.disposition: Local quarantined restore is exercised. Cross-host DR, post-backup liabilities and distributed reallocation remain pending.
decisions.body:
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Disaster recovery ownerDate 8 October 2026

Context

A database backup may omit recent grants, usage or revocations. Restoring it directly into service can repeat money or expose deleted content.

Alternatives considered

Restore and resume immediately; rely on infrastructure backup status; or restore data first and re-establish authority separately.

Proposed decision

Recover control, ledger, state registry and key material through explicit playbooks. Quarantine restored financial accounts and authorization projections until epochs, unresolved exposure and provider activity are reconciled. Replay deletion obligations before exposing restored content. Test migrations together with rollback and backup compatibility.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery may be slower than the database restore alone, especially across regions. RTO targets must include these checks. RPO 0 is conditional on the actual authoritative commit guarantee.

Required validation

Drill zone loss, cross-region snapshot restore, expired keys, partial schema migration, lost outbox and tenant deletion before/after backup.

Revisit trigger

Revisit topology or RTO/RPO promises only after repeatable recovery evidence supports them.

Related decisions AP-ADR-014 AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-023

decisions.title: Verify artifacts, builders and compatible release sets
decisions.disposition: Checksums and pinned test metadata exist. They are not publisher signatures, complete supply-chain assurance or promotion approval.
decisions.body:
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Supply-chain security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A gateway handles credentials and sensitive traffic. Verifying a tag or a signature alone does not establish the provenance or compatibility of all components.

Alternatives considered

Floating latest tags; signed runtime only; or digest-pinned artifacts with builder/provenance policy and full compatibility qualification.

Proposed decision

Pin kernel, compiler, adapter, worker, schema and bundle versions. Verify artifact digests, approved signers/builders and relevant build inputs. Record software inventory and provenance. Use expand/migrate/contract releases and keep signing credentials outside ordinary build/test execution.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Patch management and compatibility testing are ongoing operating costs. Provenance supports verification but is not proof that the code lacks vulnerabilities or that a trusted builder cannot be compromised.

Required validation

Reject unapproved digests/builders/dependencies; test mixed-version windows, schema transitions, trust-root rotation and recovery from a compromised artifact.

Revisit trigger

Revisit verification policy when threat intelligence, build infrastructure or contractual assurance requirements change.

decisions.disposition: Local readiness/observer/delivery evidence exists. Production SLOs and actual application outcomes remain unmeasured.
decisions.body:
Area Observability & UXSuggested owner SRE leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

One availability or latency number can hide provider failures, intentional denials, incomplete streams or missing evidence. Operators need to locate the actual failing contract.

Alternatives considered

Aggregate HTTP status; provider latency alone; or layered service objectives with explicit denominators and ownership.

Proposed decision

Define separate objectives for platform decisions, end-to-end application outcomes, kernel/admission overhead, configuration activation and evidence lag. Record incomplete streams explicitly. Treat proposed numerical targets as unproven until benchmarked under qualified settings. Correlate alerts by affected service and dependency.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More than one metric is necessary, but the UI can organize them around operator decisions. Trace sampling cannot supply a complete billing denominator. Healthy infrastructure is not equivalent to acceptable model quality.

Required validation

Inject policy denial, provider timeout, partial stream, ledger outage and export lag; verify metrics and alerts attribute each to the correct category.

Revisit trigger

Revisit objectives based on measured user impact and operating capability rather than marketing symmetry.

Alternatives considered

decisions.title: Treat accessibility and localization as architectural acceptance
decisions.disposition: Accessibility/localization remain acceptance targets. Responsive automation is not conformance certification.
decisions.body:
Area Product & experienceSuggested owner Design systems and accessibility leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Enterprise tools serve diverse operators and long-lived workflows. Accessibility retrofits are costly when focus, charts, dialogs and error states were designed without semantic structure.

Alternatives considered

Visual polish first with later retrofit; basic browser defaults only; or a shared accessible design system from the initial release.

Proposed decision

Target WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard-complete workflows, screen-reader labels, non-color status, visible focus, reduced motion and responsive reflow. Use explicit currency/timezone and localized presentation without changing ledger units. Treat dialogs, error recovery and exported data as part of the experience contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Automated checks cannot certify accessibility. Expert manual and assistive-technology tests are required. Internationalization can affect layout and task language, not only string translation.

Required validation

Test representative tasks at zoom, narrow widths, keyboard-only and screen reader, including failed submission, stale changes, charts and modal focus return.

Revisit trigger

Revisit the design system as supported locales, assistive technologies and accessibility requirements evolve.

Related decisions AP-ADR-036 AP-ADR-038

Evidence [R09]

decisions.title: Keep optimization and model-assisted administration advisory
decisions.disposition: Advisory posture retained. No autonomous administrative or financial authority is granted by recommendations.
decisions.body:
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner AI product and FinOps leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

An apparent cost-saving opportunity may change quality, privacy or reliability. A model-generated suggestion cannot establish its own authority to act.

Alternatives considered

Automatic cheapest-model selection; autonomous administrator; or evidence-backed suggestions processed through the same approval API.

Proposed decision

Optimize cost per accepted outcome within the existing service envelope. Recommendations disclose fixture/evaluation provenance, uncertainty, assumptions and excluded cost categories. Model assistance may summarize or draft, but all outputs pass typed validation and independent review before authority expansion.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Realized improvements take longer to deploy than unreviewed automation, and useful recommendations depend on good task data. The UI must not present estimates as proven savings.

Required validation

Test cheaper-but-ineligible models, shifted workloads, misleading evaluation samples and prompts attempting to authorize a change. Measure post-release quality and economics.

Revisit trigger

Revisit narrowly delegated automatic actions only after repeated evidence supports a safe, reversible envelope.

Related decisions AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-019 AP-ADR-020 AP-ADR-029

decisions.title: Reject unrestricted in-process extensions
decisions.disposition: Restricted candidate contract follows this direction. No broad production extension/sandbox policy is delivered.
decisions.body:
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Runtime security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Callbacks and plugins can receive prompts, credentials and financial context. Installing arbitrary code in the gateway creates a privileged execution path that can bypass the advertised controls.

Alternatives considered

Open dynamic plugins in the kernel; prohibit all extension; or constrained reviewed adapters and separately isolated external functions.

Proposed decision

Ship initial adapters and policy functions as reviewed build-time modules. External inspectors/tools run through explicit network and authority boundaries. A later extension sandbox must define CPU/memory/time/egress limits, data access and signing; it receives no implicit provider or management credentials.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Customization is slower than dropping a script into a container. That friction is intentional for a critical shared runtime. A sandbox still needs a threat model and cannot be assumed safe merely because it uses WebAssembly.

Required validation

Test extension attempts to open arbitrary destinations, read credentials, persist payloads, exhaust resources and mutate policy or ledger state.

Revisit trigger

Revisit an extension mechanism only for a validated enterprise requirement with an independently tested isolation design.

Related decisions AP-ADR-004 AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-025 AP-ADR-026

decisions.title: Design migration, ownership cost and exit from the beginning
decisions.disposition: Migration, custody and exit are documented locally. Full production economics, remote state portability and operational acceptance remain open.
decisions.body:
Area Product & experienceSuggested owner Enterprise architecture boardDate 8 October 2026

Context

A new platform can improve UX while creating a new dependency and a large operating burden. Building it is not automatically better than composing existing products.

Alternatives considered

Big-bang replacement; vendor-neutrality claims without export; or staged adoption with semantic inventory, comparable benchmarks and an explicit exit contract.

Proposed decision

Migrate bounded service cohorts after mapping identity, policy, state, costs and failure behavior. Use one tested contract across incumbent and new execution paths. Include ledger, worker, support and lifecycle costs in the decision. Export documented contracts, grants, evidence and financial adjustments; acknowledge provider-owned state that cannot be transferred.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Migration takes more analysis than copying configuration. Some workloads should remain native or on an incumbent. The architecture must demonstrate benefits in operator outcomes and correctness as well as performance.

Required validation

Run a real cutover/rollback rehearsal, compare matched workloads and verify a documented export can drive an alternate implementation for the supported contract.

Revisit trigger

Revisit the build decision when measured UX value, staffing or ownership cost no longer supports it.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-023 AP-ADR-031 AP-ADR-036

decisions.disposition: Proposed review amendment. Applies to the inspected fork and integration strategy; it does not accept the corresponding production design.

Context

Reservation enforcement has exclusions and depends on a usable cost estimate.

Alternatives

Treat strict mode as universal; prohibit all unsupported work; or approve contracts with explicit bounds.

Document estimate coverage per endpoint/model and reject or separately authorize requests outside the approved financial envelope. Preserve uncertain liability until justified reconciliation.

Consequences

May reduce available model features; financial promises become testable rather than implied.

Required evidence

Prove concurrency, unknown estimates, disconnects, missing usage, Redis failures and reset windows.

Revisit trigger

A new billing unit, endpoint, price model or reservation implementation is introduced.

decisions.disposition: Proposed review amendment. Applies to the inspected fork and integration strategy; it does not accept the corresponding production design.

Context

Fixed elapsed durations and calendar schedules share strings but differ in meaning.

Alternatives

Keep ambiguity; globally reinterpret old strings; or add explicit versioned semantics.

Decision

Land the narrow corrections first. Design elapsed/calendar modes, timezone and reset preview as a separate versioned contract with reviewed data migration.

Consequences

Additional migration work, but avoids silently altering stored spending periods.

Required evidence

UI/API agreement, DST and month-end tests, historic record preservation and dry-run migration diffs.

A duration schema change is approved or the remaining fallback behavior causes a qualified incident.

Context

File ownership and shadowed database values exist, with special treatment for resource lists.

Alternatives

Generic editable forms; one universal precedence rule; or source-aware editing.

Present effective value, source and revision. Reject conflicting writes with a useful remediation path. Qualify ownership per setting family.

Console, API and automation produce the same effective state and ownership errors.

decisions.title: Keep the managed service boundary explicit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Platform contractSuggested owner AI platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Selecting Bedrock changes which infrastructure the organization operates, but does not settle application tenancy, workflow safety, spending discipline or portability. The reference architecture needs an accountable boundary before individual AWS capabilities or an additional gateway become default dependencies.

Options considered

  • Selected: native Bedrock clients behind an organization-owned application contract, minimizing mandatory infrastructure.
  • Conditional: a gateway when shared admission, multi-provider routing or migration compatibility justifies its operating cost.
  • Rejected: treating the complete application as AWS-operated because its model inference is managed.

Proposed decision

Adopt Bedrock as a managed inference and selected capability provider. Keep application authorization, business workflows, quality acceptance and financial policy under named customer ownership. Add a gateway only against a documented requirement and measure its incremental latency, failure modes and administrative burden. Publish the resulting responsibility boundary with each workload onboarding package.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Teams gain managed capabilities while retaining responsibility for their own data and actions.
  • A gateway becomes a separately justified deployment with its own availability and patching obligations.

Required validation

  • The service inventory assigns every request hop, persisted object and privileged action to a named operating role.
  • A native-client baseline and any gateway alternative are compared using identical functional, security and latency acceptance cases.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when additional providers, mandatory centralized admission or organizational isolation requirements make the current application boundary inadequate or unnecessarily expensive.

Dependencies None; foundational decision.

decisions.title: Admit a bounded endpoint and API contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Platform contractSuggested owner API platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Similar API names do not establish identical endpoint capabilities, authorization, storage or telemetry. Applications need a declared behavior set that survives SDK upgrades and prevents unreviewed features from entering production merely because a client library exposes another parameter.

Options considered

  • Selected: an allowlisted contract for endpoint, API, model, parameters and stateful features.
  • Rejected: automatic exposure of every compatible SDK method without admission review.
  • Conditional: a separate capability lane for endpoint-specific features with distinct retention and operational requirements.

Proposed decision

Publish supported API combinations and reject unsupported parameters at the application boundary. Select the runtime endpoint for the initial contract where it satisfies requirements; introduce mantle through a separate qualification record. Treat Responses storage, background execution, server tools and alternate API shapes as explicit capabilities, each with an owner and a compatibility fixture.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • A bounded contract simplifies incident diagnosis and upgrade testing but slows adoption of newly exposed features.
  • Applications needing different behavior receive an explicit extension rather than an undocumented routing exception.

Required validation

  • Contract fixtures exercise success, validation failures, unsupported fields and streaming termination for each admitted combination.
  • Observed endpoint requests and effective client settings match the published contract; undocumented compatibility assumptions are recorded as unresolved.

Revisit trigger

Revisit whenever a required feature changes endpoint availability, authorization, retention, model support or error semantics, and before switching client compatibility layers.

Dependencies BR-ADR-001

decisions.title: Version the logical model and Region catalog
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Platform contractSuggested owner Model platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Business applications should choose a qualified capability, while operators must identify the exact model, API and routing resource used. An alias without a versioned resolution record can conceal quality changes, different data locations, lifecycle restrictions or a changed cost envelope.

Options considered

  • Selected: versioned logical aliases resolving to explicit qualified deployment tuples.
  • Rejected: unrestricted caller-supplied model identifiers and geography prefixes.
  • Deferred: automatic replacement with the newest model until quality, permission and cost acceptance succeeds.

Proposed decision

Maintain a reviewed catalog binding each alias to model identifier, endpoint, API, approved Regions or profile, lifecycle status, maximum input/output, guardrail version and price schedule reference. Record resolution in request telemetry. Promote catalog revisions independently from application releases where compatibility permits, retaining a usable prior revision and an explicit rollback decision.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Applications gain stable intent while operators retain attributable implementation choices.
  • Catalog ownership creates continuing evaluation and deprecation work; an old alias cannot promise indefinite provider availability.

Required validation

  • Every admitted alias resolves deterministically to a complete catalog entry and rejects unknown versions.
  • A promotion and rollback exercise demonstrates the selected model, policy, telemetry dimensions and pricing revision without changing application source.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when model identifiers, lifecycle dates, API availability or approved deployment Regions change, or when aliases obscure meaningful differences for application owners.

Dependencies BR-ADR-002

decisions.title: Approve geographic and global inference profiles separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Data boundarySuggested owner Data governance ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Routing for capacity can also change where inference executes and where stateful response data resides. A single availability objective cannot authorize every possible destination. Regional eligibility must be defined by organizational policy, rather than inferred from caller location or endpoint spelling.

Options considered

  • Selected: explicit approval of each geographic profile and its permitted destination set.
  • Rejected: silently substituting global routing when a regional path is throttled.
  • Conditional: global profiles only for data classifications that permit every documented destination and storage implication.

Proposed decision

Associate each workload with a reviewed geographic policy and qualified inference profile. Inventory every processing stage: generation, guardrail evaluation, structured-query generation, document parsing, memory and evaluations. Verify effective permissions and data locations for each. Keep prohibited geography failures terminal; queue, degrade to an approved capability or reject instead of widening the boundary during an outage.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Capacity flexibility is available within approved boundaries, but some outages will produce intentional rejection.
  • Profile evolution becomes a governance event requiring catalog and policy review, not only a performance adjustment.

Required validation

  • Requests using unauthorized profiles or destinations fail before sensitive content is transmitted.
  • A simulated primary-capacity shortage demonstrates only approved fallback destinations and records the actual chosen routing resource.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when destination membership, retention behavior, organizational residency requirements or model availability changes, and before enabling any global profile.

decisions.title: Use accounts as a deliberate tenancy boundary
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Identity and isolationSuggested owner Cloud platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Tenants may require different administrative authority, data policies, quotas and financial attribution. Projects and workspaces can organize selected service surfaces, but a resource label alone should not be presumed equivalent to an AWS account boundary or application authorization check.

Options considered

  • Selected: accounts or account groups for materially different trust and regulatory domains.
  • Conditional: shared accounts with separately qualified roles, projects, workspaces and data resources for compatible workloads.
  • Rejected: one broad account role with tenant labels supplied solely by callers.

Proposed decision

Define a tenancy matrix covering account, organizational unit, workload role, project or workspace where supported, model catalog, retention policy and owned storage. Separate production administration from development. Permit shared accounts only where negative authorization tests and quota allocations establish acceptable interference and disclosure boundaries. Assign lifecycle ownership for every tenant-scoped resource and its deletion.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Stronger isolation increases account provisioning and policy-management work.
  • Shared infrastructure remains possible, but its exceptions require evidence for data, financial and operational separation.

Required validation

  • Cross-tenant attempts to invoke, read, change or delete another tenant's resources are denied and attributable.
  • Tenant offboarding removes access and assigned service resources while preserving only explicitly approved audit and billing records.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when tenants acquire independent administrators, incompatible retention rules, substantial quota contention or contractual isolation requirements that exceed the shared-account evidence.

Dependencies BR-ADR-001 · BR-ADR-003

decisions.title: Bind workload permissions to least-privilege IAM roles
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Identity and isolationSuggested owner Cloud security ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

An inference caller, provisioning pipeline, ingestion service and tool executor need different powers. Broad service access makes apparently harmless application changes capable of creating resources, altering controls or reaching models outside the intended contract. Permissions must follow the selected API surface.

Options considered

  • Selected: short-lived workload roles scoped by supported actions, resources and conditions.
  • Conditional: ABAC where the action/resource matrix supports the required tag conditions.
  • Rejected: production use of blanket administrator or full-service policies for convenience.

Proposed decision

Define separate invocation, deployment, ingestion, audit and tool-execution roles. Generate policies from the admitted resource catalog and current service authorization matrix, including endpoint-specific action namespaces. Constrain role assumption and tag mutation. Use explicit denies for prohibited operations where appropriate, and treat any unavoidable wildcard resource scope as a reviewed limitation with compensating application controls.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Smaller permission sets reduce accidental administrative reach but require coordinated updates during feature promotion.
  • ABAC can simplify scale only when trusted tag assignment and actual action support are demonstrated.

Required validation

  • Policy simulations and live negative probes cover wrong account, resource, model, API namespace and attempted tag escalation.
  • Credential expiry and role revocation tests show that applications recover safely without obtaining broader permissions.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when APIs introduce new actions or resource types, supported condition keys change, or policy maintenance begins producing routinely approved wildcard exceptions.

decisions.title: Verify end-user identity before delegating service access
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Identity and isolationSuggested owner Application security ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A backend role identifies the application to AWS, not necessarily the human or tenant requesting an action. Cost tags, request metadata and user-supplied session identifiers are useful context but cannot establish authorization for documents, conversation state or downstream tools.

Options considered

  • Selected: authenticate users in the application and derive tenant context from trusted identity claims.
  • Conditional: constrained role sessions or session tags for verified attribution and isolation.
  • Rejected: accepting client-supplied tenant, email or cost-center fields as authoritative permission evidence.

Proposed decision

Validate identity-provider issuer, audience, expiry and required claims before deriving workload context. Map users to permitted roles and data scopes through server-controlled policy. Keep authorization independent from billing labels. Where identity is delegated to retrieval or tools, bind verified claims to the request and reject inconsistent tenant, session or resource identifiers.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Application identity remains an explicit security responsibility even when every AWS request is signed.
  • Per-user attribution can add session-management overhead; privacy requirements may favor pseudonymous internal identifiers.

Required validation

  • Forged tenant, audience, email and session claims fail without invoking a model, retrieving content or executing tools.
  • Revocation and group-change cases demonstrate the documented refresh bound across application sessions and any delegated credentials.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when identity providers, session lifetimes, delegated tools or retrieval connectors change, or when billing attribution pressures encourage exposing sensitive identity data.

Dependencies BR-ADR-005 · BR-ADR-006

decisions.title: Combine organization, identity and private-network controls
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Identity and isolationSuggested owner Cloud network security ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A private endpoint limits a network path but does not independently authorize a model or protect every adjacent service. Conversely, an IAM role with approved model access should not imply permission to use arbitrary network routes or administer the controls that constrain it.

Options considered

  • Selected: layered SCP, IAM and endpoint policies aligned with the approved deployment catalog.
  • Rejected: relying on private DNS or a VPC endpoint as the sole security boundary.
  • Conditional: public endpoint access for explicitly approved workloads with equivalent identity and egress policy.

Proposed decision

Provision required private endpoints and DNS behavior for each selected service surface, plus separately needed storage, key-management and tool dependencies. Apply organization policies and workload roles consistently with regional routing. Restrict control-plane access to deployment and emergency roles. Maintain an explicit list of permitted public egress destinations for capabilities requiring external services.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Defense is distributed across several policy layers, making testing and incident explanations more involved.
  • A compliant private inference path does not automatically make external retrieval or tool traffic compliant.

Required validation

  • Network probes establish approved endpoint resolution and deny unintended public or cross-account paths.
  • Policy tests cover cross-region profiles, administrative operations and missing dependency endpoints, with failures classified separately from model errors.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when endpoint coverage, DNS topology, regional routing or external tool dependencies change, and whenever a network exception becomes part of normal operation.

Dependencies BR-ADR-004 · BR-ADR-006

decisions.title: Make retention and encryption explicit release properties
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Data boundarySuggested owner Data protection ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Content can exist in request handling, stored responses, abuse review, logs, retrieval stores, batch artifacts and application history. The detailed security chapter defines current service retention behavior; this proposal turns that evidence into enforceable release choices rather than a blanket confidentiality assumption.

Options considered

  • Selected: data-classification-specific retention, encryption and secret policies recorded in the release manifest.
  • Rejected: treating a client store flag or disabled invocation logging as complete zero-retention evidence.
  • Conditional: retention-requiring capabilities only for approved data classes with documented deletion and access procedures.

Proposed decision

Require an effective retention decision for every account, Region and applicable project, then admit only models and API features compatible with it. Set stateful response behavior explicitly. Inventory each persisted copy and its owner, encryption control, deletion schedule and restoration policy. Use workload credentials and secret references; review key disablement and rotation effects before changes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Some models or stateful capabilities may be unavailable under the chosen policy.
  • Encryption and reduced retention improve control but do not replace document authorization, log minimization or trusted tool execution.

Required validation

  • A data-flow review accounts for every stored copy and demonstrates approved retention settings through service reads and representative requests.
  • Key rotation, denied decryption and deletion exercises produce expected failures and documented recovery without unauthorized plaintext export.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when model retention requirements, effective inheritance, stateful APIs, project boundaries or downstream storage change, and after any disclosure or deletion-control failure.

decisions.title: Allocate capacity by endpoint, model and workload class
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Capacity and reliabilitySuggested owner Capacity engineering ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Token demand depends on input size, output limits, cache behavior and model-specific accounting. Runtime and mantle expose different quota systems. An application concurrency limit therefore needs measured workload assumptions and explicit allocations rather than a universal requests-per-second target.

Options considered

  • Selected: endpoint/model/Region capacity envelopes with workload-specific admission queues.
  • Rejected: treating a quota increase or premium tier as unlimited capacity.
  • Conditional: reserved or provisioned capacity after demand, overflow behavior and commercial terms are qualified.

Proposed decision

Inventory actual account quotas and eligible capacity modes for every catalog entry. Bound output tokens, queued work and concurrency; allocate interactive, background and evaluation traffic separately. Forecast both steady and burst demand with documented quota accounting. Require a tested degradation path and approval before changing tier, capacity commitment or cross-region routing to address contention.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Capacity planning becomes more precise but requires current account evidence and realistic token distributions.
  • Reserved spending can improve predictability while introducing utilization and cancellation obligations.

Required validation

  • Load qualification records throttling, queue delay and completion quality at the approved workload mix and output bounds.
  • Capacity alarms distinguish account/model quota exhaustion, local admission limits and provider/service failures, including the chosen overflow behavior.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when workload shape, cache hit rate, model accounting, quota allocation or commercial capacity mode changes materially, before admitting a new high-volume tenant.

Dependencies BR-ADR-003 · BR-ADR-004

decisions.title: Give one layer ownership of retries and deadlines
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Capacity and reliabilitySuggested owner Application reliability ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Retries can originate in an SDK, gateway, workflow and user interface. Their multiplication increases cost and overload while obscuring whether an earlier request completed. Current AWS retry behavior also depends on SDK configuration and the documented 2026 opt-in, so defaults are not a stable contract.

Options considered

  • Selected: one retry owner with a total deadline and attempt budget per operation class.
  • Rejected: independent unrestricted retries in every layer.
  • Conditional: adaptive SDK behavior only with resource isolation and evidence that its delayed admission meets latency objectives.

Proposed decision

Pin the SDK version, retry strategy, maximum attempts and relevant environment settings. Assign a single layer to retry transient failures within the caller's remaining deadline. Keep authorization, validation and policy denials terminal. Record every attempt, preserve stable workflow identity, and resolve ambiguous completion before repeating side-effecting jobs or tool actions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Bounded retry amplification protects capacity and spending but may expose more transient failures to callers.
  • Explicit settings require review during SDK upgrades and when applications add a gateway or orchestration layer.

Required validation

  • Injected throttling, timeouts and service errors produce the declared total attempts and elapsed-time ceiling.
  • A request accepted upstream but disconnected before acknowledgment does not create duplicate business effects; policy denials never trigger alternate routes.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when SDK retry implementation, transport library, endpoint behavior or workflow composition changes, or when incident traces show unexpected attempts or deadline overruns.

decisions.title: Treat stream completion and cancellation as business outcomes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Capacity and reliabilitySuggested owner API reliability ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A stream may deliver useful text before ending unsuccessfully, and a disconnected client does not prove the upstream computation stopped. Applications need explicit semantics for partial output, tool-call fragments, terminal events and unknown usage, rather than equating HTTP acceptance with successful completion.

Options considered

  • Selected: a stream state machine with distinct complete, denied, interrupted and indeterminate outcomes.
  • Rejected: automatically replaying after any emitted output or assuming disconnect cancels all costs.
  • Conditional: resumable application workflows only with qualified identifiers and duplicate-effect handling.

Proposed decision

Document stream event handling for each admitted API. Propagate cancellation where supported, close abandoned transports promptly and retain enough metadata to reconcile uncertain completion. Buffer tool arguments until validated and never execute partial actions. Define whether interrupted prose may be displayed, stored or retried, and include the same decision in client behavior and SLO measurement.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Users receive honest partial-result status while applications avoid hidden duplicate generations or actions.
  • More explicit state handling increases client complexity and leaves some upstream billing outcomes temporarily unresolved.

Required validation

  • Qualification interrupts connections before first output, mid-content, during tool arguments and after terminal delivery, checking cleanup and user-visible status.
  • Stream error fixtures verify that truncated or policy-blocked results cannot be reported as complete or trigger unauthorized tool execution.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when a new streaming API, bidirectional modality, server tool or resume mechanism changes cancellation, ordering or terminal-event guarantees.

decisions.title: Version guardrails and enforce their required attachment
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Policy enforcementSuggested owner AI safety platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

An application-selected guardrail, an IAM condition requiring a specified guardrail and organization/account automatic enforcement are different controls. Their coverage is defined by the chosen API. Governance requires a deliberate enforcement design, not a single configuration field assumed to protect all inference.

Options considered

  • Selected: immutable production guardrail versions plus qualified automatic enforcement where supported.
  • Conditional: IAM conditions requiring approved guardrail identifiers on the documented API scope.
  • Rejected: relying only on voluntary caller attachment or equating a presence condition with automatic insertion.

Proposed decision

Approve guardrail policy versions through an evaluation workflow and bind them to each workload contract. Use organization or account enforcement where the selected path supports the required semantics, then add appropriate identity restrictions. Maintain an explicit matrix for request-provided, automatically enforced and separately applied policies. Prevent workload roles from weakening enforcement or selecting unreviewed versions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Central policy improves consistency but creates a shared dependency and potential false-positive impact.

  • Calls omitting, changing or attempting to bypass required policies demonstrate the documented result on every admitted endpoint/API.
  • Effective organization, account and request policy combinations are inspected and tested, including unauthorized administrative changes and version rollback.

Revisit when enforcement scope, API support, guardrail policy or organizational hierarchy changes, and after any observed bypass or unexpected policy combination.

decisions.title: Qualify guardrail coverage and preserve terminal denials
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Policy enforcementSuggested owner AI safety evaluation ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A moderation result is useful only when it covers the actual content and action boundary. Streaming, retrieved passages, attachments, tool results and generated arguments create different evaluation points. A fallback that escapes a denial would undermine the safety policy even if every individual API call succeeds.

Options considered

  • Selected: a content-and-stage coverage matrix with explicit terminal denial behavior.
  • Rejected: unguarded fallback after a policy refusal, timeout or unsupported content path.
  • Conditional: manual review or safe degradation where automatic evaluation cannot satisfy the workload requirement.

Proposed decision

Test guardrails against the actual modalities, languages and retrieval/tool paths the application exposes. Classify policy denial separately from service failure and prohibit fallback that weakens required controls. For sensitive workloads, reject or queue when mandatory evaluation is unavailable. Specify output buffering requirements before accepting a streaming mode and assign ownership for false positives and missed detections.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Policy availability becomes part of the application SLO, and buffering can increase perceived latency.
  • Evaluation evidence supports a bounded use case; it does not establish universal semantic safety or factual correctness.

Required validation

  • Adversarial fixtures cover unsafe content in each supported field, retrieved context, tool output and partial stream.
  • A denial or mandatory-policy outage produces no subsequent unguarded model attempt, tool action or confidential-content release.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when modalities, prompts, retrieval sources, tools or guardrail versions change, and whenever production review identifies a new bypass or unacceptable false-positive pattern.

decisions.title: Qualify provider prompt caching separately from answer reuse
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Data boundarySuggested owner Inference efficiency ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Prompt caching changes token processing and cost, while reusing a generated answer changes application semantics. Neither should inherit a blanket approval from the other. Cache behavior also depends on the selected model and API, so expected savings require measured reuse patterns.

Options considered

  • Selected: model-specific prompt caching only after privacy and cost qualification.
  • Rejected: treating prompt caching as a tenant-authorized response cache or a substitute for document checks.
  • Deferred: exact or semantic answer caching until separate isolation, invalidation and quality evidence exists.

Proposed decision

Record permitted cached content classes, model-supported controls and expected cache lifetime in the workload contract. Keep secrets and authorization-dependent material outside shared application cache designs unless isolation is demonstrated. Measure input, cache-write and cache-read usage separately. Any customer-owned answer cache must key on tenant, identity scope, model/prompt/policy version and data freshness, with independent invalidation tests.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Caching may reduce repeated processing but introduces privacy review and workload-specific cost behavior.
  • A failed cache experiment must be removable without changing the correctness or authorization of uncached requests.

Required validation

  • Cold, warm, changed-prefix and expired-cache cases show expected usage categories and unchanged application correctness.
  • Cross-tenant and revoked-document cases cannot return another user's cached content, including through any gateway or application answer cache.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when cache controls, model support, prompt composition or data classification changes, and whenever write charges or stale answers outweigh measured benefits.

Dependencies BR-ADR-003 · BR-ADR-007 · BR-ADR-009

decisions.title: Evaluate intelligent routing against an explicit baseline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Policy enforcementSuggested owner Model evaluation ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Dynamic selection can trade model cost against answer quality, but a routing label does not prove equivalence for a workload. The platform needs a clear distinction between selection among approved capabilities and operational fallback caused by an error or capacity shortage.

Options considered

  • Selected: a fixed qualified model baseline before enabling intelligent selection.
  • Conditional: a router with approved candidate set and measured quality/cost acceptance.
  • Rejected: unrestricted cheapest-model substitution or routing that changes geographic and policy requirements implicitly.

Proposed decision

Evaluate any native or customer-owned router on representative tasks with the same evaluation, retention, guardrail and geographic constraints as direct inference. Log the resolved candidate and routing-policy version. Separate capacity fallback from quality routing, bound their combined attempt budget, and ensure terminal authorization or policy decisions remain terminal across all candidate paths.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Measured routing can improve economics while creating another model-selection dependency to monitor.
  • Candidate-set changes require evaluation even when the public application alias stays constant.

Required validation

  • A blinded evaluation compares fixed-model and routed results across important task and tenant cohorts.
  • Fault tests establish permitted fallback order, resolved model attribution, total attempts and the absence of policy or geographic downgrade.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when the routing implementation, candidate set, workload mix or evaluation thresholds change, or when aggregate savings conceal unacceptable errors in a critical cohort.

decisions.title: Implement strict monetary admission outside billing alerts
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Financial controlSuggested owner FinOps engineering ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A token quota protects service capacity; it is not a tenant's monetary authorization. AWS Budgets uses delayed cost information. A workload requiring a hard spending envelope therefore needs a customer admission mechanism that accounts for in-flight work, unknown prices and bypass paths.

Options considered

  • Selected: atomic reservations against a bounded customer ledger before costly work starts.
  • Rejected: treating AWS Budgets alerts or service token quotas as a real-time dollar ceiling.
  • Conditional: softer post-call budgets for explicitly accepted overspend exposure in lower-risk workloads.

Proposed decision

Require a conservative cost bound before admission, including maximum output, permitted retries and priced auxiliary operations. Reject unknown, missing or nonpositive estimates on strict-budget paths. Fail closed if admission authority is unavailable. Reserve atomically, reconcile completed work and retain uncertain reservations until resolved. Allocate spending authority across Regions and prevent direct credentials from bypassing admission. Describe the ceiling as conditional on complete coverage and valid bounds.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Strict admission adds a critical customer-operated dependency and may reject work during ledger outages.
  • Unbounded tools or unmodeled charges remain excluded until their financial exposure can be constrained.

Required validation

  • Concurrent requests at the remaining-budget boundary cannot collectively reserve more authority than allocated.
  • Ledger outage, client disconnect, duplicate completion and unknown-price tests produce conservative admission and exactly-once accounting transitions.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when pricing, retries, new tools, regional topology or direct-access paths invalidate the cost bound, or when accepted overspend tolerance changes.

decisions.title: Separate request estimates from reconciled AWS charges
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Financial controlSuggested owner FinOps ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Operational decisions need prompt-level usage quickly, while financial reporting needs the AWS bill and contractual rates. These are related records with different granularity. The cost documentation's explicit FAQ resolves conflicting snippets in favor of aggregate billing reconciliation rather than a request-identifier join.

Options considered

  • Selected: an append-only request ledger plus aggregate AWS billing reconciliation.
  • Rejected: presenting token-rate calculations as invoice-exact per-request charges.
  • Selected: AWS Budgets alerts and reviewed actions as supplementary financial monitoring and escalation.

Proposed decision

Capture tenant, resolved model, endpoint, tier, token categories, attempts and rate-card revision without content. Mark amounts as estimated, adjusted or reconciled. Export AWS billing data with approved attribution dimensions, reconcile at supported model/usage/time granularity and allocate discrepancies transparently. Activate and test applicable cost tags before launch. Route budget alerts to a named owner with a documented response.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Teams gain timely operational allocation and authoritative aggregate financial control without inventing precision.
  • Discounts, commitments and shared costs require an allocation policy rather than silent proportional assumptions.

Required validation

  • A billing fixture reconciles token categories, tier, routing and applicable discounts within a reviewed tolerance.
  • Duplicate events, late usage and corrected billing periods update the ledger without losing original evidence or charging the same request twice.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when billing schema, attribution mechanisms, commercial discounts or service pricing change, and when reconciliation residuals exceed the agreed explanation threshold.

decisions.title: Own durable orchestration around native async and batch jobs
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Workflow stateSuggested owner Workflow platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Native asynchronous and batch APIs expose job resources and idempotency tokens, but the application still owns intent, authorization, output consumption and downstream side effects. A process crash must not lose the business workflow or cause blind resubmission of work already accepted by AWS.

Options considered

  • Selected: a durable customer workflow record referencing native job identifiers and output artifacts.
  • Rejected: treating an in-memory polling loop as the only record of submitted work.
  • Conditional: external workflow engines when retries, approvals or multi-step recovery justify their operational cost.

Proposed decision

Persist a stable business operation identifier and idempotency token before submission. Record the returned job resource, reconcile ambiguous submissions and resume polling after restarts. Validate outputs before committing downstream effects; use deduplication for consumers. Distinguish pending, running, failed, partially completed, stopped and completed states according to each API, and define artifact retention and cleanup ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Native job execution reduces synchronous-client dependence while durable orchestration remains a customer responsibility.
  • Exactly-once business effects require application design even when submission supports idempotency.

Required validation

  • Crash exercises before submission, after service acceptance and during output consumption recover without losing intent or duplicating effects.
  • Repeated submissions with the same token, partial outputs and denied storage access produce documented job and ledger outcomes.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when job APIs, idempotency scope, output formats, retention or workflow complexity change, and before adding a new modality or downstream side effect.

decisions.title: Admit media and large jobs through separate resource limits
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Capacity and reliabilitySuggested owner Workload admission ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Images, documents, audio, video and batch files have different storage, parsing, duration and cost behavior from a short text exchange. A single generic request-size limit cannot control their practical resource exposure or establish that their contents are safe to process.

Options considered

  • Selected: modality-specific size, duration, item-count and concurrency limits.
  • Rejected: sharing one unbounded admission queue across interactive text and large jobs.
  • Conditional: asynchronous preprocessing with isolated workers and explicit storage permissions.

Proposed decision

Classify each workload before inference and validate allowed content types, dimensions, duration, object ownership and references. Separate interactive and bulk queues, spending allocations and timeouts. Use staged artifacts with approved encryption and retention; reject remote references or archive expansion that exceeds policy. Qualify output delivery and partial-failure handling before admitting a new modality.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Resource isolation protects interactive users but increases queue and artifact-management complexity.
  • Large jobs may be deferred or rejected even while text capacity remains available.

Required validation

  • Boundary cases test maximum accepted sizes, malformed files, unauthorized objects, decompression expansion and unexpectedly long outputs.
  • Bulk-load qualification demonstrates bounded storage growth and no starvation of the interactive workload class.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when models accept new modalities, upstream object formats change, or observed memory, duration and cost distributions exceed the admitted envelope.

Dependencies BR-ADR-002 · BR-ADR-009 · BR-ADR-010 · BR-ADR-019

decisions.title: Default to bounded metadata telemetry and qualified content capture
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and auditSuggested owner Observability ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Runtime invocation logging can capture content, while mantle has a different observability surface. Operators need request outcomes without routinely expanding the sensitive-data footprint. A single dashboard or logging toggle cannot be assumed to cover every admitted endpoint, stream and stateful operation.

Options considered

  • Selected: content-free application telemetry with stable bounded dimensions and correlation identifiers.
  • Conditional: approved invocation-content capture with limited scope, access and retention.
  • Rejected: indiscriminate prompt, response, document or credential logging for troubleshooting convenience.

Proposed decision

Define a telemetry contract for logical and resolved model, endpoint, tenant pseudonym, attempts, timing, usage, policy outcome and completion state. Instrument missing client-observed signals explicitly. Review every content-capture destination and modality before enabling it. Monitor delivery failures and telemetry loss separately from inference availability, and prevent sensitive values from entering tags, traces or exception messages.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Useful operations remain possible with less retained content, but some incidents require controlled reproduction.
  • Additional client metrics may be needed where service metrics do not expose the application-level behavior.

Required validation

  • Synthetic secrets and personal data do not appear in routine logs, metrics, trace labels or exported errors.
  • Every admitted API produces correlated start, terminal and accounting evidence, including interrupted streams and failed log delivery.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when endpoint coverage, observability products, tracing libraries or incident needs change, and after any unplanned content capture or cardinality incident.

decisions.title: Audit each service namespace and resource event class
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and auditSuggested owner Security operations ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

CloudTrail event selection differs between runtime and mantle, and some capability calls require explicit data-event capture. Audit completeness therefore depends on the admitted API inventory. An apparently healthy organization trail can still omit the actions most relevant to a workload investigation.

Options considered

  • Selected: centrally governed trails and data-event selectors matched to the service inventory.
  • Rejected: assuming default event history contains every inference and capability event.
  • Conditional: tighter scoped selectors where cost is material, provided required incident questions remain answerable.

Proposed decision

Specify retained management and data events for inference, guardrails, retrieval, orchestration and administration. Include both service namespaces when used, protect audit destinations from workload roles and define retention independently from prompt logs. Correlate AWS request identifiers with customer workflow records. Keep audit metadata free of secrets and document limitations in attributing combined policy evaluations.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • A defensible audit trail adds data-event and storage cost.
  • Selected events establish actions and identities but do not replace invocation payload records or prove semantic correctness.

Required validation

  • Representative calls and denied changes appear in the expected trail with correct account, Region, namespace and resource class.
  • Disabling capture, changing selectors or altering retention triggers an independently delivered alert and leaves an attributable administrative record.

Revisit trigger

decisions.title: Manage declarative configuration and verify unsupported drift
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Change and recoverySuggested owner Infrastructure platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Bedrock resources can participate in infrastructure-as-code workflows, but automated drift detection does not cover every property or resource. Production policy must therefore distinguish declared desired state, service defaults, supported drift checks and additional evidence needed for security-sensitive settings.

Options considered

  • Selected: reviewed infrastructure definitions and effective-state snapshots with one owner per resource.
  • Rejected: console changes as an undocumented normal deployment path.
  • Conditional: controlled API reconciliation for features lacking adequate declarative support, with equivalent review and rollback.

Proposed decision

Keep account policies, endpoints, roles, catalog bindings, guardrails and supported service resources in version control. Set important defaults explicitly. Record unsupported resource properties and validate them through read APIs or purpose-built checks. Restrict production mutation to deployment roles, with time-bounded emergency access whose changes are reconciled into desired state before normal operation resumes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Reproducibility improves while unsupported features require extra reconciliation work.
  • A green drift status is treated as evidence only for checked properties, not comprehensive proof of compliance.

Required validation

  • A clean environment can be provisioned from approved definitions and compared with the effective-state manifest.
  • An injected console edit and an unsupported sensitive-property change are detected by their respective controls and assigned to an accountable owner.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when resource-provider support, default behavior or drift coverage changes, or when emergency changes repeatedly escape timely reconciliation.

decisions.title: Release models, policies and application adapters together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Change and recoverySuggested owner Release engineering ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

A managed service can evolve independently of customer code, while a single customer release may change prompts, model aliases, SDK behavior, guardrails and retrieval configuration. Rollback is meaningful only when the previous combination remains available and authorized under current service constraints.

Options considered

  • Selected: a release manifest and staged promotion of a complete qualified configuration.
  • Rejected: independent untracked updates to model aliases, policy versions and client adapters.
  • Conditional: expedited security changes with reduced rollout scope and documented residual validation.

Proposed decision

Version the application artifact, SDK configuration, model catalog, prompts, guardrails, retrieval settings and policy references as one reviewable release unit. Run contract and quality gates before progressive exposure. Define stop conditions and verify a viable previous path. Treat model retirement, schema changes and state migration as explicit rollback constraints requiring alternative recovery plans.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Changes become attributable and reversible where dependencies permit, at the cost of release coordination.
  • Rollback cannot restore a provider model or service capability that is no longer available.

Required validation

  • A staged release demonstrates controlled traffic exposure and automatic or operator-directed stop on defined regressions.
  • Rollback restores the prior approved behavior and state compatibility; unavailable prior dependencies produce a rehearsed forward-recovery procedure.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when release frequency, managed capability changes or irreversible state transitions make the current manifest and promotion process inadequate.

Dependencies BR-ADR-003 · BR-ADR-011 · BR-ADR-013 · BR-ADR-023
