decisions.title: Qualify streaming and preventive guardrails together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Request executionSuggested owner AI safety and reliability leadsDate 6 October 2026

Context

Streaming delivery can release content before a complete response is available for inspection. The configured guardrail capability changes buffering, latency and memory behavior. Policy enforcement therefore needs one contract spanning input, output, cancellation, provider retries and client-visible completion.

Options considered

  • Selected: mandatory unsampled input controls and explicitly qualified preventive output handling.
  • Rejected: presenting detect-only, sampled or logs-only evaluation as a complete prevention boundary.
  • Deferred: modalities or streaming paths whose required inspection coverage cannot be demonstrated.

Proposed decision

Match mandatory rules at every approved entry and cache path. Apply input controls before provider or tool dispatch and withhold output when prevention requires complete evaluation. Set policy timeouts, failure behavior, buffer limits and stream deadlines explicitly. Test cancellation and completion accounting; disable unsupported surfaces rather than silently weakening a required control.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Preventive streaming can delay first output and consume memory proportional to buffered responses.
  • External evaluators add latency, cost and data-processing obligations; output blocking cannot reverse an already completed tool action.

Required validation

  • Forbidden canaries never reach protected destinations or clients under guardrail timeout, retry, cache-hit and partial-stream cases.
  • Maximum response sizes and slow clients stay within the memory envelope; cancellation produces an identifiable terminal outcome.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when evaluator capability, supported modality, stream implementation or user-latency requirements change the tradeoff between immediate delivery and preventive policy enforcement.

decisions.title: Treat native budgets as thresholds and bound paid admission separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area State and financial controlSuggested owner FinOps engineering leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

The inspected budget path checks recorded usage and a remote baseline, while cost settles after provider work. This does not establish an atomic reservation for in-flight requests. A contractual ceiling therefore needs a stronger admission contract than a configured budget number alone.

Options considered

  • Selected: native thresholds for secondary governance plus explicit admission envelopes for hard ceilings.
  • Rejected: assuming PostgreSQL or eventual cluster synchronization creates an atomic global reservation.
  • Selected: concurrency and regional allocations that remain conservative when pricing or coordination is uncertain.

Proposed decision

Classify each budget as approximate or strict. For strict budgets, place an authoritative reservation service before paid dispatch, require conservative priceable envelopes, cap concurrency and reject unverifiable work. Reconcile actual usage afterward and allocate regional capacity explicitly. Keep Bifrost limits as additional controls and measure their overshoot under contention.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Strict admission adds a dependency and may reject useful work during uncertainty.
  • Approximate budgets remain simpler but require accepted overshoot, alerts and ownership rather than a promise of zero excess spend.

Required validation

  • Concurrent near-limit calls, missing prices, long streams and retries remain within the approved exposure envelope.
  • Partition, restart and expired-window tests cannot create fresh allowance or silently bypass the external admission authority.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when Bifrost provides a documented reservation contract, workload economics change, or measured overshoot and coordination outages exceed the agreed financial tolerance.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-003 · BIF-ADR-009 · BIF-ADR-010

decisions.title: Maintain a reconciled financial ledger outside transient counters
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area State and financial controlSuggested owner FinOps data ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Gateway accounting protects routine attribution, but asynchronous settlement and process-local deduplication do not establish durable exactly-once financial history. Failed attempts, missing usage, price changes and replay must remain explainable after a gateway or database recovery.

Options considered

  • Selected: durable append-only usage events with reconciliation and explicit uncertainty states.
  • Rejected: treating dashboard totals or mutable counters as the sole financial authority.
  • Rejected: silently pricing unknown usage as zero or collapsing all provider attempts into one successful call.

Proposed decision

Persist logical-call and provider-attempt identifiers, workload ownership, usage categories, price versions and settlement status in a reconciled ledger. Retain provider-confirmed values separately from estimates. Make ingestion idempotent across recovery, queue exceptions for missing evidence, and compare totals with provider billing before using them for external chargeback.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • A durable ledger supports audits and correction but introduces storage, reconciliation and data stewardship work.
  • Financial truth can lag serving; the admission service must account for that uncertainty without resetting prior spend.

Required validation

  • Crash and replay exercises produce one explainable settlement per billable attempt with no lost logical-call linkage.
  • Provider reconciliation reports differences, missing prices and late usage as visible exceptions with accountable resolution.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when billing categories, asynchronous provider workflows, pricing sources or chargeback obligations change, or reconciliation differences exceed the accepted error budget.

decisions.title: Disable response reuse until identity and quality isolation pass
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area State and financial controlSuggested owner Application data ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Exact replay and semantic reuse change response freshness and may expose previously generated content. Virtual-key partitioning helps separate credentials but does not identify individual users sharing one key. A cache must preserve the application's authorization and policy version, not merely improve hit rate.

Options considered

  • Selected: caching disabled during baseline qualification; narrowly approved exact reuse may follow.
  • Deferred: semantic reuse until a separate quality and confidentiality evaluation demonstrates acceptable errors.
  • Rejected: caller-defined shared partitions or cross-model reuse without a server-controlled authorization boundary.

Proposed decision

Enable exact reuse only for approved workloads with trusted tenant, user, model and policy partitions and bounded retention. Keep provider and model separation unless explicitly justified. Qualify cache invalidation after revocation and policy changes. Evaluate semantic thresholds, embedding costs and false reuse independently before enabling semantic search.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Safe reuse can reduce repeated provider work, while finer partitions lower achievable hit rates.
  • Cache stores and embedding calls become data-processing dependencies; a hit must not bypass required policy or attribution.

Required validation

  • Identical requests from adversarial identities, reused keys and crafted partitions never return unauthorized cached content.
  • A versioned quality corpus measures semantic false hits, stale answers and policy changes separately from cache-hit latency.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when application sharing semantics, authorization, embedding model, cache implementation or freshness requirements change, and after any unexpected replay or isolation failure.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-002 · BIF-ADR-005 · BIF-ADR-006 · BIF-ADR-009 · BIF-ADR-010

decisions.title: Separate durable configuration, logs and cache storage
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Deployment and stateSuggested owner Database platform ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Configuration recovery, high-volume request logging and reusable response storage have different consistency and retention needs. A common database technology does not make their operational roles equivalent. The first deployment should keep dependencies understandable while protecting configuration from noisy analytical workloads.

Options considered

  • Selected: managed PostgreSQL configuration and initially separate logical metadata-log storage.
  • Deferred: ClickHouse logs or object payload offload until measured retention and query demands justify them.
  • Rejected: shared SQLite across gateway replicas or a response cache used as durable governance authority.

Proposed decision

Use PostgreSQL for shared-service durable configuration, with explicit authentication, TLS, pool limits and backups. Isolate log capacity and retention from configuration transactions. Treat vector caching and object payloads as optional dependencies with their own access policies. Verify the exact Enterprise build supports every selected backend before rollout.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • A familiar initial datastore reduces operational breadth but may need later log-path specialization.
  • External stores add recovery and network obligations; storage availability alone does not synchronize live OSS governance.

Required validation

  • Load and failure exercises show log ingestion cannot starve configuration queries or exceed the database connection ceiling.
  • A backend compatibility matrix and restored dataset validate encoding, schema, encryption and representative governance entities.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when measured database pressure, retention volume, tenancy requirements or supported backend changes justify a different split or a dedicated analytical store.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-006 · BIF-ADR-007 · BIF-ADR-012

decisions.title: Qualify Enterprise synchronization as eventually consistent coordination
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Deployment and stateSuggested owner Gateway SRE leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Enterprise mesh separates membership from application-state propagation. Healthy membership can coexist with delayed policy or counter updates, and broker deployment introduces a shared relay. The reference service needs an explicit stale-state policy rather than equating node count with control correctness.

Options considered

  • Selected: a private regional Enterprise mesh when synchronized mutable governance is required.
  • Deferred: broker mode until relay loss, congestion and reconnection behavior meet the service requirement.
  • Rejected: treating discovery consensus or a PostgreSQL backend as proof of atomic gateway budget admission.

Proposed decision

Operate a regional mesh with authorized peers, observed policy versions and measured convergence. Monitor membership and application traffic independently. Remove or restrict stale nodes according to the agreed authorization and financial envelope. Approve broker or cross-region variants only after their distinct failure modes and recovery paths are demonstrated.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Coordination can preserve availability during routine node changes, while partitions may widen stale-state exposure.
  • A broker simplifies connectivity but creates a shared synchronization dependency that must have its own incident procedure.

Required validation

  • Independent gossip, gRPC, discovery and database failures produce documented membership, authorization and accounting outcomes.
  • A revoked key and changed policy converge across every serving node within the approved bound after partition and rejoin.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when topology, region count, synchronization implementation or consistency requirements change, or observed lag invalidates the accepted exposure envelope.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-011 · BIF-ADR-014

decisions.title: Deploy a small regional service with explicit runtime limits
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Deployment and stateSuggested owner Container platform leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

The deployment platform must support the chosen storage and communication model while draining long-lived requests safely. More replicas can increase database, provider and synchronization pressure. Resource settings should follow a verified workload envelope rather than copied example manifests.

Options considered

  • Selected: the existing managed container platform with private administration and failure-domain spread.
  • Rejected: simultaneous introduction of unfamiliar orchestration, databases and execution modes without a necessary service benefit.
  • Deferred: serverless broker deployment until its lifecycle and connection restrictions are qualified.

Proposed decision

Start the Enterprise pilot with three failure-domain-separated replicas and sufficient capacity to lose one. Pin the chart and image, restrict filesystem writes and privileges, and size connection pools against shared limits. Configure readiness, liveness and termination deliberately, and cap autoscaling by provider and datastore capacity as well as CPU.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The initial topology supports controlled maintenance but creates minimum running cost and platform ownership.
  • Additional replicas must carry usable headroom; autoscaling cannot manufacture provider quota or synchronized policy authority.

Required validation

  • Rendered manifests enforce approved secrets, network routes, process privileges, pool limits and topology constraints.
  • A rolling replacement under long streams drains correctly and leaves the surviving replicas within their qualified resource envelope.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when workload concurrency, provider limits, platform restrictions or availability requirements exceed the current regional capacity and operational model.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-008 · BIF-ADR-014 · BIF-ADR-015

decisions.title: Qualify performance through completed governed workloads
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Deployment and assuranceSuggested owner Performance engineering leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Raw gateway throughput omits costs introduced by authentication, logging, policy evaluation, provider behavior and long connections. Capacity and service objectives should reflect the actual workload mix and complete outcomes. No benchmark in this report establishes Bifrost's performance in the proposed deployment.

Options considered

  • Selected: reproducible deterministic and capped real-provider tests with the intended controls enabled.
  • Rejected: ranking candidates from incomparable vendor benchmarks or mixed cache-hit and cache-miss results.
  • Selected: separate objectives for interactive streams, embeddings, large media and asynchronous workflows.

Proposed decision

Set application-approved availability, latency, attribution and recovery objectives before the pilot. Measure direct-upstream and gateway paths using the same corpus, topology and policies. Track tail latency, completed streams, active work, queue age, heap, pools and synchronization. Publish limits and regressions with the release rather than relying on aggregate request rate.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Comparable evidence can expose resource and compatibility tradeoffs that throughput headlines hide.
  • A realistic corpus and observability instrumentation require sustained maintenance as application behavior changes.

Required validation

  • The pilot publishes complete configuration, workload distributions and p50/p95/p99 outcomes, with all intentional exclusions identified.
  • Fault and overload tests preserve the accepted policy and completion contract within the documented operating envelope.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when usage mix, dependencies, policy set or implementation changes materially affect cost, latency, concurrency or the definition of a successful operation.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-002 · BIF-ADR-010 · BIF-ADR-015 · BIF-ADR-016

decisions.title: Apply privacy and bounded delivery at every telemetry destination
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and assuranceSuggested owner Observability data ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Payload controls are applied independently at the log store, connectors and optional object retention. Suppressing a root span or hiding dashboard content does not establish that all downstream data is absent. Telemetry therefore needs an explicit inventory and per-destination privacy contract.

Options considered

  • Selected: metadata-only capture everywhere, with bounded retention and exceptional diagnostic access.
  • Rejected: assuming one client setting suppresses all connector or object-storage content.
  • Deferred: caller-controlled logging overrides until application policy can authorize and audit them safely.

Proposed decision

Disable content capture in the client and each connector, disable hidden payload retention and unapproved overrides, and allow only bounded metadata dimensions. Specify queue capacity, backpressure or drop behavior and alert on loss. Permit time-limited diagnostic capture only with a data owner, restricted access and verified deletion.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Reduced content exposure improves data minimization but limits retrospective debugging.
  • Asynchronous telemetry can lose data during failure; required financial and administrative records need stronger independent durability contracts.

Required validation

  • Canary prompts, tool arguments, reasoning, raw bodies and credentials are absent from every enabled sink under success and failure.
  • Sink outages and hostile label input produce bounded memory and cardinality, with observable backlog or loss.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adding a connector, changing diagnostic needs, retaining object payloads or introducing a metadata field that alters privacy or cardinality risk.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-005 · BIF-ADR-007 · BIF-ADR-016

decisions.title: Retain administrative audit independently from request diagnostics
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and assuranceSuggested owner Security operations ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Administrative changes can alter the gateway's trust boundary and must remain attributable after application logs expire. Signed events and object archives help preserve evidence, but retention and archival are independent mechanisms. The service needs proof of completeness and recoverability, not only signature verification.

Options considered

  • Selected: protected audit events with separate retention, export permissions and signing-key custody.
  • Rejected: relying exclusively on mutable request logs or dashboard visibility for administrative evidence.
  • Selected: independently retained archives with monitored lag and a deletion margin.

Proposed decision

Record sensitive administrative actions with actor, target, outcome and change reference. Configure signing and retain historical verification keys separately. Archive to protected object storage where required, monitor unarchived windows, and keep database retention longer than the verified archival delay. Restrict audit export and retention changes to designated roles.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Independent audit aids incident reconstruction while creating additional sensitive identity metadata and key-management work.
  • HMAC validates integrity of retained records; missing or unrecorded events still require reconciliation and coverage checks.

Required validation

  • Sensitive changes generate complete attributable events and unauthorized users cannot alter retention or export protected records.
  • Archive interruption, replay and retention exercises preserve reconciled event counts and historical signature verification.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when retention obligations, archive architecture, signing scheme or administrative API coverage changes, and after any missing-event incident.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-004 · BIF-ADR-007 · BIF-ADR-014 · BIF-ADR-018

decisions.title: Rehearse migration, restore and rollback as one recovery contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and assuranceSuggested owner Database recovery leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Startup migrations can outlive an image rollback, and encrypted backups depend on retained keys. Asynchronous usage may also leave a restored snapshot behind actual provider spend. Recovery must reconstruct an authorized, financially coherent service rather than merely start a container.

Options considered

  • Selected: consistent backups, protected encryption material and representative restore exercises before upgrades.
  • Rejected: assuming Helm rollback reverses schema or that successful database import proves application recovery.
  • Selected: forward repair or full restore when an older image cannot safely read the migrated schema.

Proposed decision

Retain image, effective configuration, schema history, encryption material and ledger checkpoints as one recovery set. Rehearse migration on restored data, serialize the initial upgrade bootstrap, and validate before expanding replicas. Define RTO and RPO explicitly, reconcile post-snapshot spend, and recheck authorization before restoring traffic.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Recovery preparation increases release effort but reduces surprises during irreversible schema changes.
  • A restore can discard legitimate recent changes; operators need a documented reconciliation and communication procedure.

Required validation

  • An isolated restore validates keys, roles, providers, logs, decryptability and accurate remaining budget against the recovery record.
  • Interrupted migrations and attempted downgrades follow a documented safe path without silently losing records or reopening access.

Revisit trigger

Revisit whenever schemas, encryption, persistence backends or asynchronous accounting change, and when a restore drill misses its recovery objectives.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-006 · BIF-ADR-007 · BIF-ADR-012 · BIF-ADR-014 · BIF-ADR-015 · BIF-ADR-019

decisions.title: Verify artifact provenance and patch against actual exposure
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Observability and assuranceSuggested owner Product security leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Historical advisories describe particular versions and deployment prerequisites, while vendor security statements describe processes rather than the artifact an organization runs. Module versions, dynamic plugins and Enterprise bases can change exposure. Patch decisions need an accurate inventory and controlled evidence.

Options considered

  • Selected: digest-pinned artifacts, provenance review and an owned vulnerability-response process.
  • Rejected: declaring an image safe because a repository tag is newer or a vendor advertises scanning.
  • Selected: regression qualification tailored to management, URL-fetch and executable-extension attack surfaces.

Proposed decision

Inventory transport, core, framework, plugins, image and Enterprise base versions. Validate available provenance and scan the actual artifacts, track advisories and resolve ambiguous version ranges with the maintainer. Prioritize patches by reachable exposure, rehearse deployment and rollback, and preserve regression evidence for previously affected boundaries.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Version precision improves response quality while adding review work and emergency patch obligations.
  • Some provenance or private-edition evidence may require vendor support; an unresolved gap remains an explicit acceptance exception.

Required validation

  • The inventory maps each official advisory to the deployed component and records why it is applicable, fixed or uncertain.
  • A patched candidate passes the relevant authorization and egress regressions before production promotion.

Revisit trigger

Revisit upon a new advisory, compromised build dependency, changed Enterprise base, unsupported release line or failure to obtain required artifact evidence.

Area Extensions and lifecycleSuggested owner Extension review ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Native Go plugins share the gateway process and may influence identity, routing and per-attempt behavior. Their build compatibility and hook position affect correctness as well as security. An extension is therefore a release component with authority, not a harmless configuration addition.

Options considered

  • Selected: a small allowlist of reviewed native extensions built and pinned with the host.
  • Rejected: arbitrary runtime plugin URLs or unreviewed code loaded through administration.
  • Deferred: deprecated or planned extension mechanisms until a supported implementation satisfies the required contract.

Proposed decision

Approve each extension's hook placement, inputs, secret access, network effects, timeout and idempotency. Keep credential-supplying transport hooks distinct from post-authentication hooks and per-attempt LLM hooks. Build against the qualified host, disable unneeded loading paths, and require application authorization for every extension-induced external side effect.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Custom behavior remains possible but expands the trusted codebase and couples release compatibility.
  • Panic recovery or type checking cannot contain arbitrary native code; strong isolation requires an external execution boundary.

Required validation

  • Hook-order tests show identity and mandatory policy cannot be weakened by extension placement or short-circuit responses.
  • Retry, reload, timeout and shutdown exercises demonstrate bounded execution and no duplicate unauthorized side effects.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when a plugin changes, host ABI or lifecycle changes, or a supported isolated extension interface becomes available with evidence of equivalent functionality.

decisions.title: Isolate tool execution and govern MCP as delegated authority
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Extensions and lifecycleSuggested owner Agent platform security leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

MCP transports add tool discovery, delegated credentials and potentially local process execution to the gateway's trust boundary. A permitted model call does not authorize every tool action. Output inspection also cannot reverse a completed external mutation.

Options considered

  • Selected: default-deny tool registration and scoped remote executors with independent authorization.
  • Rejected: unrestricted stdio processes or broad tool credentials inside the shared inference gateway.
  • Deferred: autonomous multi-step execution until identity, approval and side-effect limits are demonstrated.

Proposed decision

Inventory approved servers and tools, require authenticated administration for changes, and isolate tool execution from gateway secrets. Bind each call to a principal and permitted action, validate arguments before execution, and enforce step, time and result-size limits. Configure explicit OAuth issuer and callback identities and preserve application-owned transaction approvals.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Agent integration becomes reviewable while adding tool-specific policy, token and execution infrastructure.
  • Read-only tools still introduce data exposure; state-changing tools require idempotency and authorization at their actual target.

Required validation

  • Unapproved tools, unauthorized principals and malicious arguments cannot trigger external actions or access gateway secrets.
  • OAuth confusion, reconnect, timeout, repeated calls and partial agent failure preserve scoped identity and produce complete execution records.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when a tool gains new capabilities, authentication changes, local execution becomes necessary or agent autonomy expands beyond the approved action envelope.

Dependencies BIF-ADR-003 · BIF-ADR-005 · BIF-ADR-008 · BIF-ADR-010 · BIF-ADR-022

decisions.title: Keep service accountability, commercial terms and exit practical
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
Area Extensions and lifecycleSuggested owner Architecture review boardDate 6 October 2026

Context

An enterprise gateway is a long-lived organizational dependency. Open-source rights, Enterprise entitlements, operational support and application quality have different owners. A useful decision record must preserve those responsibilities and provide a feasible exit without assuming that compatible APIs eliminate switching costs.

Options considered

  • Selected: named service ownership, explicit commercial requirements and a maintained exit inventory.
  • Rejected: transferring application evaluation or business authorization to the gateway vendor by implication.
  • Selected: conditional adoption with measurable acceptance gates, reviewed exceptions and scheduled decision renewal.

Proposed decision

Contract for the required edition, support, license behavior and recovery assistance. Keep application quality evaluations, prompts and business authorization with application owners. Export portable aliases, policy definitions and reconciled usage, inventory provider-bound resources, and rehearse an alternative path. Accept these ADRs only after evidence, owners and remaining exceptions are recorded.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The organization preserves negotiating and migration options while funding portability and evaluation work.
  • Stateful provider resources and custom extensions can remain costly to move despite a compatible inference API.

Required validation

  • An exit exercise routes the approved contract corpus through an alternative and accounts for retained resources and outstanding usage.
  • The adoption review records signed ownership, entitlement evidence, acceptance results and expiry dates for every exception.

Revisit trigger

Revisit at contract renewal, major architectural change, material service failure or when an alternative meets the same contract with demonstrably better organizational outcomes.

decisions.title: Select the AI entity operating boundary explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerPlatform architecture leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The organization needs common governance across applications, but managed administration and fully self-hosted operation are different trust choices. Dedicated AI Gateway entities use a Konnect control plane and customer data planes; on-premises AI capabilities use the plugin configuration model. Existing Kong operational experience does not establish shared resources or complete feature parity.

Options considered

  • Adopt dedicated Konnect AI entities with customer-operated nodes.
  • Operate an independently qualified Kong Gateway plugin stack.
  • Retain native provider access or an existing self-hosted AI gateway.

Proposed decision

Pilot dedicated entity mode only where managed-plane connectivity, processing terms and support cadence are accepted. Record plugin mode as a separate alternative rather than an interchangeable deployment flag. Approve the complete service composition, including auxiliary services and application responsibilities, before production.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The managed boundary can reduce administration-service operations while retaining customer runtime duties. It introduces a vendor availability, data-processing and lifecycle dependency. A disconnected requirement disqualifies this reference topology rather than being waived through wording.

Required validation

Obtain the product/topology entitlement record; deploy the selected generation in a qualification environment and demonstrate the intended management and traffic boundaries.

Acceptance gates: KG-T01, KG-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

An offline requirement, material licensing change, unsupported mandatory capability or different identity boundary.

DependenciesNone — foundational product-boundary decision.

decisions.title: Qualify the exact runtime and managed-plane release pair
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerRelease engineering leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The AI Gateway product has its own release line. The observed runtime baseline is 2.2.0, while some support and example pages describe older versions. Synchronization and packaging changes can affect configuration delivery even when an application's request schema remains unchanged.

Options considered

  • Track a floating image tag and trust generic hybrid compatibility.
  • Pin a tested runtime, managed-plane compatibility and tooling bundle.
  • Use a separately qualified plugin-generation release policy.

Proposed decision

Pin runtime artifacts and delivery tools; retain the supported managed-plane/runtime compatibility evidence with every release. Treat entity mode and plugin mode as different qualification lanes. Do not infer Kong Gateway LTS guarantees or generic rolling-upgrade compatibility for dedicated AI Gateway.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Release evidence becomes reproducible, but upgrades require recurring engineering work. A managed-plane change may require vendor coordination rather than an independently reversible binary change. An old cached node is not proof that the new fleet can synchronize.

Required validation

Verify configuration synchronization, warm/cold startup, critical endpoint fixtures and rollback behavior for the exact artifact pair. Resolve the changelog/support-table discrepancy before production reliance.

Acceptance gates: KG-T01, KG-T07, KG-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new minor/patch, managed-plane compatibility change, image variant, platform change or security advisory.

DependenciesKG-ADR-001

decisions.title: Publish a bounded endpoint and protocol contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerAPI platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Normalized LLM requests, provider-native endpoints, byte-preserving passthrough, MCP and A2A have different parsing, policy and state behavior. A working chat request cannot qualify the entire advertised surface. Applications need a stable promise that survives changes in gateway implementation.

Options considered

  • Expose every enabled provider endpoint by default.
  • Publish a small capability contract and expand through evidence.
  • Use passthrough universally and move all policy into applications.

Proposed decision

Expose only approved tuples of runtime, entity type, API family, wire format, provider target and policy set. Start with bounded LLM inference. Qualify MCP, A2A, media and asynchronous routes independently. Maintain explicit unsupported-field, error, streaming and retained-resource behavior.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The initial surface is smaller, reducing integration ambiguity. Some upstream innovations will require a separate native or passthrough exception. Those exceptions must declare which gateway controls no longer apply rather than inherit a false common guarantee.

Required validation

Execute the positive/negative protocol suite, including tools, structured output, usage, error bodies and unsupported parameters, against each approved tuple.

Acceptance gates: KG-T04, KG-T05, KG-T16, KG-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new provider/API, protocol revision, model capability or policy relying on request/response parsing.

DependenciesKG-ADR-001, KG-ADR-002

decisions.title: Version aliases and eligible target service promises
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerModel service ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

An AI Model alias can hide several targets. Updating a target can change quality, context, tools, pricing or processing geography without changing the client-visible name. Configured defaults may be overridden by requests and should not be assumed to enforce hard limits.

Options considered

  • Allow arbitrary provider model selection by callers.
  • Use stable organizational aliases with versioned capability promises.
  • Expose only physical provider deployments.

Proposed decision

Define each alias outside the vendor configuration with approved capabilities, output bounds, quality criteria, data envelope and eligible targets. Treat a change to that promise as an application-facing version decision. Enforce hard request ceilings separately from target defaults and reject unapproved route overrides.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications gain a stable integration boundary and migration path. The platform must maintain contract records and evaluate replacements. Transparent price or latency optimization is constrained by the promise rather than allowed to change semantics silently.

Required validation

Test body/header/path resolution, all fallback targets, parameter overrides and quality fixtures; prove that unauthorized aliases or destinations cannot be selected.

Acceptance gates: KG-T03, KG-T04, KG-T06. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Any target-set, model-version, geographic, quality or maximum-cost change.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003

decisions.title: Issue distinct accountable workload credentials
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerIdentity engineering leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Shared consumer credentials obscure ownership and enlarge the impact of compromise. Model access, billing attribution and incident response need a verified workload identity. Generated keys and their one-time retrieval also need a secure provisioning workflow.

Options considered

  • Share one gateway key per department.
  • Issue separate credentials per workload and environment.
  • Require delegated end-user identity for every call.

Proposed decision

Assign a distinct consumer or approved identity mapping to each service/environment, with a named owner and scoped resource grants. Deliver secrets through the organization's secret channel, disable query-key use and prevent logging or unintended forwarding. End-user identity may supplement but not replace accountable workload ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Credential count increases, so automated provisioning and rotation are necessary. Attribution and containment improve. Applications must not reuse administrative tokens or embed provider credentials merely to avoid the lifecycle work.

Required validation

Demonstrate provisioning, rotation, revocation, leak-free telemetry and correct attribution across replicas. Verify that one workload cannot use another's grants or management authority.

Acceptance gates: KG-T02, KG-T03, KG-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new authentication scheme, credential-sharing exception, service ownership change or revocation incident.

DependenciesKG-ADR-001, KG-ADR-003

decisions.title: Validate OIDC trust and strategy composition explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerIdentity security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Signature validity alone does not establish the intended application audience or resource entitlement. Auth Strategy combinations and the shared OIDC strategy constraint influence how many trust domains can safely inhabit one gateway. Key and OIDC alternatives should not be mistaken for cumulative authentication requirements.

Options considered

  • Accept any token verified by an upstream ingress.
  • Use a qualified OIDC strategy and mandatory consumer mapping.
  • Use workload API keys for routes that cannot meet the OIDC contract.

Proposed decision

For OIDC routes, specify issuer, audience, algorithms, expiry, key refresh, consumer mapping and revocation bounds. Keep trust-domain boundaries explicit and separate gateway resources when the strategy constraint requires it. Do not permit an optional or absent mapping to confer broad resource access.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Identity is easier to explain, but multi-issuer estates may need more gateway instances. IdP and signing-key discovery become tested dependencies. A valid token from another service remains unauthorized even when signed by a trusted organization.

Required validation

Test wrong issuer/audience, expired and malformed tokens, absent mappings, method-alternative behavior, key rotation and warm/cold identity-provider outages.

Acceptance gates: KG-T02, KG-T07. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Issuer consolidation, identity federation, claim mapping, gateway strategy support or trust-domain changes.

DependenciesKG-ADR-005

decisions.title: Enforce tenant and resource isolation on every path
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerSecurity architecture leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Identity objects organize callers but do not create hard isolation across caches, tool catalogs, tasks, documents and telemetry. Resource identifiers or metadata can cross trust boundaries independently of model authorization. Some workloads require separate administrative or runtime domains.

Options considered

  • Rely only on consumer/group model ACLs.
  • Apply resource-specific authorization with risk-based physical separation.
  • Deploy a separate complete stack for every application.

Proposed decision

Derive tenant authority from verified identity and enforce it for model selection, cache hits, retrieval, tools, sessions, provider resources and operational views. Use separate gateways or stores where trust, identity constraints or sensitivity require stronger isolation. Never treat caller-supplied tenant tags as authority.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The design avoids universal per-tenant duplication while retaining explicit boundaries. It requires application cooperation for business resources and a comprehensive negative-test corpus. Logical namespaces are not represented as equivalent to independent credentials or infrastructure.

Required validation

decisions.title: Separate administrative authority from inference access
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerPlatform security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Configuration can redirect traffic, weaken policies and expose credentials. Application callers and CI administrators therefore need different authority and network/access paths. A private data plane does not automatically make the remote management plane private or least-privileged.

Options considered

  • Reuse broad platform administrator credentials for automation.
  • Use named operators and narrowly scoped delivery identities.
  • Allow application teams unrestricted production configuration.

Proposed decision

Use separate named administrative identities, scoped CI permissions and reviewed production promotion. Keep application credentials unable to mutate configuration. Protect recovery access with a documented break-glass procedure and export administrative evidence independently of inference logs.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Change review introduces process overhead but provides attribution and limits blast radius. Emergency work remains possible through an auditable path; temporary changes must be reconciled into declared state before closure.

Required validation

Test application attempts to change models, providers, consumers and policies. Verify CI scope, operator attribution, break-glass expiry and audit export through a simulated emergency change.

Acceptance gates: KG-T03, KG-T20, KG-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Administrative API/RBAC changes, new delivery tooling, organizational ownership changes or an access-control incident.

decisions.title: Separate node trust, traffic TLS, secrets and session keys
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerSecrets and PKI ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Control-plane certificates, serving certificates, consumer keys, provider credentials and session encryption protect different relationships. Their compromise and rotation effects differ. A Vault reference is configuration for a secret backend, not a complete secret lifecycle.

Options considered

  • Use a small set of broadly shared credentials.
  • Maintain separate credential classes with scoped custody and rotation.
  • Embed long-lived credentials directly in manifests.

Proposed decision

Inventory each credential class and owner; use least-privilege workload identity or controlled secret references where supported. Keep data-plane private keys on customer nodes, separate session encryption from access credentials, and rotate with bounded overlap. Preserve independent recovery material outside configuration exports.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More lifecycle procedures are required, but compromise impact and recovery become clearer. Revoking node synchronization is not assumed to stop a stale node from serving; containment also removes traffic and upstream authority.

Required validation

Rotate and revoke every class, including cold-node bootstrap and session continuity. Confirm redaction in plans/logs and successful containment of a node retaining old configuration.

Acceptance gates: KG-T10, KG-T16, KG-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New secret backend, certificate mechanism, token exchange, session mode or compromise.

decisions.title: Bind all egress and processing locations to approved contracts
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerNetwork and data-governance ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Model inference is only one outbound flow. Identity, telemetry, vector stores, inspection, tool discovery and execution can carry sensitive information through independent transports. Forward-proxy support is mode-specific and does not establish universal auxiliary egress coverage.

Options considered

  • Approve only the model provider region.
  • Maintain and enforce a complete destination/data-flow inventory.
  • Allow unrestricted egress and rely on application prompts.

Proposed decision

Approve destinations, credentials, data classes and processing geography for every enabled flow. Enforce fixed routing and network controls, validate TLS, restrict forwarded headers and redirects, and reject client-controlled upstream URLs. Qualify each forward-proxy mode and auxiliary transport independently.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Integration requires more explicit network work, especially for identity and inspection services. The data-processing claim becomes defensible across the complete composition. A provider-region label alone is insufficient for approval.

Required validation

Observe all destinations with synthetic markers, block unapproved routes and prove that inference, token acquisition, vector access and telemetry follow the declared paths without credential leakage.

Acceptance gates: KG-T10, KG-T11, KG-T15. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new provider, policy service, agent, proxy mode, region, redirect behavior or telemetry destination.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-007, KG-ADR-009

decisions.title: Start with weighted routing among contract-equivalent targets
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerModel platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Adaptive routing can optimize observed latency or cost but may obscure which service promise is being delivered. Provider capacity and health observations change under load. The target set must remain compatible with the application before any balancing algorithm is considered.

Options considered

  • Route to the lowest observed latency or price immediately.
  • Start with explicit weights among approved equivalent targets.
  • Bind every application permanently to one physical target.

Proposed decision

Use a simple, observable weighted baseline within each alias's approved set. Introduce adaptive policies only after measuring a benefit and proving that eligibility, quota, geography and quality constraints remain intact. Record the selected target and routing-policy version in protected operational evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Initial optimization may be modest, but behavior is easier to explain and recover. The platform must maintain capacity assumptions and test restoration after cooldown or outage. Faster targets are not allowed to absorb traffic without regard to their limits.

Required validation

Measure distribution, quota saturation, failure recovery and target eligibility under representative load. Compare any adaptive alternative against the same baseline and policy set.

Acceptance gates: KG-T04, KG-T06, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Changed traffic, provider capacity, quality envelope or demonstrated optimization benefit.

DependenciesKG-ADR-004, KG-ADR-010

decisions.title: Assign one retry owner and a total deadline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerApplication reliability leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

SDK, gateway, ingress and application retries can multiply attempts and charges. A timeout after dispatch can leave work running. Repeating model generation, a provider-resource operation and a mutating tool action have different safety properties.

Options considered

  • Allow every layer's default retries.
  • Assign one owner per operation with an end-to-end deadline.
  • Disable all recovery at every layer.

Proposed decision

Define one retry owner for each operation family, bound attempts and elapsed time, and classify failures by dispatch and output state. Restrict fallback to the original eligible set. Stateful or side-effecting operations require owner-aware idempotency/reconciliation; do not replay after response content is released.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some failures will be returned instead of hidden by retries, preserving correctness and cost visibility. Applications need explicit recovery for incomplete tasks. The platform gains a measurable bound on attempted work rather than a stack of independent timeout settings.

Required validation

Inject connection, provider, quota and timeout failures at several lifecycle points. Confirm the maximum attempts, total deadline, no cross-boundary fallback and correct uncertain-outcome classification.

Acceptance gates: KG-T05, KG-T06, KG-T17, KG-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new SDK retry default, endpoint family, provider idempotency contract or latency objective.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-004, KG-ADR-011

Evidence informing this proposal[KG21] [KG22] [KG33]

decisions.title: Specify streaming and cancellation as first-class outcomes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerAPI reliability ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Streaming commits status before the application result is complete. Tool arguments and usage can arrive incrementally, and output cannot be withdrawn once delivered. A disconnected client does not prove cancellation of provider computation or billing.

Options considered

  • Treat HTTP 200 as complete success.
  • Define terminal, partial, cancelled and uncertain outcomes.
  • Disable streaming for every workload.

Proposed decision

Publish the permitted stream events, termination rules, timeout phases and cancellation behavior. Prohibit transparent replay after output. Preserve partial/unknown usage for reconciliation and use buffered output where required preventive checks cannot coexist with incremental disclosure.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Client libraries and dashboards must understand incomplete responses. Some sensitive workloads lose interactive streaming benefits. The resulting contract prevents silent truncation and contradictory concatenated answers from being represented as success.

Required validation

Test every selected format through actual ingress with slow clients, malformed chunks, provider errors, tool fragments and disconnects before terminal usage. Confirm bounded buffers and accurate outcome metrics.

Acceptance gates: KG-T05, KG-T11, KG-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A streaming protocol, inspector, provider adapter, ingress timeout or cancellation capability changes.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-012

decisions.title: Make preventive controls protocol-specific and release-aware
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerAI security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A configured guardrail does not prove prevention for every endpoint. Parsed-body policies are unavailable on some passthrough paths; input-only defaults and streamed inspection can differ from the intended output guarantee. External inspection also creates an additional data processor.

Options considered

  • Attach a common policy label and assume universal coverage.
  • Qualify input and output release rules per protocol.
  • Move all inspection to applications and expose no gateway guarantee.

Proposed decision

Classify each control as preventive or detective, specify its endpoint scope, and test the exact output-release and failure rule. Default required inspection to deny on unverifiable results. Keep passthrough exceptions explicit and sensitive streaming disabled unless a bounded preventive design passes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Policies can add latency and reduce availability during inspection outages. Separate services need capacity, TLS, version and privacy ownership. The service promise becomes narrower but testable, avoiding a false guarantee based on configuration presence.

Required validation

Inject detectable markers, service errors and timeouts in input, output and streams. Observe when content is emitted and verify no claimed prevention occurs only after disclosure.

Acceptance gates: KG-T10, KG-T11. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new policy/provider, inspection mode, streaming buffer, protocol or sensitivity class.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-013

decisions.title: Keep response caching disabled until exact eligibility is proven
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerApplication data ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Reusing output can reduce cost but can also leak personalization or return stale business information. The semantic-cache policy's exact lookup option does not establish exact-only matching. Cache authorization and retention differ from inference authorization.

Options considered

  • Enable response caching globally.
  • Keep caching off and approve narrowly scoped exact reuse separately.
  • Rely on semantic similarity for all repeated questions.

Proposed decision

Disable response caching in the initial service. Any exact-reuse implementation must demonstrate actual exact-only behavior, tenant/policy/model partitioning, current authorization and deletion. Exclude side-effecting, personalized and sensitive requests unless a specific exception passes application review.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The baseline gives up potential savings while avoiding an unqualified data store. A separately qualified cache may be needed when Kong's semantic policy cannot express the required exact-only semantics. Cache entries become governed data with an owner.

Required validation

Test nonidentical near-matches, cross-principal access, model/policy changes, stale documents and deletion. Confirm that a cache hit cannot bypass current access or output rules.

Acceptance gates: KG-T12. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A measured cache benefit, new implementation, eligibility class or retention requirement.

decisions.title: Evaluate semantic caching as an application-quality feature
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerProduct evaluation leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Similarity can be useful for repetitive tasks but does not prove answer equivalence. Embedding choice, distance threshold, model changes and tenant context affect false hits. A cache optimization can change business output even when the gateway transport behaves correctly.

Options considered

  • Adopt a global similarity threshold from an example.
  • Approve a narrow use case through measured false-hit and quality criteria.
  • Keep semantic caching disabled permanently.

Proposed decision

Treat semantic caching as a separate product decision with an approved corpus, acceptable error rate, freshness rules and controlled store. Partition authority and policy context, version embeddings and thresholds, and retain a rapid disable/invalidation procedure. Do not infer safety from the exact-cache toggle.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Evaluation and vector operations add work and expense. Benefits must include quality-adjusted task cost, not just hit rate. New embeddings or models may require rebuilding or invalidating the cache rather than retaining superficially compatible entries.

Required validation

Measure false hits and task correctness using unseen examples, adversarial near-matches and cross-tenant negatives. Test embedding failure, store outage, invalidation and recovery.

Acceptance gates: KG-T12, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Changed task distribution, model/embedding version, similarity threshold or unacceptable cached outcome.

DependenciesKG-ADR-004, KG-ADR-007, KG-ADR-015

decisions.title: Use Konnect as entity desired-state authority, not a fictional customer database
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerPlatform architecture leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The earlier LiteLLM reference uses customer PostgreSQL for durable governance. Dedicated Kong entity mode has a different ownership boundary: managed desired state, customer declarations and node-local applied configuration. Transplanting the PostgreSQL assumption would misrepresent the product.

Options considered

  • Add a customer database as an assumed Kong management authority.
  • Use managed AI entities with customer-owned declarative recovery artifacts.
  • Select a separately qualified self-managed plugin topology.

Proposed decision

Treat Konnect as authoritative for accepted entity state, version control as authority for approved intended changes, and node observations as evidence of application. Do not prescribe customer SQL operations on Konnect internals. Independently inventory any customer-owned vector, session, accounting or application databases.

Consequences and tradeoffs

There are multiple clearly labeled views of state rather than one fictitious universal store. Recovery needs managed API reconstruction plus separately held secrets. A local export may omit generated or write-only values and must be tested for completeness.

Required validation

Compare declared, accepted and applied state; reconstruct a qualification gateway from retained artifacts and independent secrets. Identify fields and identities that require remapping.

Acceptance gates: KG-T07, KG-T22, KG-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new self-hosted management offering, persistence model, export capability or deployment-generation choice.

decisions.title: Separate shared counters from cache and session storage
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerStateful platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Rate counters, semantic response bodies, retrieval vectors and MCP sessions have different correctness, eviction and recovery needs. Local counter behavior changes with node count. Redis failure can cause documented local fallback, which does not preserve the same global limit.

Options considered

  • Use one unqualified Redis instance for all features.
  • Separate storage roles and qualify each coordination/failure contract.
  • Use local counters and accept explicitly approximate enforcement.

Proposed decision

For shared limits, configure supported Redis coordination and stable namespaces, with explicit synchronization and failure choices. Verify required model/provider match partitioning. Isolate critical counters from expendable payload caches by suitable infrastructure and policy; session/vector compatibility is qualified separately.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More storage configuration and possibly services are required. High availability does not imply preserved counters after every partition or restore. Workloads accepting local approximation must have a bounded exposure decision; strict admission cannot silently inherit that mode.

Required validation

Test multi-node bursts, namespace-preserving changes, `partition_by` behavior, memory pressure, partitions and restore. Observe counters and admitted work rather than only Redis availability.

Acceptance gates: KG-T08, KG-T12, KG-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Scaling, Redis topology/version, eviction policy, new state role or failure-mode change.

decisions.title: Distinguish operating budgets from strict spending authorization
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerFinOps and platform ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Kong's documented cost limiting reflects usage on the next request and model matching can follow the requested rather than fallback model. Shared completed-usage counters therefore do not establish a strict maximum-cost reservation before provider dispatch.

Options considered

  • Treat the configured cost window as an unconditional ceiling.
  • Accept bounded approximate budgets for ordinary workloads.
  • Add an independent reservation authority for strict financial workloads.

Proposed decision

Classify each workload's financial requirement. Use gateway limits for approved operational control; for strict ceilings require conservative atomic reservation, maximum output/target bounds and fail-closed handling when authority is unverifiable. Keep uncertain dispatched attempts pending and reconcile them before releasing authority.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Strict admission adds latency, state and an availability dependency and may reject work conservatively. Approximate workloads gain simpler operation but must accept documented in-flight and degraded-mode exposure. Neither class may silently convert unknown cost into zero.

Required validation

Run synchronized near-limit calls, expensive fallback, missing pricing, Redis failure and partial streams. Demonstrate the promised exposure bound or reject the strict-ceiling claim.

Acceptance gates: KG-T08, KG-T09. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New pricing/modality, financial risk tolerance, concurrency, regional topology or provider usage behavior.

DependenciesKG-ADR-004, KG-ADR-012, KG-ADR-018

decisions.title: Reconcile logical calls, provider attempts and billed usage
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerFinOps ledger ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

One user call can create several attempts, and final usage may arrive late or not at all. Target pricing, cached tokens and provider billing adjustments can differ from the gateway's reported estimate. Request logs are not automatically a complete or durable financial ledger.

Options considered

  • Bill internally from sampled analytics alone.
  • Maintain an independent attempt-aware ledger and reconcile supported aggregates.
  • Use only provider invoices without application attribution.

Proposed decision

Retain logical request, attempt, reservation and accounting identities with usage confidence and price version. Reconcile by the upstream's supported billing dimensions; preserve explained variance and pending amounts. Separate internal attribution from actual provider charges and avoid claiming unsupported per-request invoice joins.

Consequences and tradeoffs

An additional data pipeline and reconciliation owner are required. The organization gains traceable cost decisions without false precision. Privacy rules apply to identifiers, model names and retained operational metadata even when prompt bodies are absent.

Required validation

Reconcile a bounded live trial with retries, cache classes, cancelled streams and delayed jobs. Verify deduplication, missing-event alerts, price updates and recovery from a failed writer.

Acceptance gates: KG-T09, KG-T18, KG-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Provider billing schema, tariff, reconciliation granularity, telemetry schema or attribution-policy changes.

DependenciesKG-ADR-005, KG-ADR-019

decisions.title: Make declared configuration ownership and deletion intent explicit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerInfrastructure delivery ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Desired state, live emergency edits and saved plans can diverge. The documented planning default is sync, while apply is create/update-only. Unclear namespace ownership can turn a routine rollout into unintended deletion or leave unmanaged security drift.

Options considered

  • Let UI edits and CI changes coexist without precedence.
  • Assign scoped declarative ownership with reviewed plans and drift handling.
  • Synchronize the entire account from a convenience export.

Proposed decision

Keep security-sensitive desired state in reviewed version control with explicit gateway, region and namespace ownership. Generate apply-mode plans for additive changes. Require a separately approved deletion/sync plan and reconcile emergency edits before closure. Re-plan when relevant live state changes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Delivery is more deliberate and requires a drift process. The plan artifact becomes sensitive operational evidence even without plaintext secrets. Apply-only operation does not clean up obsolete grants automatically, so authorized retirement remains a required workflow.

Required validation

Test missing namespaces, destructive plans, concurrent changes, emergency edits and saved-plan application. Verify final fleet behavior and stable rate-counter namespaces after promotion.

Acceptance gates: KG-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

CLI/declarative schema changes, new management ownership, workflow changes or drift-related incident.

DependenciesKG-ADR-008, KG-ADR-017, KG-ADR-018

decisions.title: Promote releases with explicit managed-plane and rollback boundaries
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerRelease managerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Runtime, managed configuration, external policies and credentials can change together. Entity-level atomicity does not mean fleet-wide atomicity, and a managed-plane version may not be independently reversible by the customer. Long-lived requests can bridge a rollout.

Options considered

  • Upgrade all nodes automatically from a floating tag.
  • Promote a versioned release bundle through a canary and observed fleet state.
  • Freeze indefinitely on one release.

Proposed decision

Bundle artifact identity, managed-plane compatibility, CLI, desired state, policy-service versions and test evidence. Promote through a canary with explicit hashes and negative authorization checks. Define supported rollback and open-request treatment before rollout; do not promise a downgrade unsupported by the current managed plane.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Release throughput is constrained by qualification capacity, but failures are containable and diagnosable. Some rollbacks may require restoring configuration or coordinating with support rather than merely changing an image. Security revocations may require independent traffic exclusion.

Required validation

Rehearse a failed canary, partial fleet convergence, long stream drain and compatible recovery. Record what can and cannot be reversed and who authorizes reopening traffic.

Acceptance gates: KG-T01, KG-T07, KG-T22, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new release, synchronization contract, container variant, external policy dependency or rollback failure.

DependenciesKG-ADR-002, KG-ADR-013, KG-ADR-017, KG-ADR-021

decisions.title: Separate components only where trust and scaling justify it
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerPlatform architecture leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A managed control plane already separates administration from traffic, but model, MCP, agent and auxiliary workloads still have different resource and trust profiles. Additional pools or gateway instances can improve isolation while multiplying configuration and operations.

Options considered

  • Put all traffic and auxiliary services in one undifferentiated pool.
  • Separate by proven trust, protocol or capacity boundary.
  • Create a dedicated deployment for every endpoint.

Proposed decision

Use a small shared baseline, then separate gateway instances, traffic pools or auxiliary services where identity constraints, sensitivity or measured interference justify it. Verify that the chosen routing/configuration arrangement supports the intended scope; do not infer arbitrary per-pool entity partitioning.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some policy and credential definitions may be duplicated and need consistency checks. Stronger boundaries can reduce noisy neighbors and simplify egress. Mere process separation does not remove shared Redis, identity or provider dependencies.

Required validation

Demonstrate intended entity exposure and cross-pool isolation, independent scaling and failure containment. Measure whether separation improves the stated objective enough to cover its operating cost.

Acceptance gates: KG-T03, KG-T07, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New protocol, trust domain, resource bottleneck, identity constraint or material configuration complexity.

DependenciesKG-ADR-001, KG-ADR-007, KG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-017

decisions.title: Scale active work, buffers and connection pools together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE capacity ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Request rate and CPU alone do not capture long model streams, slow clients, large payloads or auxiliary policy latency. Autoscaling can also require control-plane and secret availability for cold nodes. Forward-proxy transport behavior may differ from direct connections.

Options considered

  • Scale only on CPU with default pools and timeouts.
  • Use measured active-work and resource indicators with bounded admission.
  • Overprovision indefinitely without testing saturation.

Proposed decision

Capacity-plan active requests, streams, tokens, bytes, sockets, buffers and auxiliary throughput together. Bound payloads and output, admit within measured capacity, and maintain enough warm capacity for the agreed failure scenario. Test the exact direct or forward-proxy network path.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Autoscaling becomes workload-aware and requires richer telemetry. Some burst traffic will be rejected to preserve service quality. Warm capacity costs more than scale-to-zero but provides a clearer outage contract.

Required validation

Sweep realistic concurrency and payloads, include slow readers and inspector saturation, and demonstrate bounded memory, latency and draining during node/zone failure.

Acceptance gates: KG-T05, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Changed workload mix, provider latency, proxy path, instance shape or policy dependency.

DependenciesKG-ADR-012, KG-ADR-013, KG-ADR-018, KG-ADR-023
