decisions.title: Export minimized telemetry through bounded and observable paths
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerObservability and privacy ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Telemetry is needed for latency, failure and cost diagnosis but can disclose identities, prompts, tool arguments and provider details. Emitted schemas change by runtime. Exporter queues, sampling and drops can create misleading operational or financial conclusions.

Options considered

  • Log full payloads for every call.
  • Use minimized metadata with explicit diagnostic exceptions.
  • Disable all telemetry to avoid data exposure.

Proposed decision

Default to metadata-only operational export, with payload and raw blocked-content logging disabled. Version the emitted schema, control cardinality and tracing baggage, and bound queues with visible drop/lag metrics. Use separate authoritative paths for required audit and financial evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some incidents require approved temporary capture rather than immediate full content access. Metadata itself still needs classification and retention. Observability failures must not silently consume unlimited memory or be mistaken for complete accounting.

Required validation

Scan exports using synthetic sensitive markers; verify correlation, terminal outcomes and denial fields under sink outage and schema change. Confirm loss detection and safe queue limits.

Acceptance gates: KG-T10, KG-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New exporter/schema, diagnostic need, data class, policy logger or retention obligation.

Configuration changes and inference events answer different audit questions. Konnect administrative source retention is seven days; longer organizational retention therefore depends on collection. The CLI can retrieve events but does not itself verify available signatures.

Options considered

  • Rely on the managed source as the permanent archive.
  • Operate a durable verified export with gap detection.
  • Use request logs as a substitute for administrative evidence.

Proposed decision

Export administrative events into a protected archive with durable checkpoints, deduplication, integrity verification where supplied and early lag alerts. Separate audit-reader from configuration-writer authority. Preserve explicit completeness gaps and test recovery inside the source expiration window.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The customer owns a small but important evidence pipeline. Archive contents may include personal identities and sensitive resource details. Collection success must be measured, not assumed from a scheduled job or webhook configuration.

Required validation

Interrupt the collector, restore from checkpoint, process duplicate/out-of-order deliveries and verify signatures independently. Demonstrate the configured retention and access policy.

Acceptance gates: KG-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Source retention, audit schema, collection mechanism, signature contract or organizational evidence requirement changes.

decisions.title: Control configuration migration and customer schemas without assuming Konnect SQL access
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerMigration leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The original reference concern about database migrations changes under managed entity mode. Customers migrate declared configuration and their own stores; they do not run schema jobs against Konnect internals. Conversion from older Kong configurations cannot reconstruct all security objects.

Options considered

  • Treat converted configuration as production-ready.
  • Use one controlled migration authority per customer-owned state domain.
  • Apply arbitrary database changes to mirror a self-hosted gateway design.

Proposed decision

Treat converter output as a draft, explicitly reconstruct Auth Strategies, Vault references and resource ACLs, and validate released schemas. Assign one owner and compatible migration procedure to each customer vector, session or accounting store. Keep managed-plane schema operations within supported APIs and vendor procedures.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Migration requires semantic and security work beyond syntax. Some objects and credentials must be reissued or remapped. The design avoids unsupported database assumptions while retaining controlled evolution of customer-owned state.

Required validation

Migrate a representative configuration, execute all denied-access cases, verify counter continuity and restore the prior compatible state. Confirm no secret or ACL was omitted by conversion.

Acceptance gates: KG-T22, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Configuration-generation change, converter update, storage schema or plugin-to-entity migration.

decisions.title: Separate liveness, serving readiness and graceful draining
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE service ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

An open process port does not prove valid configuration, usable credentials or mandatory policy dependencies. Conversely, a managed-plane interruption need not make a warm node immediately unusable. Long-lived streams need a defined removal and termination procedure.

Options considered

  • Use one shallow health endpoint for all decisions.
  • Define separate process, serving and dependency indicators.
  • Restart every node whenever the managed plane is unreachable.

Proposed decision

Use liveness only for process recovery, readiness for the approved serving contract, and independent dependency/configuration-age telemetry. Drain nodes before replacement, bound long-request termination and preserve incomplete outcomes. Exclude stale sensitive nodes through traffic control rather than indiscriminate restart loops.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Health logic is more nuanced but avoids destroying warm capacity during management outages. A policy-staleness rule can intentionally reduce availability. Drain duration must fit rollout and recovery objectives.

Required validation

Test warm/cold nodes, stale ACLs, unavailable required inspection, revoked credentials and long streams during removal. Confirm that readiness decisions match the approved degraded mode.

Acceptance gates: KG-T05, KG-T07, KG-T21, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Health API, ingress behavior, mandatory dependency or acceptable policy-age change.

DependenciesKG-ADR-007, KG-ADR-013, KG-ADR-022, KG-ADR-024

decisions.title: Demonstrate multi-zone availability before adding regions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerInfrastructure reliability leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A second geographic region adds identity, state, quota and data-governance complexity. Many initial failures can be addressed with multiple warm nodes across zones in one approved region. Merely drawing a standby does not provide provider or inspection capacity.

Options considered

  • Start with one unprotected node.
  • Establish a multi-zone service and prove its failure behavior.
  • Begin with active-active global routing.

Proposed decision

Build a multi-zone baseline in one approved processing region, with explicit node, provider and auxiliary capacity for the selected zone-loss scenario. Add regions only after a concrete recovery, latency or residency requirement justifies the additional design.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This limits initial complexity but does not cover complete regional loss. The residual regional risk must be accepted. Shared identity, Redis and inspection remain dependencies and need their own availability design.

Required validation

Lose a serving node and zone under representative traffic, verify limits and identity behavior, and demonstrate recovery without unsafe retries or policy gaps.

Acceptance gates: KG-T07, KG-T08, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A regional continuity requirement, provider concentration risk or unacceptable measured recovery result.

DependenciesKG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-018, KG-ADR-023, KG-ADR-024, KG-ADR-028

decisions.title: Allocate capacity and monetary authority by regional enforcement domain
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerGlobal platform and FinOps ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Regional failover can duplicate quota or spending authority when counters are not globally consistent. Cross-region movement can also violate model, document and retained-resource ownership. Global coordination trades simpler accounting for latency and availability dependence.

Options considered

  • Assume one configuration implies globally shared limits.
  • Allocate bounded regional authority with explicit rebalancing.
  • Use a separately qualified strongly coordinated global admission service.

Proposed decision

For the reference multi-region extension, allocate explicit provider capacity and spending envelopes to each region and reconcile centrally. Rebalance through an auditable authority transfer, not concurrent grants. Keep fallback inside the approved processing and resource-ownership envelope. Use a global service only when its latency and failure contract is accepted.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Unused capacity may remain stranded during a partition, reducing utilization but bounding risk. Operations need a reallocation procedure and regional observability. A failover cannot exceed the surviving region's approved authority merely because demand moved.

Required validation

Partition regions, activate recovery traffic and attempt simultaneous near-limit dispatch. Verify total authority, provider capacity and forbidden destination rejection.

Acceptance gates: KG-T08, KG-T09, KG-T10, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Regional topology, financial exposure tolerance, residency constraints or global coordination capability changes.

DependenciesKG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-018, KG-ADR-019, KG-ADR-020, KG-ADR-029

decisions.title: Recover configuration, credentials and external state coherently
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerDisaster recovery ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A running node image is not the complete service. Recovery may require declared entities, write-only credentials, session keys, vector state, accounting reservations and application mappings to provider resources. Restoring stale state can resurrect access or lower spend counters.

Options considered

  • Restore only containers and hope the managed plane fills all gaps.
  • Maintain a coordinated recovery manifest and independent secret custody.
  • Snapshot every store without consistency or retention review.

Proposed decision

Document the recovery authority and acceptable loss for each state domain. Reconstruct managed entities through supported APIs and restore customer-owned stores with compatible versions and key material. Reconcile financial and access state before reopening traffic; retain provider-resource ownership outside the gateway.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery requires cross-team coordination and periodic exercises. Some caches can be discarded, while sessions, reservations and task mappings may need durable restoration. Backups carry the same confidentiality obligations as their source data.

Required validation

Rebuild an isolated environment, restore required stores and credentials, and verify no expired grant, duplicate task or reduced financial authority is silently introduced.

Acceptance gates: KG-T16, KG-T18, KG-T21, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New stateful feature, backup mechanism, retention policy, encryption key or recovery objective.

decisions.title: Verify artifact provenance and sustain the AI release cadence
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSoftware supply-chain ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A gateway handles provider credentials and sensitive traffic, making its image and privileged dependencies high-impact artifacts. Distroless, read-only and FIPS-oriented packages address different concerns. The dedicated AI release line has no LTS and requires an active update process.

Options considered

  • Trust floating vendor tags and automatic production upgrades.
  • Pin verified artifacts and maintain recurring security qualification.
  • Freeze a release without a supported patch plan.

Proposed decision

Record image digests and available provenance evidence, verify acquired artifacts, scan the deployed bill of materials and restrict runtime privileges. Qualify packaging/TLS variants independently. Maintain a funded patch and supported-minor process with an emergency lane; do not claim whole-system compliance from a package label.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Security and release work becomes recurring operational cost. Minimal images can complicate diagnostics, requiring approved external tooling. Updates remain controlled rather than untested automatic changes or indefinite deferral.

Required validation

Verify artifact identity, least-privilege startup, writable paths, TLS behavior, dependency inventory and rollback. Exercise an emergency security promotion through the core contract tests.

Acceptance gates: KG-T01, KG-T21, KG-T22, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Security advisory, image provenance change, FIPS requirement, platform base image or supported-version policy change.

decisions.title: Treat extensions and policy services as privileged code
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerPlatform extension ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Custom functions, plugins and external policy services can inspect content, alter requests and use powerful network credentials. Their capabilities may differ between entity and plugin mode. A configuration extension is not harmless merely because it is shorter than an application service.

Options considered

  • Allow arbitrary team-defined production extensions.
  • Maintain an approved extension inventory and isolated service boundary.
  • Forbid all extensions, including necessary policy integrations.

Proposed decision

Permit only reviewed, versioned extensions supported by the chosen deployment model. Restrict executable configuration, outbound destinations, secret access and runtime model downloads. Operate external inspection or credential services with their own deployment, security and failure contracts. Never accept executable code or callback destinations from ordinary callers.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some bespoke requirements may need a separate application component rather than an in-process extension. Review and testing add delivery work but make the trust boundary explicit. An extension failure must not silently bypass mandatory authorization or inspection.

Required validation

Exercise unapproved-code rejection, secret/egress restrictions, dependency failure and upgrade compatibility. Verify that administrative scope prevents application callers from installing or modifying privileged behavior.

Acceptance gates: KG-T03, KG-T10, KG-T11, KG-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New extension mechanism, custom policy, external service, runtime language or privilege requirement.

DependenciesKG-ADR-001, KG-ADR-008, KG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-014, KG-ADR-032

decisions.title: Default-deny MCP tools and separate execution authority
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerAgent security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

MCP discovery, per-tool ACLs, aggregation and invocation credentials are distinct contracts. Per-tool rules can override defaults, and catalog visibility does not authorize an action on a business resource. An LLM's requested tool call must not become a grant of privilege.

Options considered

  • Publish all discovered tools under a shared powerful credential.
  • Use explicit catalog/tool grants and backend business authorization.
  • Expose only application-specific tool endpoints outside the gateway.

Proposed decision

Default-deny the published tool set and review every override. Authorize discovery and execution separately, use distinct discovery/invocation credentials, restrict forwarded headers and destinations, and require executor-side ownership checks and idempotency. Qualify delegated exchange only for the supported protocol/mode.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Tool onboarding requires security review and a negative-test corpus. Some catalog convenience is lost, but privilege is not inferred from model output, schema annotations or aggregator membership. Gateway and executor must share usable correlation without exposing secrets.

Required validation

Test missing/overriding ACLs, catalog caching, aggregation collisions, credential scope, argument manipulation, denied-call evidence and timeout after a mutating action.

Acceptance gates: KG-T14, KG-T15, KG-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New tool/source, ACL semantics, token exchange, protocol revision, credential audience or business action.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-007, KG-ADR-009, KG-ADR-010, KG-ADR-012, KG-ADR-025, KG-ADR-033

Context

Files, responses, jobs and agent tasks can outlive a gateway connection. A2A proxying does not create gateway-owned task state. MCP protocol statelessness does not eliminate application sessions. Moving these operations between targets without an owner map can fail or disclose resources.

Options considered

  • Balance all operations freely by model alias.
  • Persist explicit resource/task owner and principal mappings.
  • Ban all stateful APIs from the platform.

Proposed decision

Keep durable resource authority in the application or owning upstream and bind operations to the authenticated principal, provider account and approved geography. Use gateway/session stores only for their qualified scope. On uncertain completion, reconcile through the owner before retry; re-authorize every retrieval, cancellation and deletion.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications retain lifecycle responsibilities even with a common gateway API. Some fallback and migration paths become intentionally constrained. State exports and recovery must include mappings and independent secret/session material, not only endpoint configuration.

Required validation

Test cross-principal resource access, stale IDs, task recovery, session replay/rotation and provider-bound continuation during gateway restart or regional change.

Acceptance gates: KG-T03, KG-T16, KG-T17, KG-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New stateful endpoint, session mode, agent protocol, storage owner or migration requirement.

decisions.title: Govern asynchronous, batch and media workloads separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerAsynchronous workload ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Large uploads and delayed jobs consume resources beyond a synchronous request. Job acceptance, job completion and billable usage occur at different times. A submission timeout may leave a real upstream job, so immediate resubmission can duplicate work and cost.

Options considered

  • Apply chat timeouts and post-response budgets to all work.
  • Use a durable job authority and workload-specific admission.
  • Route asynchronous work outside the gateway with equivalent controls.

Proposed decision

Approve each batch/media API separately with payload limits, durable ownership, cost envelope, idempotency/reconciliation and result retention. Record submission and completion as distinct events. Keep unknown jobs and usage pending, and bind polling/retrieval/deletion to their owner rather than ordinary model balancing.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The application needs job state and cleanup procedures. Gateway convenience does not remove object storage, modality pricing or provider lifecycle differences. Some paths may be better served directly when the gateway adds no required control.

Required validation

Test uncertain submission, oversized media, delayed completion, duplicate delivery, result authorization, deletion and missing final usage under gateway restart.

Acceptance gates: KG-T09, KG-T18, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New modality, batch API, provider job lifecycle, storage destination or pricing unit.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-012, KG-ADR-019, KG-ADR-020, KG-ADR-024, KG-ADR-035

decisions.title: Keep application quality and retrieval authorization with accountable product owners
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerProduct and data ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A valid normalized response can still be wrong for the task. Model substitution, injected retrieval and semantic reuse change application behavior. Document authorization and malicious source instructions cannot be solved merely by routing through an AI policy.

Options considered

  • Treat gateway/provider compatibility as sufficient quality acceptance.
  • Maintain application-owned quality and data-access gates.
  • Freeze one model and avoid all evaluation.

Proposed decision

Require product-owned task evaluations for aliases, fallbacks, tools, retrieval and cache changes. Keep document ownership and ingestion/deletion lifecycle explicit. Use application-managed retrieval as the baseline; enable gateway RAG only after explicit ACL/filter and provenance tests resolve the documented ambiguities.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Platform and product releases must coordinate. Model and cache optimization are constrained by measurable task quality. The gateway remains a shared enforcement/integration layer rather than the sole authority for business correctness or source access.

Required validation

Run representative and adversarial task fixtures, structured-output validation, unauthorized-document tests and source-deletion cases. Compare complete task outcomes, not only response syntax or latency.

Acceptance gates: KG-T04, KG-T12, KG-T13, KG-T15. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Changed model, prompt, retrieval/index, tool catalog, data entitlement or quality distribution.

decisions.title: Contract for topology, entitlement, support and operating duties
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerProcurement and service ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Documentation establishes available concepts but does not confirm the organization's license, deployment rights, support response or processing terms. Dedicated entity mode, self-managed plugins and adjacent products can have different commercial and operational boundaries.

Options considered

  • Assume all documented Kong capabilities are included.
  • Obtain an explicit bill of required capabilities and responsibilities.
  • Choose solely on a public headline request price.

Proposed decision

Confirm the selected generation, regions, environments, traffic families, required policies, support level, version obligations, data handling and recovery/exit rights in the agreement. Price customer-operated dependencies and release work alongside the license. Treat Context Mesh and other adjacent services as separate unless expressly included.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Procurement requires a precise architecture and may change the shortlist. A managed plane can save some operations while leaving data-plane and auxiliary duties with the customer. No monetary savings or service guarantee is assumed without terms and measured evidence.

Required validation

Complete the capability/ownership checklist, obtain written responses for unresolved deployment and support questions, and reconcile the contract with the deployed topology and runbooks.

Acceptance gates: KG-T01, KG-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Renewal, new environment/region, traffic-family expansion, support policy, pricing or adjacent-service adoption.

decisions.title: Qualify performance and service objectives with the real policy stack
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerPerformance engineering leadDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Published throughput and sizing guidance use specific assumptions. Authentication, Redis, guardrails, embeddings, long streams and provider limits can dominate actual performance. Comparing different models or disabled policies would not answer the organization's selection question.

Options considered

  • Adopt vendor headline numbers as production capacity.
  • Run matched workload and failure experiments against a direct baseline.
  • Choose the implementation language presumed fastest.

Proposed decision

Measure the approved application contract with the intended policy, network and storage composition. Report latency phases, percentiles, completed/incomplete tasks, resource saturation, provider throttling and cost per successful task. Use realistic streaming, media and failure cases and retain reproducible artifacts.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Benchmarking consumes engineering effort and limited provider spend. Results apply to the measured workload and version, not a universal ranking. A faster gateway is not preferred if it weakens the required governance or quality contract.

Required validation

Execute direct and gateway baselines with matched provider parameters, then load and fault sweeps. Accept only objectives agreed by application and operations owners with visible residual limits.

Acceptance gates: KG-T05, KG-T19, KG-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Runtime, hardware, policy chain, provider, network, workload mix or service objective changes.

DependenciesKG-ADR-003, KG-ADR-013, KG-ADR-024, KG-ADR-025, KG-ADR-029, KG-ADR-037, KG-ADR-038

decisions.title: Maintain a tested exit strategy and a living decision register
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerEnterprise architecture ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A common request shape does not remove dependency on managed configuration, credential mappings, policy behavior and retained resources. Commercial terms and a rapid AI lifecycle can change the preferred option. Proposed decisions must not become permanent by being forgotten.

Options considered

  • Assume OpenAI compatibility makes migration trivial.
  • Maintain independent contracts and rehearse a bounded exit.
  • Avoid all managed products regardless of demonstrated value.

Proposed decision

Keep application contracts, quality fixtures, normalized accounting and resource ownership outside vendor-specific configuration. Maintain independent secret recovery and export procedures. Rehearse one low-risk workload on another qualified path. Review accepted ADRs on their triggers, with explicit supersession and residual-risk ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some portability work is paid before it is needed, but switching risk and procurement dependency become visible. Not every capability will port unchanged; differences are recorded as contract changes rather than hidden through a nominally compatible endpoint.

Required validation

Move a representative workload to direct provider access or another gateway and verify identity, complete streams, resource lifecycle, quality and attribution. Restore the original route without duplicate side effects.

Acceptance gates: KG-T22, KG-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Contract renewal, unsupported capability, lifecycle change, material cost/quality shift or missed operating objective.

decisions.title: Choose native Foundry and gateway composition explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerAI platform architectDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Foundry supplies model and application services, while APIM supplies a policy and API operating boundary. Adding a gateway can centralize useful controls but also adds latency, credentials, failure dependencies and duplicated mechanisms. The reference organization needs shared governance without assuming that every application benefits from another layer.

Options considered

  • Direct native service calls with application-owned controls.
  • Established APIM managed gateway over approved Foundry endpoints.
  • Dedicated preview gateway, or a customer-operated alternative such as LiteLLM/Bifrost.

Proposed decision

Establish a bounded native Foundry contract first. Add an established APIM composition only for named shared requirements that cannot be met more simply at the application boundary. Evaluate the dedicated preview tier separately. Record which layer owns caller authorization, provider translation, model selection, retries, budgets, state and telemetry; leave no mandatory responsibility implied by a product name.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The design preserves a direct behavioral baseline and prevents premature gateway commitment. It requires an explicit capability and responsibility inventory, and may leave simple applications on a separately governed direct path. An existing well-operated gateway is not replaced without evidence of benefit.

Required validation

Compare native and mediated fixtures, complete task quality, latency, operational effort and cost for representative callers. Test every allowed direct path for equivalent mandatory controls. Reject a composition with an unowned or bypassable invariant.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T02 · AZ-T04 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new provider, shared-policy requirement, operating constraint or measured duplication changes the value of the gateway.

DependenciesFoundational record; no earlier Azure ADR dependency.

Evidence informing this proposal[H31] [MS02] [P28] [P29]

Original concernADR-001. Choose the shared-service boundary rather than assume an AI gateway is mandatory. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Qualify gateway generation, SKU and feature maturity as one baseline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerAPI platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Established APIM classic/v2/workspace/self-hosted gateways, the Foundry portal association and the dedicated AI Gateway tier are different deployment contracts. The newer tier remains preview, while its September update supersedes parts of older identity and alias documentation. A single Azure product label is insufficient release evidence.

Options considered

  • Treat all APIM AI descriptions as a common interchangeable feature set.
  • Select one exact service/API/SKU/region/feature manifest and qualify it.
  • Run separate baseline and preview pilots with explicit parity gates.

Proposed decision

Maintain a manifest of gateway family, SKU, API versions, region, enabled previews, policy support and tenant rollout. Use established managed v2 as the initial composed candidate, not a universal production mandate. Pilot the dedicated tier separately and test the September Entra, alias and streaming changes. Preserve documented contradictions and require observed behavior before resolving them in favor of a design.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The organization cannot blindly reuse XML policies, workspace assumptions or support commitments across modes. Qualification work increases, but preview exposure is visible and rollback is meaningful. The manifest becomes part of every application acceptance record.

Required validation

Deploy the actual selected topology, exercise each required policy and management operation, and record observed rollout/version evidence. Prove that an unsupported mandatory feature blocks release rather than being silently ignored.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T14 · AZ-T18 · AZ-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A service reaches GA, changes management schema, adds a required policy, or changes SKU/region support.

decisions.title: Publish a bounded API and capability contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerApplication/API ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A common client schema does not establish behavioral equivalence across native model APIs, APIM mediation, Responses, streams and agent protocols. Some options are model-specific, some are preview, and some state remains provider-owned. Broad route exposure increases combinations faster than a small team can qualify.

Options considered

  • Expose every imported operation and rely on provider errors.
  • Approve a narrow positive capability catalog with explicit expansion gates.
  • Offer unrestricted passthrough alongside the normalized API.

Proposed decision

Publish supported tuples of endpoint, model/version, deployment mode, gateway, policy, geography and state behavior. Reject unspecified operations or parameters rather than silently discarding their meaning. Start with a small chat contract and independently version embeddings, Responses, batch and tools. Any passthrough route requires the same authorization, privacy and accounting review as a normalized route.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications gain a stable, testable interface at the cost of delayed access to some newly released features. Contract ownership stays with the organization, not with whichever provider schema is easiest to import. Additive provider fields can be tolerated without making unsupported actions available.

Required validation

Retain positive and negative fixtures for fields, tools, structured output, errors, content checks and state operations. Compare direct and mediated paths and explain every material difference. Test newly exposed operations before promotion.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T07 · AZ-T08 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

An application requires a new modality, protocol, provider-native feature or stateful lifecycle.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-001 · AZ-ADR-002

Evidence informing this proposal[MS13] [MS20] [MS21] [MS51] [MS59]

Original concernADR-003. Preserve the bounded endpoint and semantic-contract concern. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

Compare direct and mediated paths and explain every material difference. Test newly exposed operations before promotion. Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T07 · AZ-T08 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T19 . decisions.title: Version aliases and model-router candidate promises
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaPlatform contractSuggested ownerModel platform and product ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A stable alias can be retargeted while its model behavior, context capacity, cost and processing scope change. Router candidates can evolve independently of client code. Applications therefore need a service promise stronger than a name that continues to resolve.

Options considered

  • Treat aliases and router defaults as transparent infrastructure.
  • Pin a concrete model permanently and avoid routing.
  • Version a logical alias with approved candidates and application evidence.

Proposed decision

Own logical aliases in reviewed configuration. Bind each to approved deployments or an explicitly constrained router policy, supported capabilities, processing scope and a task-quality threshold. Treat retargeting, candidate additions and retirement replacements as releases. Preserve requested alias, effective policy and available observed model identity in restricted evidence; do not imply an immutable candidate set from the router version string alone.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Provider changes become manageable without being invisible. Product teams must participate in model promotion, and some fast catalog updates will wait for evidence. A pinned alias can still require replacement when its underlying model retires.

Required validation

Run task, tool, schema and long-context regressions for every candidate; verify privacy and cost bounds. Test that an unauthorized or incompatible target cannot be reached by fallback or alias manipulation.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T05 · AZ-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Retargeting, candidate-set change, retirement notice, material pricing change or quality regression.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-003

Evidence informing this proposal[MS06] [MS16] [MS17] [MS18] [MS25]

Original concernADR-004. Preserve logical model versioning while adding router-pool lifecycle. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Assign accountable identities to workloads and environments
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerIdentity platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Shared credentials obscure ownership, make revocation disruptive and can give several teams the same apparent policy identity. APIM subscription keys, Foundry resource keys and Entra workload identities have different authority and lifecycle. Attribution metadata supplied by a caller cannot repair an untrustworthy credential model.

Options considered

  • Share one gateway/provider key across applications.
  • Issue separately controlled keys with documented limitations.
  • Prefer distinct Entra workload identities with explicit environment ownership.

Proposed decision

Use distinct workload identities for production services and environments where the selected endpoint supports them. Record owner, purpose, allowed APIs/models and credential lifecycle. Keep end-user identity separate and derive cost attribution from verified mappings. Permit keys only through an explicit exception inventory with narrow exposure, rotation and revocation tests; never use an administrator credential as a normal inference credential.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More identity objects and lifecycle automation are required. Incident containment and cost attribution become more precise. Key-only clients may need an application adapter or a bounded exception rather than an automatic broad grant.

Required validation

Demonstrate that one workload can be disabled without affecting unrelated applications. Verify owner attribution across aliases, caches, tools and asynchronous jobs and that client-supplied labels cannot charge another owner.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T02 · AZ-T03 · AZ-T11. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new application/environment, identity compromise, unsupported client authentication or organizational ownership change.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-001 · AZ-ADR-003

Evidence informing this proposal[MS19] [MS29] [MS06] [MS07]

Original concernADR-005. Replace the default virtual-key assumption with qualified Entra workload identity. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Validate issuer, audience and runtime grants independently
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerSecurity/identity ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A correctly signed token may belong to another tenant, another API or a principal without the required operation. Gateway runtime roles, Foundry project roles and backend service permissions must not be treated as interchangeable. The preview gateway now offers scoped Entra runtime grants, but older key descriptions remain relevant to key-mode risk.

Options considered

  • Accept any valid tenant token.
  • Check issuer/audience only and delegate all authorization to the backend.
  • Validate credential context and an explicit grant before resolving a backend.

Proposed decision

Require approved issuers and audiences plus applicable application roles or gateway asset grants. Bind caller context to verified claims. Keep backend token acquisition independent, with an explicit intended resource and destination. Qualify preview alias/MCP-server scope and role propagation; do not infer per-tool business permissions or narrow API-key grants from the new Entra surface.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications must request the correct token audience and receive deliberate grants. Misconfiguration fails earlier and more visibly. The policy owner must manage role definitions and claim changes rather than relying on a generic bearer-token check.

Required validation

Exercise wrong tenant, audience, role, principal and resource scope; test expiry and grant removal. Confirm that an authorization rejection produces no upstream dispatch and that downstream tokens are never returned to the caller.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T02 · AZ-T03 · AZ-T04. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Identity-provider configuration, role definition, client authentication flow or gateway release changes.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-003 · AZ-ADR-005

Evidence informing this proposal[MS29] [MS30] [MS19] [MS06]

Original concernADR-006. Preserve explicit JWT/OIDC validation and separate it from downstream authority. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Enforce tenant and object isolation beyond projects and workspaces
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerApplication security and data ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Foundry projects and APIM workspaces are administrative constructs with specific runtime behavior. They do not automatically authorize business documents, tool actions or stateful IDs. Resource keys can bypass the granular Foundry RBAC model, and indexed permission projections can be stale.

Options considered

  • Use project/workspace names as the sole tenant boundary.
  • Add application-owned authorization and separate identities to shared infrastructure.
  • Separate resources, gateways, stores or subscriptions for stronger isolation.

Proposed decision

Make tenant and resource isolation an end-to-end invariant. Derive tenant identity server-side; authorize every retrieval, conversation/file/job operation and tool action against the owner. Select physical/resource separation when shared controls cannot meet the threat model. Construct Search permissions from trusted identity and track their freshness. Test keys, direct paths and global policy inheritance rather than assuming a project or workspace confines them.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some applications need separate resources or explicit ownership stores, increasing cost and administration. Shared deployments remain possible where negative tests prove isolation. Revocation and deletion must include caches, citations and active agent workflows.

Required validation

Perform cross-tenant enumeration, guessed-ID, filter-injection and tool-object tests. Measure source-permission revocation to denial across retrieval and cached answers. Inspect effective shared identities and grant inheritance.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T13 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

External tenants, more sensitive data, new stateful APIs, workspace adoption or permission-ingestion changes.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-003 · AZ-ADR-005 · AZ-ADR-006

Evidence informing this proposal[MS19] [MS42] [MS55] [MS56]

Original concernADR-007. Extend tenant isolation to Foundry resources, Search projections and application-owned state. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Separate administration from inference and policy use
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerPlatform security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

An operator who changes routes or policies may control which destinations receive content and which credentials the gateway can exercise. Runtime callers should not acquire that authority. Portal convenience can blur provisioning, development and production operations.

Options considered

  • Allow application teams broad service administration.
  • Delegate narrow API administration under enforced central policy.
  • Use separate production management identities, approvals and network exposure.

Proposed decision

Restrict administrative grants independently of runtime invocation. Use controlled deployment identities, named operator access and narrowly delegated scopes. Treat policy/backend edits as privileged security changes, especially where managed identities are assigned. Keep administration off application-facing routes and require attributable emergency changes followed by reconciliation into reviewed source.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Self-service becomes structured rather than unrestricted. Emergency edits remain possible but must be time-bounded, audited and reconciled. Separate management access reduces accidental credential and policy exposure without proving complete runtime isolation by itself.

Required validation

Attempt management operations with runtime identities and policy edits with restricted developer identities. Inspect role assignments, effective credential use and audit exports. Confirm management APIs are not exposed through inference routing.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T02 · AZ-T03 · AZ-T14 · AZ-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New delegated teams, automation identities, privilege incidents or a change of gateway/control-plane model.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-005 · AZ-ADR-006 · AZ-ADR-007

Evidence informing this proposal[MS19] [MS30] [MS42] [MS46]

Original concernADR-008. Preserve independent administrative access and privilege review. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Separate encryption lifecycle from access credentials
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerSecurity and key-management ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Managed identities reduce static secrets but external providers, tool connections, certificates and customer data stores still introduce credential and encryption dependencies. Rotation and restoration have different purposes: rotating access should not make durable data unreadable, and restoring keys should not restore obsolete access.

Options considered

  • Embed provider keys and encryption values in deployment configuration.
  • Use managed identities and approved secret references with distinct key lifecycles.
  • Require customer-managed keys for every service regardless of available benefit or support.

Proposed decision

Prefer workload identity where supported; use controlled secret references otherwise. Maintain separate lifecycle and ownership for provider credentials, signing/TLS material and encryption keys. Record service-specific customer-key support and exclusions rather than making a blanket encryption claim. Restore key references and data coherently while reapplying current revocations and least-privilege grants.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Key and secret inventories become part of deployment and recovery. Customer-managed encryption can add availability dependencies and does not control every service processing path. Some external providers remain key-based and need bounded exceptions.

Required validation

Rotate identities and secrets under load, inspect every log/trace sink, disable key versions in nonproduction and restore the approved state/key set. Verify that clients never receive backend tokens or secrets.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T04 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T22 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Provider/tool addition, key-management requirement, credential compromise or retention/recovery change.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-005 · AZ-ADR-006 · AZ-ADR-008

Evidence informing this proposal[MS15] [MS30] [MS31]

Original concernADR-009. Preserve distinct encryption and access-credential lifecycles. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Bind routing to approved processing and network envelopes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity and trustSuggested ownerNetwork and privacy ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Gateway location, private connectivity, model processing geography and storage location are distinct properties. Global or data-zone model deployment can reach a broader processing scope than the gateway region. Safety, embedding, telemetry and tool calls introduce additional destinations beyond inference.

Options considered

  • Infer residency from the gateway or account region.
  • Approve every reachable destination and processing/storage contract.
  • Forbid all cross-region services even when the workload permits them.

Proposed decision

Approve a complete data-flow envelope per alias and workload: client/gateway/backend paths, model processing scope, state storage, safety/embedding services, tools and telemetry. Enforce destination and region restrictions before primary or fallback dispatch. Configure inbound and outbound private networking independently where required, and treat managed identity as authentication rather than network bypass. Unknown processing terms block the dependent sensitive workload.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some models, router candidates or gateway regions may be excluded despite technical availability. The design can still use wider processing scopes where policy explicitly permits them. Network and privacy owners must participate in model and tool changes.

Required validation

Verify DNS, routing, public-path denial and all auxiliary recipients. Trigger fallbacks and confirm destination eligibility. Review service-specific retention/processing evidence for the actual deployment, not a generic catalog description.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T04 · AZ-T05 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new region, deployment mode, router candidate, tool, telemetry destination or network feature changes the flow graph.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-004 · AZ-ADR-006 · AZ-ADR-007 · AZ-ADR-009

Evidence informing this proposal[MS10] [MS14] [MS15] [MS32] [MS47]

Original concernADR-010. Preserve egress/residency control across Azure processing and auxiliary paths. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Separate semantic model selection from endpoint load balancing
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerModel platform and SRE ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Foundry model router changes which model performs a task, while APIM pools select endpoints and apply transport resilience. Both can be enabled at once, creating hidden selection and retry interactions. Models that share an input schema are not necessarily equivalent in quality, context or tools.

Options considered

  • Enable adaptive selection and fallback independently at every layer.
  • Use fixed approved aliases and simple equivalent-target pools initially.
  • Adopt one constrained router policy after task-level evaluation.

Proposed decision

Start with fixed approved models or equivalent deployment pools. Introduce semantic routing as a separately reviewed product capability with one accountable candidate-policy owner. Distinguish router decisions from transport attempts in evidence. Every candidate and fallback must satisfy the same authorization, state, feature and processing envelope; do not let a successful fallback override those requirements.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The initial design may forgo automatic cost/quality optimization but is easier to explain and recover. Later routing experiments need representative quality and complete-cost data. A change in candidate set is an application-facing release even when the alias remains stable.

Required validation

Compare fixed and routed task outcomes, verify all possible destinations and observe nested attempts under failure. Test long-context, tool and structured-output cases where apparent schema compatibility is insufficient.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T05 · AZ-T06 · AZ-T18 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Measured cost/quality opportunity, provider capacity constraint or new router capability with adequate evidence.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-003 · AZ-ADR-004 · AZ-ADR-010

Evidence informing this proposal[MS16] [MS17] [MS28]

Original concernADR-011. Preserve deliberate routing, distinguishing equivalent endpoints from model choice. No automatic acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Assign one retry owner and preserve the total deadline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerRuntime platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Applications, SDKs, APIM policies, router services and providers can each perform recovery. Multiplying retries can increase cost, overload a failing provider and duplicate tool effects. A client timeout does not reveal whether upstream execution happened.

Options considered

  • Accept each layer’s default retries.
  • Disable all recovery and return every transient failure.
  • Assign a bounded recovery owner and explicit retryability contract.

Proposed decision

Assign one recovery owner per route and document any unavoidable inner behavior. Bound total attempts, backoff and elapsed deadline across all layers. Retry only an eligible request against approved targets, accounting for possible prior execution. Do not replay after client-visible output, durable submission or a business side effect without an explicit idempotency/reconciliation contract. Carry remaining deadline and attempt context through the call graph.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some transient failures become visible instead of being hidden by repeated attempts. Provider expense and tail latency become more predictable. The application must distinguish confirmed pre-dispatch failure from uncertain execution and expose a useful recovery path to users.

Required validation

Inject each failure class and count upstream dispatches. Verify deadline exhaustion, Retry-After handling, no unauthorized fallback and no duplicate business action. Confirm SDK retry configuration instead of relying on defaults.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T06 · AZ-T07 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

SDK, policy, router or provider behavior changes; a new stateful or side-effecting route is introduced.

decisions.title: Publish streaming, cancellation and incomplete-outcome semantics
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerApplication and API runtime ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Streaming commits response headers and content before final model usage and success are known. Gateways may buffer, add events or terminate after a policy finding. A disconnected client can leave billable work running, and a partial tool argument stream is not an executable complete instruction.

Options considered

  • Treat HTTP 200 and socket closure as success.
  • Buffer every response before delivery.
  • Publish explicit streaming modes and outcome states with tested cancellation.

Proposed decision

Define complete, refused, policy-blocked, incomplete, client-cancelled and uncertain-upstream outcomes. Qualify ingress/gateway/provider event behavior, including usage-only chunks. Choose buffering versus incremental delivery per risk and latency requirement. Never silently replay or merge a second answer after visible output. Propagate cancellation where supported and preserve unresolved usage/spend until the upstream result is known.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Clients need protocol-aware parsers and explicit recovery UX. Preventive output checks may increase first-token latency. Financial reporting cannot always settle immediately on disconnect, and some provider operations may remain noncancellable.

Required validation

Interrupt streams at each lifecycle stage and use slow consumers. Assert event ordering, partial tool handling, terminal errors, cancellation acknowledgement and accounting status. Inspect actual bytes, not only gateway metrics.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T07 · AZ-T08 · AZ-T11. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New client library, stream protocol, content-check mode, preview usage event or long-running model behavior.

decisions.title: Qualify required safety controls by route and release boundary
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaRouting and runtimeSuggested ownerSafety and application security ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Foundry filtering, APIM content checks and application validators are separate mechanisms. Their scope, data destinations and timing differ. Streaming checks can detect content after earlier fragments were released; a text check cannot authorize a transaction or guarantee safe retrieval.

Options considered

  • Assume default model filtering covers every organizational requirement.
  • Apply every available guardrail without ownership or latency analysis.
  • Specify required preventive/detective controls per route and test their execution.

Proposed decision

Name the required check, enforcement point, inspected fields, failure policy and processing location for each endpoint. Use a hold-before-release design where complete prevention is mandatory, otherwise explicitly approve incremental exposure. Fail closed on unavailable mandatory checks. Keep business authorization and transaction validation outside model-content classification, and review every new safety recipient as a data flow.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some workloads accept greater latency or cannot use an unqualified streaming path. Duplicate filtering is avoided unless it addresses a distinct requirement. Operators can distinguish a model refusal, a policy block and a broken detector.

Required validation

Inject safe synthetic markers into all relevant fields and fail the checking service. Assert no prohibited byte or action escapes required prevention, including cache hits, native passthrough and tools. Measure latency and false-positive impact.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T08 · AZ-T13 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New policy requirement, endpoint, safety integration, threshold, streaming mode or processing destination.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-003 · AZ-ADR-007 · AZ-ADR-010 · AZ-ADR-013

decisions.title: Keep exact response reuse off until eligibility is proven
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerApplication/data ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A cached answer can contain personalized or permission-sensitive data and can outlive its model, prompt or source policy. Native prompt-prefix caching is a different optimization from returning a previous complete result. Cost savings alone do not justify reuse across authorization boundaries.

Options considered

  • Enable broad response caching to reduce provider calls.
  • Disable complete-response reuse initially.
  • Permit explicitly eligible exact reuse with scoped keys and invalidation.

Proposed decision

Keep complete-response caching disabled at initial rollout. Permit exact reuse only for approved read-only requests with a key binding trusted tenant/permission context, model and prompt contract, safety policy and all relevant inputs. Authenticate and authorize every hit. Exclude side-effecting operations and sensitive personalized results unless a specific safe contract is demonstrated. Set retention and invalidation obligations.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Initial provider consumption may be higher. Cache behavior becomes understandable and tenant-safe. Model/policy/source changes may require invalidation and can create miss bursts that must fit capacity and budget.

Required validation

Test cross-owner requests, changed permissions, policy/model updates, expiry, deletion and cache outage. Demonstrate that hits do not bypass current authorization or mandatory safety checks and that reported cache savings use honest accounting.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T13 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A measured repetitive workload with safe reuse potential, or a change in data classification or authorization semantics.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-003 · AZ-ADR-004 · AZ-ADR-007 · AZ-ADR-014

decisions.title: Treat semantic caching as an evaluated application feature
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerProduct and retrieval ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Semantic similarity can identify related questions without preserving the correct answer, time context or permission scope. APIM semantic caching introduces an embedding path and a configured cache, with feature availability dependent on topology. A similarity threshold is not a security or correctness guarantee.

Options considered

  • Use semantic caching as a transparent gateway optimization.
  • Use exact reuse only.
  • Run a separately governed semantic-reuse experiment for eligible tasks.

Proposed decision

Approve semantic caching independently of exact caching. Define eligible tasks, a permission-bound namespace, model/prompt versions, cache lifetime and a measured false-match tolerance. Include embedding and cache destinations in the privacy inventory. Do not ignore security-relevant system instructions or permit cross-tenant reuse. Verify the chosen gateway supports the required external cache configuration before deployment.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Evaluation and invalidation work can outweigh savings for low-repetition tasks. Similarity tuning is application-specific. A cache rollout can improve latency while degrading answer accuracy, so quality and authorization remain release gates.

Required validation

Use adversarial near-neighbor prompts, conflicting facts, different roles/tenants and revoked documents. Compare task correctness and complete cost against exact/no-cache baselines. Test cache-miss overload and deletion propagation.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T05 · AZ-T13 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new task family, embedding version, similarity configuration, workspace topology or source-permission model.

decisions.title: Assign durable authority across managed and customer state
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerPlatform/data architectDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Unlike a customer-operated gateway with one selected database, the Azure composition has several managed control planes and separate application stores. Desired policy, model deployments, conversations, search permissions and financial events have different authorities and restore semantics. Treating the whole stack as stateless conceals these dependencies.

Options considered

  • Assume managed services eliminate state-ownership decisions.
  • Copy all state into one customer database.
  • Identify the authoritative system and recovery contract for each state class.

Proposed decision

Maintain an authority map: reviewed source for desired configuration; Azure services for deployed resource state; the business system for permissions; the application for user/resource ownership; selected service stores for durable responses/jobs; and an explicit ledger for financial events. Record replication, consistency, retention, deletion and export behavior. Do not claim customer control over undocumented managed-service internals.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery and governance require a composed inventory rather than one database backup. Some state is reconstructed, some exported, and some remains service-bound. The map enables honest portability and explains where an outage or restoration can create stale authority.

Required validation

Trace create/update/delete operations to their authority and replicas. Restore representative state classes, verify current permission and financial state, and demonstrate that inferred caches cannot become authoritative accidentally.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T11 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New service, stored API, retrieval source, budget mechanism, retention requirement or regional replication design.

Evidence informing this proposal[MS02] [MS21] [MS23] [MS44] [MS56]

decisions.title: Define coordination by actual gateway enforcement domain
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerPlatform/SRE ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

APIM operational counters and backend circuit decisions do not form one globally serialized gateway state. Regional and workspace gateways can enforce independently. A Redis deployment from another product’s reference architecture does not automatically become APIM’s coordination mechanism.

Options considered

  • Repeat one organization-wide limit on every gateway and call it global.
  • Allocate limits per actual gateway/region and measure aggregate exposure.
  • Use an external authority for invariants requiring stronger coordination.

Proposed decision

Inventory where each token, request, concurrency and circuit state is evaluated and shared. Define trusted counter keys and avoid inconsistent settings for reused keys. Allocate operational allowances by enforcement domain; use a separately qualified authority when global consistency is required. Keep optional payload caches distinct from rate, authorization and financial state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Regional allowances can strand capacity and require controlled rebalancing. Counter behavior remains useful for traffic governance without being misrepresented as global financial correctness. Additional coordination is justified only by a stated invariant.

Required validation

Run synchronized bursts through every selected gateway and partition. Observe combined admission, counter reset and recovery, including streams and cached results. Record overshoot and allocate headroom based on evidence rather than zero-overshoot assumptions.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T09 · AZ-T10 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New gateway/region/workspace, SKU algorithm change, quota increase or stricter global governance requirement.

decisions.title: Separate strict spending authorization from operational budgets
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerFinOps and platform ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Token controls, observed cost policies and invoice totals are different mechanisms. Streaming estimates, concurrent calls, tool charges and asynchronous jobs make an unconditional hard-cap claim unsafe without a bounded dispatch model. The preview tier’s cost-limit scope does not by itself establish that model.

Options considered

  • Accept soft budgets with documented exposure and alerts.
  • Treat a token/cost counter as an exact financial ceiling.
  • Implement a bounded reservation authority for selected strict workloads.

Proposed decision

Classify each workload as soft-budget or strict-admission. For strict workloads, require a conservative cost bound, serialized reservation or non-overlapping regional allocation, one-use dispatch permission and durable settlement. Fail closed when authority or pricing cannot establish the bound. Retain uncertain execution exposure. Exclude or explicitly constrain unbounded agent/tool/job costs rather than silently weakening the guarantee.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Strict admission adds availability and engineering dependencies and can reject work conservatively. Soft-budget workloads remain simpler but must carry a named exposure acceptance. Unresolved reservations can reduce usable capacity until reconciliation.

Required validation

Race near-limit calls, remove prices, fail the ledger, crash around dispatch and settle duplicate/late events. Demonstrate the claimed maximum exposure for each supported contract; classify unsupported cases honestly.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T09 · AZ-T10 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A stricter budget obligation, new billing dimensions, unbounded tools, regional expansion or observed overspend.

Context

A user call can include multiple provider attempts, cached outcomes, safety/embedding calls and tool actions. Sampled telemetry and final response usage may omit failed or incomplete work. Provider bills can use dimensions and timing that differ from application traces.

Options considered

  • Use sampled observability dashboards for chargeback.
  • Persist only successful final response usage.
  • Maintain durable attributed events and reconcile them against billing evidence.

Proposed decision

Record call, attempt, job and tool identities with owner, alias/model, policy version, reported/estimated usage, price basis and uncertainty. Make settlement idempotent and correction-aware. Reconcile aggregates against actual available billing/export dimensions; do not invent a per-request join where unsupported. Keep unknown amounts visible and assign exception owners. Retain operational metrics separately from financial authority.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Storage, reconciliation and privacy work increase. Chargeback becomes explainable and failures are no longer falsely free. A complete account can lag the user response when jobs or uncertain attempts settle later.

Required validation

Compare synthetic dispatch counts with event and settlement totals, replay events, lose final stream trailers and reconcile a selected billing period. Investigate every unattributed attempt or unexplained variance before approving chargeback.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T10 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New provider/model price units, telemetry schema, settlement delay, credits, tool billing or cost-allocation rules.

decisions.title: Make reviewed desired state authoritative and inspect inheritance
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerAPI platform delivery ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Effective behavior is determined by APIs, policy scopes, backends, identities, model aliases, network settings and service features. Portal changes and generated imports can diverge from reviewed intent. A locally correct policy fragment can omit an inherited mandatory control.

Options considered

  • Let portal state be the operational source of truth.
  • Manage all objects through one undifferentiated automation identity.
  • Use reviewed desired state with delegated ownership and effective-policy checks.

Proposed decision

Store security-sensitive configuration and model contracts in versioned source. Assign explicit ownership to generated, delegated and runtime-managed objects. Promote reviewed changes with a least-privilege delivery identity, then compare deployed effective policies and routes with the release artifact. Emergency changes require an audit record and reconciliation into source before closure. Reject undeclared privilege, backend or operation expansion.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Teams need change discipline and drift handling, but can still delegate bounded administration. The repository alone is insufficient evidence; effective deployed configuration remains a verification target. Generated portal integration is treated as a reviewed artifact, not trusted by origin.

Required validation

Remove inherited controls, alter backend destinations and make a portal-only change in nonproduction. Verify detection and deployment blocking. Recreate the intended service from source and compare its effective behavior.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T14 · AZ-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new policy scope, portal integration, delegated workspace, management API or drift incident.
