decisions.title: Promote coordinated releases with a state-aware rollback envelope
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerPlatform release ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Managed gateway updates, application SDKs, model versions, prompts and policy changes have independent release cycles. A preview API or alias change can alter behavior without a whole-platform version number. Rolling back configuration may be unsafe after state or model lifecycle changes.

Options considered

  • Consume service defaults and latest SDK/model changes automatically.
  • Freeze every dependency indefinitely.
  • Use a qualified release manifest, canary and explicit rollback limits.

Proposed decision

Promote application, policy, identity, model/candidate and customer-state changes as a tested release set. Pin customer artifacts and management API versions where applicable; track managed-service notices and model retirements. Canary representative workloads before broad traffic. Classify reversible configuration changes separately from irreversible jobs, tool effects and state migrations. Never roll back accounting or grants to an obsolete authority state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Release coordination adds work but avoids accidental dependency drift. Managed-service updates cannot always be frozen, so proactive compatibility tests are essential. A retired model can invalidate an old rollback target even when its configuration is retained.

Required validation

Exercise canary rejection, API additive changes, preview toggles and model replacement. Prove that rollback preserves current resource ownership, revocations and spending exposure. Record a replacement strategy where the prior target cannot return.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T14 · AZ-T18 · AZ-T22 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Model retirement, SDK/API change, managed-service update, new preview dependency or state schema migration.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-004 · AZ-ADR-017 · AZ-ADR-020 · AZ-ADR-021

Evidence informing this proposal[MS20] [MS25] [MS45] [MS60]

decisions.title: Componentize only for a demonstrated boundary or scale need
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerPlatform architect and SRE ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

APIM, Foundry, Search, agents, caches and financial services can be deployed as many separate resources. More boxes do not automatically create better isolation, and a workspace label can share runtime capacity or exclude required features. Conversely, privileged tools may need stronger isolation than ordinary inference.

Options considered

  • Deploy one shared stack for all applications and trust labels.
  • Split every concern into a separate service.
  • Separate components when identity, data, failure or scale requirements justify it.

Proposed decision

Start with the minimum composed service that satisfies the approved contract. Isolate high-risk tool execution, sensitive tenant boundaries and strict financial authority when required. Select workspace or separate-gateway deployment only after proving feature compatibility and effective identity isolation. Each added service must have an owner, data classification, failure policy and measurable benefit over the simpler composition.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The reference design avoids both a monolithic trust boundary and unnecessary service proliferation. Some shared infrastructure remains economical; some workloads justify separate resources. Workspaces are not used as a shortcut around unsupported managed identity, caching or tool requirements.

Required validation

Test noisy-neighbor load, credential and policy isolation, dependency failure and per-component recovery. Verify the selected topology supports every required policy rather than relying on an architectural diagram.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T14 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new tenant class, tool risk, capacity bottleneck, feature exclusion or operating-team boundary.

decisions.title: Size gateway, model and dependent services together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE/capacity ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Useful capacity depends on active stream duration, input/output tokens, retries, safety/cache calls, model quotas and state services, not only gateway request throughput. Provisioned model capacity and allowed quota are different operational conditions. Autoscaling one layer can overload another.

Options considered

  • Size by average requests per second alone.
  • Overprovision every dependency without workload evidence.
  • Model the complete concurrency and token distribution and test saturation.

Proposed decision

Use representative input/output distributions, active durations and policy paths to size gateways, model deployments and dependencies. Bound concurrent work and queues before relying on autoscaling. Keep retry and regional allocation effects in the model. Qualify provisioned-throughput economics and actual deployment capacity against the workload rather than treating quota as a performance commitment.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Capacity planning needs realistic traces or synthetic distributions and periodic refresh. Conservative admission may reject bursts, while unconstrained scaling is avoided. Optimizations such as caches or router choices require rerunning the sizing model when their hit rates or output profiles change.

Required validation

Load test matched native and gateway paths through saturation, including slow consumers, long outputs, cold caches and failed dependencies. Measure latency percentiles, active connections, token admission and recovery rather than a single peak throughput number.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T06 · AZ-T09 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Traffic growth, model/output changes, new policies, changed cache hit rate, regional rollout or revised capacity purchase.

decisions.title: Export minimized telemetry through bounded paths
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerObservability and privacy ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Traces help explain latency and model selection but can expose prompts, personal identifiers and tool results. Metrics with unbounded dimensions become costly and difficult to operate. Preview telemetry can change schema, while sampled diagnostics cannot replace durable financial events.

Options considered

  • Log full request/response bodies by default.
  • Disable observability to avoid privacy risk.
  • Use minimized metadata with controlled diagnostic exceptions.

Proposed decision

Default to request/attempt outcome, timing, approved alias/model context and bounded identity attribution without raw content or secrets. Restrict claim export and high-cardinality dimensions. Apply sampling only to diagnostic traces, not mandatory financial or audit evidence. Use bounded buffers and explicit loss behavior for sinks. Permit payload diagnostics only for an approved cohort, purpose and retention period.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some incidents require a deliberate diagnostic escalation instead of immediate access to all prompts. Cost and privacy exposure decrease. Operators must distinguish telemetry loss from model failure and understand which signals remain complete.

Required validation

Inspect exported records for credentials/content, stress sink outages and cardinality, and compare observed attempts with the durable ledger. Test schema changes and identity-claim redaction in the selected preview or established gateway.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T11 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New telemetry sink, claim export, model protocol, incident diagnostic mode or observability schema release.

decisions.title: Keep administrative audit distinct from runtime diagnostics
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSecurity operations ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Changing an alias, backend identity, policy, grant or retention setting can materially change who can access data and where it goes. Runtime traces may be sampled or retained briefly; they cannot establish a complete history of privileged changes.

Options considered

  • Rely on ordinary application traces for all investigations.
  • Retain every diagnostic payload indefinitely.
  • Maintain attributable administrative audit with its own access and retention.

Proposed decision

Collect privileged configuration, role, credential-reference, model/candidate and network changes into an independently protected audit destination. Associate each with actor, approval/release record, affected resource and effective time. Keep audit retention separate from raw inference diagnostics and define which managed-service events are available. Record gaps explicitly and add customer delivery audit where service logs are insufficient.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Audit storage and access governance add an operating responsibility. The service becomes easier to explain after a policy incident without retaining unnecessary prompt content. Unknown propagation times still require runtime evidence alongside the change record.

Required validation

Make representative allowed and denied administrative changes, inspect attribution and retention, and demonstrate who can alter or delete audit evidence. Correlate a policy change with its effective runtime behavior.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New control plane, delegated role, compliance obligation, retention policy or identified audit gap.

decisions.title: Coordinate configuration and customer-store migrations
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerDelivery and data ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The customer does not run schema migrations for Microsoft’s private service databases, but still changes API definitions, policies, state/ledger schemas, index formats and agent artifacts. Concurrent or incompatible migrations can lose ownership, duplicate spending or serve stale permission projections.

Options considered

  • Treat managed services as eliminating all migration work.
  • Let every application replica apply changes independently.
  • Use one controlled migration authority per customer-owned state transition.

Proposed decision

Separate managed-service evolution from customer-owned migration. Apply reviewed, idempotent configuration and schema changes through one coordinated release job or equivalent authority. Use expand/contract patterns where appropriate, preserve current ownership and revocations, and make index rebuilds version-aware. Record rollback compatibility before promotion; provider-owned resource IDs are not rewritten to pretend portability.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Migration coordination can slow deployment but prevents conflicting writers. Some transitions require a temporary compatibility window, reindex or explicit cutover. Restoring a historical ledger or permission snapshot is not a valid generic rollback.

Required validation

Replay the migration, interrupt it mid-transition, test mixed application versions and restore into clean infrastructure. Verify event idempotency, current grants, resource ownership and vector/permission consistency.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T11 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T22 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Customer schema/index change, API contract migration, gateway generation switch or agent state redesign.

decisions.title: Separate liveness, policy readiness and safe draining
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE/runtime ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

An answering gateway may still lack valid backend authority, current policy, model capacity or required state dependencies. A successful health probe does not establish a working application contract. During shutdown or route cutover, streams and durable submissions may remain active.

Options considered

  • Use one HTTP health check as proof of availability.
  • Probe every real dependency on every liveness check.
  • Define separate process, policy-readiness and functional-service signals.

Proposed decision

Distinguish runtime reachability, configuration/policy readiness and end-to-end functional health. Use lightweight liveness checks, bounded readiness evidence and controlled synthetic canaries. Drain or stop new admission before cutover where the selected runtime permits it; preserve active stream/job outcomes and accounting. Do not restart healthy processes in a loop because an external provider is degraded.

Consequences and tradeoffs

decisions.title: Prove primary-region availability before regional expansion
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE and platform architectDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Additional regions can reduce some outages while multiplying policy, identity, state and financial consistency problems. Gateway replication alone does not recreate model capacity or application data. The required availability must be measured for the full composed service.

Options considered

  • Deploy many regions immediately and trust automatic routing.
  • Use one untested instance indefinitely.
  • Establish a qualified primary deployment and then add justified recovery regions.

Proposed decision

Begin with a supported primary topology meeting the workload’s availability needs, using zone or other supported redundancy where appropriate. Prove dependency failure and restoration before adding regions. For each secondary, validate policy, model capacity, data processing, state ownership and financial authority. Do not assume APIM regional gateway deployment implies Foundry/application state failover.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The initial rollout remains simpler and recovery gaps become visible early. Some regional resilience work is deferred until justified. Where a business requirement demands multiple regions immediately, all dependent gates must still pass before production.

Required validation

Fail primary components and selected dependencies, measure functional recovery and verify denied paths remain denied. For a secondary, demonstrate eligible model capacity and owner-aware state handling before routing users there.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T04 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T21 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Documented availability requirement, geographic user need, residency constraint or evidence of unacceptable primary-region risk.

decisions.title: Allocate quotas and spend by regional enforcement domain
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaData and financeSuggested ownerFinOps and SRE ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Gateway counters are not aggregated automatically across an entire APIM instance, and backend quota/capacity also has its own scope. A failover can double available allowance if the same budget is independently configured in both regions. A global coordinator can instead become a continuity dependency.

Options considered

  • Duplicate the full allowance at every gateway.
  • Require one strongly coordinated global authority for all traffic.
  • Use explicit non-overlapping regional allocations with controlled transfers, or a qualified shared authority.

Proposed decision

Document the enforcement domain for operational token/request limits and financial admission. Partition strict allowances so regional totals cannot exceed the approved global authority, or use a shared reservation service with tested availability. Rebalance through an auditable transfer that never spends the same allowance twice. Define failover behavior for exhausted or unreachable allocations before an incident.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Capacity or budget may be temporarily stranded in a healthy region. Rebalancing adds operational work, but prevents hidden exposure multiplication. Soft operational quotas can use a different allocation model from strict spending authority if the distinction is explicit.

Required validation

Run simultaneous cross-region load, network partitions, failover and repeated transfer requests. Reconcile reservations and settlements after recovery and prove no duplicated global allowance or unauthorized destination.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T09 · AZ-T10 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New region/gateway, increased allowance, allocation-policy change or a continuity requirement incompatible with the current authority model.

decisions.title: Recover configuration, current authority and durable state together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and reliabilitySuggested ownerSRE/data recovery ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A gateway-only restore can leave model deployments, DNS, secrets, user resource mappings, Search permissions and spend authority inconsistent. Old backups can revive revoked grants or lower financial counters. Some managed state is exportable, some reconstructible and some service-bound.

Options considered

  • Restore only gateway configuration.
  • Assume all managed services recover coherently without customer action.
  • Maintain and rehearse a composed recovery manifest with state-specific RTO/RPO.

Proposed decision

Create a recovery inventory covering desired state, deployed configuration, identities/current revocations, secrets/encryption references, application ownership, indexes, jobs and financial exposure. Define state-specific recovery objectives and irrecoverable gaps. Reapply current deny state and settle or retain uncertain work before reopening admission. Validate actual backup/API applicability for the selected SKU rather than assuming one backup captures the service.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery exercises need several teams and controlled test environments. Some state may require reconstruction or a user-visible restart instead of transparent failover. The design gains an honest recovery contract instead of an unsupported zero-loss claim.

Required validation

Restore into clean infrastructure using retained artifacts and keys, then run authorization, ownership, accounting and application canaries. Include offline gateway startup if self-hosting is selected and verify that restored permissions do not exceed current authority.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T21 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New durable service, encryption change, RTO/RPO requirement, region topology or failed recovery drill.

decisions.title: Verify customer artifacts and track managed-service lifecycle
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerSupply-chain and platform ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A managed model/gateway reduces some host operation but does not remove customer SDKs, agent containers, policy artifacts or IaC from the supply chain. Model and service updates can introduce behavioral changes independently of those artifacts. An old pinned dependency can become unsupported or vulnerable.

Options considered

  • Use latest tags and unconstrained dependencies for convenience.
  • Freeze all versions without an update process.
  • Pin verified customer artifacts and actively qualify service/model changes.

Proposed decision

Use tested dependency lockfiles, signed or otherwise verified artifacts where available, immutable container digests for customer runtimes, and restricted build identities. Track service updates, API previews and model retirement as release inputs. Maintain an active patch and canary process rather than treating pinning as permanent safety. Record which components are customer-inspected and which remain managed-service contracts.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Build and release work persists even in a mostly managed stack. Faster updates may be delayed for qualification, but urgent security fixes need a preplanned path. The report’s source review is not represented as an audit of Microsoft’s internal supply chain.

Required validation

Reproduce builds, inspect provenance and dependency inventories, simulate a revoked artifact and apply a patch through the canary process. Verify rollback viability against current model lifecycle.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T18 · AZ-T22 · AZ-T23 · AZ-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Security advisory, dependency/runtime update, managed-service change, preview transition or model retirement.

decisions.title: Treat policy editors, plugins and agent code as privileged execution
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerPlatform security ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

APIM policy authors can direct traffic, invoke services and exercise assigned managed identities. Hosted agents and external integrations can run code or call tools with similarly important authority. Delegating policy editing is therefore more than allowing someone to adjust harmless request formatting.

Options considered

  • Permit broad policy/agent extension access for developer flexibility.
  • Forbid all customization.
  • Provide reviewed extension points with narrow authority and isolated execution.

Proposed decision

Treat policies, expressions, fragments, backend changes and agent artifacts as privileged code. Restrict writers, require review and limit the identities/destinations they can exercise. Keep powerful managed-identity policies out of broad global scopes unless every descendant is intended to share that authority. Isolate risky custom execution and external checks; set time, payload and network limits. Do not expose tokens in variables/logs available to untrusted extensions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Developer extension workflows need approvals or a constrained sandbox. Some convenient global policies must be duplicated at narrower scopes to preserve security. The architecture remains extensible without making every policy editor a de facto backend administrator.

Required validation

Attempt token exfiltration and unintended destination routing in a controlled test, inspect policy-writer grants and verify code/artifact provenance. Confirm inherited policies cannot leak privileged context to delegated workspaces.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T14 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New extension/plugin, delegated policy writer, global identity policy, hosted agent or external integration.

decisions.title: Default-deny tools and authorize business actions independently
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerTool platform and business-service ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

MCP discovery, model-generated tool calls and A2A agent communication do not establish permission to act on business objects. Gateway authentication can hide broad backend authority, and retries can repeat side effects. Remote tool catalogs and agent cards can change after onboarding.

Options considered

  • Allow all tools available to a configured server.
  • Rely solely on model instructions or tool schema descriptions.
  • Require explicit tool grants, constrained backend identity and business transaction authorization.

Proposed decision

Default-deny tool servers, operations and resource scopes. Authenticate discovery and invocation separately, bind sessions/tasks to owners, and validate arguments plus object-level permissions at the business service. Require explicit approval for selected consequential actions, bound to the actual arguments and authority. Use transaction idempotency and reconcile ambiguous outcomes instead of replaying blindly. Review remote catalog/card changes before expanding access.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Agent workflows gain more explicit permission and approval steps. Some broad third-party connectors are unsuitable without a constraining adapter. Gateway tool governance complements rather than replaces business authorization and transaction control.

Required validation

Attempt hidden operations, cross-owner objects, stolen sessions, altered approved arguments and duplicate actions after a timeout. Verify backend bypass prevention, approval binding and task cancellation behavior.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T08 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New tool/server, external agent, side-effecting operation, connector scope or remote schema/card change.

decisions.title: Preserve owner and origin for stateful API resources
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerApplication state ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Responses, conversations, files and agent sessions are durable resources whose IDs can be reused in later calls. Authentication to a gateway does not prove ownership of an arbitrary ID. A different provider or deployment may not understand the resource even when the API field name matches.

Options considered

  • Proxy state identifiers without application ownership checks.
  • Treat IDs as portable and retry them against any compatible schema.
  • Maintain owner/origin mapping and authorize each lifecycle operation.

Proposed decision

Bind every stateful resource to a verified owner, originating service/deployment, policy and retention contract. Authorize read, continue, list, cancel and delete independently. Route only to compatible origin services; any reconstruction or migration is explicit and privacy-reviewed. Preserve current authorization on session continuation and include derived artifacts and logs in deletion inventory.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The application needs an ownership mapping and cannot promise transparent cross-provider state portability. Some failover scenarios require a new session or controlled reconstruction. Resource cleanup becomes an auditable lifecycle rather than a best-effort client request.

Required validation

Use guessed/leaked IDs across users, replay IDs after revocation and attempt continuation through another deployment. Test deletion, restore and session migration without restoring unauthorized access.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T03 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New Responses/agent feature, file store, retention requirement, migration target or stateful fallback path.

decisions.title: Govern batch, background and media work separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerApplication and FinOps ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Asynchronous and media workloads have different payload sizes, completion times, retention and cost units from ordinary chat. Submission acceptance can precede billable execution by a long interval. A client timeout can create ambiguity about whether a durable job was created.

Options considered

  • Apply the ordinary chat timeout, limits and accounting unchanged.
  • Block all noninteractive workloads.
  • Create distinct admission, ownership and settlement contracts for each family.

Proposed decision

Qualify batch, background Responses and media endpoints independently. Bound input/output exposure, retain owner and origin, persist submission intent and provider IDs, and use supported idempotency or reconciliation for ambiguous outcomes. Authorize polling, output access, cancellation and deletion. Set explicit retention and delayed-settlement rules; do not release all exposure merely because the submitter disconnected.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Long-running workloads require durable coordination and cleanup. Some jobs cannot support an immediate hard cancellation or precise upfront cost; those limitations must be accepted or excluded. The gateway can mediate submission without becoming the authoritative job scheduler.

Required validation

Test oversized submissions, duplicate attempts, partial completion, expired credentials, delayed usage, cancellation limits and restart recovery. Confirm no cross-owner output access and no hidden provider jobs after an ambiguous request.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T10 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T12 · AZ-T16 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New endpoint family, media modality, job size, provider capacity mode or retention/budget requirement.

decisions.title: Keep quality, retrieval and agent evaluation with product owners
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAgent and applicationSuggested ownerProduct and model evaluation ownersDrafted6 October 2026

Context

A successful API call, safe content classification or lower average cost does not prove that an application works. Router changes, semantic reuse, retrieval permissions, prompts and tools can affect business outcomes while the interface remains valid. Evaluation data itself can contain sensitive information.

Options considered

  • Use gateway success rate as the main product-quality measure.
  • Delegate all model selection to provider defaults.
  • Maintain task-specific evaluation and release gates owned by the product.

Proposed decision

Version representative task datasets and acceptance criteria for correctness, structured output, tools, retrieval/citations, safety and cost. Compare fixed and routed models and cache modes on the same tasks. Test permission-sensitive and failure cases. Keep product owners accountable for promotion; platform teams provide reproducible execution and evidence. Review evaluator services and datasets as data recipients with retention rules.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Quality work remains an application responsibility even with managed evaluation tooling. Some model/caching optimizations will be rejected despite speed or price benefits. Data collection and evaluation require privacy controls and maintenance as user tasks evolve.

Required validation

Run regression and adversarial suites before model, prompt, router, retrieval or tool changes. Track task-adjusted quality and complete cost, and demonstrate that the suite catches a deliberately degraded or unauthorized result.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T05 · AZ-T08 · AZ-T13 · AZ-T15 · AZ-T17 · AZ-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New task population, model/candidate/prompt change, retrieval rebuild, tool behavior change or observed quality drift.

decisions.title: Contract for exact support, capacity, privacy and preview exposure
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerProcurement and platform ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

The service name alone does not establish an SLA, region availability, support scope, price, model entitlement or processing agreement. The dedicated gateway remains preview with an evolving commercial contract, while established APIM tiers and Foundry deployments have their own terms. Managed does not mean cost-free or risk-free.

Options considered

  • Assume all Azure-branded components share production commitments.
  • Reject every preview regardless of workload.
  • Contract and approve risk at the exact composition and workload scope.

Proposed decision

Confirm the selected SKU/API/region/model availability, quotas versus deployable capacity, support escalation, pricing dimensions, data terms and customer export rights. Record preview-dependent features and restrict them to explicitly approved workload risk. Do not promise a composed service SLA stronger than the validated dependencies support. Obtain actual commercial inputs before final procurement rather than filling unknown prices with zero.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The shortlist may exclude an otherwise attractive feature or require a different topology. Noncritical preview pilots remain possible with clear owners and rollback. Procurement must review external tools/providers and auxiliary services, not just APIM and model tokens.

Required validation

Retain written terms, capacity evidence, service-support boundaries and a cost model for the actual workload. Confirm how an incident crosses gateway, model, identity and tool support teams and demonstrate the approved exit path.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T16 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T21 · AZ-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

GA transition, commercial change, new region/provider/tool, revised SLA requirement or support incident.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-001 · AZ-ADR-002 · AZ-ADR-010 · AZ-ADR-024 · AZ-ADR-029 · AZ-ADR-031 · AZ-ADR-032

decisions.title: Qualify performance with representative complete executions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerSRE and product ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Gateway microbenchmarks omit model duration, streaming, safety checks, retrieval, tool execution and state. Native and mediated paths can differ in retries, caching and usage. A high throughput number is not evidence that the intended user experience or governance remains correct under load.

Options considered

  • Adopt published headline benchmarks as the capacity plan.
  • Measure a minimal happy-path request only.
  • Use matched native/gateway workloads and failure-aware service objectives.

Proposed decision

Define product SLOs and an incremental gateway-overhead budget before tests. Measure representative prompt/output distributions, concurrency, policy paths, streams and agent jobs against a native baseline. Include tail latency, incomplete outcomes, dispatch multiplication, quality, cost and policy correctness. Separate cold/cache-hit and normal/failure regimes. Do not claim a comparative performance win without controlled evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Qualification requires realistic fixtures and enough observability to attribute time by layer. A faster configuration may fail quality or privacy gates and therefore be unsuitable. Results are valid only for the tested tuple and workload envelope.

Required validation

Run reproducible staged load and soak tests, dependency failures and recovery. Retain latency distributions, resource saturation, model quality, event completeness and complete cost. Re-run when the workload or routing/caching policy changes materially.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T05 · AZ-T06 · AZ-T07 · AZ-T09 · AZ-T20 · AZ-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Traffic mix or volume change, new model/gateway/policy, capacity purchase, SLO breach or proposed optimization.

DependenciesAZ-ADR-011 · AZ-ADR-012 · AZ-ADR-013 · AZ-ADR-020 · AZ-ADR-024 · AZ-ADR-025 · AZ-ADR-029 · AZ-ADR-037 · AZ-ADR-038

decisions.title: Preserve an exit path and review decisions on material change
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaCommercial and lifecycleSuggested ownerArchitecture governance ownerDrafted6 October 2026

Context

Foundry state, Azure identity/policy configuration, model routing and agent integrations can make a platform valuable and also create migration cost. An architecture decision is not permanently correct when model availability, service maturity, privacy terms or organizational priorities change.

Options considered

  • Accept provider-specific coupling without documenting it.
  • Restrict the platform to a lowest-common-denominator API.
  • Use deliberate native capabilities with an explicit portability and review plan.

Proposed decision

Maintain organization-owned contracts, exportable customer ownership/financial data, provider-origin mappings and tested deployment artifacts. Identify nonportable state and the procedure to reconstruct, archive or abandon it. Keep at least one evaluated alternative for critical capabilities without assuming zero-effort substitution. Review each ADR when its trigger occurs and record acceptance, exceptions and supersession with a named owner.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some platform-specific capabilities remain appropriate, but their exit cost is visible. A future move to Bedrock or another gateway still needs model-quality and state qualification. Retaining the native baseline and complete decision evidence reduces rediscovery during migration.

Required validation

Rebuild a representative application path against an alternative or clean target using retained contracts and safe fixtures. Export state/ledger data, verify deletion obligations and identify irrecoverable or costly gaps before a crisis.

Acceptance gates: AZ-T01 · AZ-T11 · AZ-T18 · AZ-T19 · AZ-T23 · AZ-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Material service/price/support change, new privacy obligation, model retirement, platform strategy change or repeated acceptance-gate failure.

decisions.title: Add a shared gateway only for explicit enterprise requirements
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerPlatform architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The reference organization has multiple applications but no supplied proof that all need an additional mediation layer. The choice must distinguish a managed model service from an API governance service. Adding a gateway creates another privileged dependency, operating contract and source of failures.

Options considered

  • Use native model APIs with application-owned controls.
  • Standardize on managed Apigee for shared API governance.
  • Adopt an AI-native gateway or combine narrowly separated services.

Proposed decision

Establish one native Google model-platform contract as the control group. Add managed Apigee only when product access, identity enforcement, policy administration or API/tool governance closes a documented requirement. Keep application authorization, task quality and any strict financial service with named owners. Approve a second gateway only with a responsibility map showing why one layer cannot meet the requirement. Do not make adoption of retrieval, agents or memory implicit in the model-access decision.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This gives a measurable baseline and avoids duplicating controls, but may produce more than one approved integration pattern. The platform must publish where native access remains allowed and prevent an unmanaged route from bypassing mandatory shared controls.

Required validation

Compare native and proxied calls on identical fixtures, security requirements and operating costs. Demonstrate the additional controls, then exercise bypass paths. Architecture approval requires a documented benefit and an accountable service owner rather than a feature-count score.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T02, GC-T06, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when the number of teams, provider requirements, existing API investment or policy obligations changes.

Dependencies Reference assumptions and an approved business requirement.

Evidence informing this proposal [GP01] [GP03] [GP53]

decisions.title: Qualify managed, hybrid, Extension Processor and Agent Gateway separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerEnterprise architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The Google offerings expose different runtime and policy boundaries. Treating them as interchangeable versions of one gateway can approve a topology that lacks a mandatory control. Hybrid runtime placement also introduces customer persistence and cluster responsibilities.

Options considered

  • Use the managed Apigee proxy path.
  • Use supported hybrid runtime for a justified placement requirement.
  • Use Extension Processor or native Agent Gateway for a separately defined enforcement role.

Proposed decision

Make managed Apigee the reference gateway candidate. Require a separate architecture manifest and gate results for hybrid, Extension Processor and Agent Gateway. Do not infer policy parity or a fully self-hosted management plane. A required unsupported policy must be replaced by an explicitly owned equivalent control or the topology must be rejected. Record the hybrid runtime/platform version and all external data dependencies before approving runtime placement.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Separate qualification increases initial analysis but prevents hidden differences from surfacing during incidents. Optional native agent governance can coexist without forcing model/API traffic into its identity model. Product-specific operational runbooks remain necessary.

Required validation

Build a policy-by-topology matrix with exact support references and actual tests. Verify unsupported combinations fail deployment or remain out of scope. Demonstrate control-plane and datastore outage behavior for the selected design.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T05, GC-T20, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after policy-support changes, runtime lifecycle changes or a new placement/perimeter requirement.

Dependencies GC-ADR-001

decisions.title: Publish a bounded, versioned client contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerApplication platform leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A provider-neutral endpoint name can hide differences in parameters, tool behavior, errors, usage and stateful resources. Model or gateway upgrades can preserve transport compatibility while breaking a business task. Testing one successful text call cannot qualify an entire API family.

Options considered

  • Expose the full upstream API without organizational constraints.
  • Publish a narrow versioned application contract with explicit supported features.
  • Maintain independent native and compatibility contracts for specialized clients.

Proposed decision

Publish a bounded initial contract for approved text generation and streaming, adding tools or structured output only when required and tested. Specify required/forbidden fields, error classes, payload limits, terminal outcomes and ownership of resource IDs. Keep native and OpenAI-compatible paths separately qualified. Reject unsupported fields or document deliberate transformations; never silently discard meaning-changing options. Expand the contract through versioned release review.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The constrained surface reduces immediate convenience for advanced clients but makes replacement and support more realistic. Protocol adapters become maintained components with explicit ownership rather than informal policy snippets.

Required validation

Run schema and golden-task tests against every model/API candidate, including failures, empty candidates and safety outcomes. Compare client libraries and native REST. Demonstrate that a malformed or unsupported request fails before dispatch.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T06, GC-T11, GC-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when a new modality, tool feature, stateful endpoint or required client cannot fit the approved contract.

Dependencies GC-ADR-001, GC-ADR-002

Evidence informing this proposal [GP25] [GP26] [GP61]

decisions.title: Use reviewed model aliases with concrete capability manifests
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerModel platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Applications need stable names, but an alias can conceal changes in quality, geography, pricing and context capacity. A route configuration is therefore also a product and privacy decision. Embedding model changes have a different migration impact from chat model changes.

Options considered

  • Expose provider model identifiers directly to all clients.
  • Use mutable aliases without a versioned candidate record.
  • Use organization-owned aliases mapped to reviewed concrete contracts.

Proposed decision

Use stable application-facing aliases with a reviewed manifest of concrete model/version, publisher, API, location, credentials, capacity mode and capability limits. Record actual target resolution on every attempt. Version embedding/index contracts separately. Alias changes require relevant quality, security and lifecycle checks; they may not silently expand processing geography or accept incompatible stateful IDs. Keep a rollback or replacement candidate before an upstream retirement date.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The application gains stable integration while platform releases must manage semantic change explicitly. Multiple aliases may be needed for different quality, locality and cost classes. This is intentional clarity, not needless duplication.

Required validation

Exercise every eligible candidate with maximum-context, tool/schema and quality fixtures. Force fallback, inspect actual destinations and verify alias-retargeted permissions. Confirm lifecycle dates and ownership before promotion.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T06, GC-T08, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit on model retirement, pricing/capability changes or newly required processing boundaries.

decisions.title: Issue scoped workload credentials and manage revocation as a service
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerIdentity platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A gateway application credential identifies an integration but can be shared across many users and environments. Broad shared credentials weaken attribution and containment. Cached or distributed authorization introduces a measurable revocation interval.

Options considered

  • Share one credential across applications.
  • Issue separate application/environment credentials with governed enrollment.
  • Use workload federation or verified JWTs where the selected integration supports them.

Proposed decision

Assign each production application and environment a distinct approved credential or workload identity. Bind it to the minimum API products, operations and model aliases. Separate administration credentials from runtime access and avoid granting an application the role of its human creator. Define expiry, rotation, revocation and containment owners. Publish the maximum accepted revocation lag and test it on all active runtime paths, including long-lived tool sessions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More identities require enrollment automation and lifecycle inventory, but reduce the blast radius of compromise and clarify spend ownership. Revocation cannot be represented as instantaneous unless the deployed architecture demonstrates that behavior.

Required validation

Test cross-application access, key sharing detection, rotation during load and revocation under partial management connectivity. Verify historical attribution remains understandable after a credential is replaced.

Acceptance gates: GC-T02, GC-T03, GC-T04, GC-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when client identity capabilities, application ownership or incident-containment requirements change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-001, GC-ADR-002

Evidence informing this proposal [GP44] [GP53] [GP56]

decisions.title: Derive authority from verified claims, not request metadata
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerIdentity and application securityDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A validly signed token can still be intended for another service. Client-supplied tenant identifiers, cost centers, roles and tool context are not proof of authority. Agent-native identities and Apigee app identities also need an explicit relationship.

Options considered

  • Trust supplied tenant and user metadata after transport authentication.
  • Validate tokens and enforce an explicit claim-to-policy mapping.
  • Delegate selected decisions to an external authorization service with a defined failure contract.

Proposed decision

Validate issuer, audience, allowed algorithm, expiry and required claims at the intended boundary. Resolve an immutable application/tenant mapping before quota, cache, route or tool selection. Strip or reject client overrides of privileged variables. Separate actor identity from any delegated end-user subject, with an explicit permitted delegation chain. For native agents, map the actual workload identity and target grant rather than inferring equivalence to an Apigee app.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This requires coordinated identity and application schemas and may reject older clients that relied on unverified metadata. In exchange, all downstream control keys derive from the same trusted context. Missing authoritative context is a denial, not a default broad tenant.

Required validation

Use wrong-audience, wrong-issuer, expired, tampered and ambiguous-claim tokens. Attempt privilege injection in headers/body. Verify key, JWT and agent identity paths produce only their intended permissions.

Acceptance gates: GC-T02, GC-T03, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when an issuer, audience, federation rule or delegation model changes.

Dependencies GC-ADR-005

decisions.title: Enforce tenant and object isolation independently of API access
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerApplication security architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Permission to call an assistant or API product does not authorize every document, file, context cache, job or business transaction reachable behind it. A shared gateway principal may have wider backend access than an individual user.

Options considered

  • Rely on gateway/API-product permission alone.
  • Add tenant/resource ownership checks in the application domain.
  • Use separate projects or stacks for high-assurance tenants in addition to logical controls.

Proposed decision

Require authenticated owner checks for retrieval, cached answers, provider resource IDs, tool sessions, jobs and business objects. Derive tenant from verified context and validate it before privileged backend access. Use separate projects or deployments where contractual or risk boundaries demand stronger isolation; do not assume a database label or resource name creates that boundary. Keep backend authorization authoritative for side-effecting actions even after gateway approval.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This adds domain-specific checks outside gateway configuration, but avoids confusing transport access with data entitlement. Partitioned infrastructure raises cost and deployment effort; it should be reserved for requirements that logical controls cannot satisfy.

Required validation

Use known foreign resource IDs, overlapping semantic prompts, shared folders and cross-tenant tool arguments. Change ACLs during sessions and prove denied retrieval and mutation. Confirm error responses do not leak another tenant’s metadata.

Acceptance gates: GC-T02, GC-T14, GC-T15, GC-T16, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when introducing shared indexes/caches, external customers or stricter isolation obligations.

Dependencies GC-ADR-005, GC-ADR-006

decisions.title: Separate application ingress from administrative authority
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerNetwork and platform securityDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The service has distinct application, policy publication, identity, runtime and diagnostic surfaces. A convenient shared endpoint or broad operator credential can expose configuration changes to clients or hide who changed a critical control.

Options considered

  • Publish all interfaces through one generally reachable boundary.
  • Separate administrative access with narrow identities and network controls.
  • Use stronger project/environment separation for sensitive administration.

Proposed decision

Expose only approved application APIs on caller-facing listeners. Restrict administration, policy publication, deployment, debugging and credential lifecycle to named roles and approved paths. Use separate production/nonproduction authority and require independent review for security-sensitive changes. Network controls supplement identity; they do not replace it. Document a break-glass path with time-bounded access, audit and mandatory reconciliation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Operational convenience is reduced, and emergency access requires deliberate preparation. This prevents application credentials from becoming administration shortcuts and makes incident changes attributable. A compromised policy publisher remains high impact and must be treated accordingly.

Required validation

Probe administrative and debug paths from application networks and identities. Exercise approved break-glass access and verify expiry and audit. Confirm deployment principals cannot read unrelated application data by default.

Acceptance gates: GC-T02, GC-T05, GC-T18, GC-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after network redesign, organizational role changes or an incident involving policy or credential misuse.

Dependencies GC-ADR-002, GC-ADR-005, GC-ADR-006

decisions.title: Separate provider credentials, key custody and workload authority
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerCloud security and key-management ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Encryption, identity federation and backend authorization solve different problems. Removing a long-lived API key does not prevent a broad managed identity from accessing unauthorized resources, and a backup without key custody can be unrecoverable.

Options considered

  • Use broadly shared static service credentials.
  • Use scoped workload/service identity with explicit target bindings.
  • Use managed secrets only where a selected upstream requires them, with separate encryption and recovery custody.

Proposed decision

Prefer scoped workload or supported service identity for Google backends. Bind each route to an approved principal, audience and destination; never choose them from untrusted request fields. Where secrets remain necessary, store and rotate them separately from policy code. Assign encryption-key and recovery custody explicitly for customer-owned state and backups. Test token refresh, secret rotation and key loss as separate failure modes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Identity and key inventories become part of release management. Fewer distributed long-lived secrets improve rotation, but policy authors can still misuse backend authority unless publication and egress are constrained.

Required validation

Attempt forbidden backend actions under each principal, redirect credentials, rotate while serving traffic and restore with controlled key access. Inspect logs and error handling for secret/token disclosure.

Acceptance gates: GC-T03, GC-T05, GC-T19, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit on provider onboarding, role expansion, key rotation or a change in backup encryption ownership.

Dependencies GC-ADR-005, GC-ADR-006, GC-ADR-008

Evidence informing this proposal [GP20] [GP56] [GP48]

decisions.title: Approve every processing destination and auxiliary egress path
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerData protection and network architectureDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A model call can trigger safety, embedding, retrieval, logging and tool processing. Runtime placement and private addressing do not establish the location or retention contract of all these services. Fallback can silently widen the path.

Options considered

  • Allow any technically reachable endpoint.
  • Approve a model endpoint but leave auxiliaries implicit.
  • Maintain a complete content-bearing data-flow and destination policy.

Proposed decision

Approve the complete route, including model, Model Armor, embeddings, vector retrieval, telemetry, identity and tools. Record service-specific location, retention, key and perimeter requirements. Prevent caller-controlled URLs and approve fallback destinations against the same envelope. Distinguish at-rest residency from processing location and global routing. Qualify peered/non-peered networking and Agent Gateway resource prerequisites separately; a private IP is not proof of all required controls.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This can constrain availability and model choice, and requires coordination across teams owning auxiliary services. It makes privacy exceptions visible rather than allowing an emergency fallback or cache feature to change the data boundary silently.

Required validation

Trace allowed and denied paths under normal, fallback and outage conditions. Verify DNS, token audience, network routes and service-specific controls. Review all new targets before deploying alias or policy changes.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T08, GC-T15, GC-T22, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit whenever a target, region, retention setting, network topology or auxiliary service changes.

Dependencies GC-ADR-002, GC-ADR-004, GC-ADR-006, GC-ADR-009

decisions.title: Constrain routing to equivalent and authorized candidates
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerModel routing ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Routing improves availability only when the destination still satisfies the caller’s authorization, application capability, geography and financial policy. A generic healthy target or low-cost model is not necessarily an eligible replacement.

Options considered

  • Route to any available model/provider.
  • Use a fixed target without fallback.
  • Use reviewed candidates with explicit eligibility and failure rules.

Proposed decision

Start with a small fixed or weighted approved candidate set. Evaluate eligibility before every attempt using verified caller scope, contract capabilities, state ownership, location and remaining admission authority. Keep adaptive optimization optional until a simple baseline is demonstrated. Record the concrete target and reason. Never treat a denied primary or exhausted tenant allowance as justification to bypass policy on a fallback route.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Availability may be lower than unrestricted failover, but successful responses retain a meaningful application and governance contract. Maintaining equivalence requires ongoing quality testing and lifecycle review of every candidate.

Required validation

Force failures, reduced quota and incompatible contexts; prove prohibited candidates are never chosen. Test route updates under load and confirm all attempts remain explainable with the effective policy revision.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T06, GC-T08, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adding providers, capacity classes, task-specific routing or new residency constraints.

decisions.title: Assign one retry owner and one bounded execution deadline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerReliability leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Clients, SDKs, proxies, load balancers and job workers can all retry. Independently reasonable policies can multiply upstream calls and exceed deadlines or spending assumptions. A timeout after dispatch does not establish that work stopped.

Options considered

  • Allow retries independently at every layer.
  • Disable all recovery attempts.
  • Assign one upstream retry owner with classification, attempt and deadline budgets.

Proposed decision

Assign a single owner for inference retry and maintain one end-to-end deadline propagated into remaining stage budgets. Disable or explicitly account for lower-layer retries. Separate pre-dispatch failure, uncertain execution, partial output and completed work. Permit only eligible fallback attempts, each with identity and financial attribution. Side-effecting tools and job submission need separate business idempotency; a correlation identifier alone is not deduplication.

Consequences and tradeoffs

decisions.title: Make streaming completion and cancellation explicit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerClient protocol ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Streaming exposes partial results before final status and usage are known. Event-processing placement and limits can alter which policies execute. Client disconnection, upstream completion and cancellation acknowledgment are different outcomes.

Options considered

  • Treat HTTP success as request completion.
  • Buffer every response and disable interactivity.
  • Publish explicit streaming and terminal-state semantics with selective buffering.

Proposed decision

Define one effective EventFlow plan and a client contract for partial text, tool assembly, safety events, final usage and incomplete termination. Preserve UTF-8 and protocol event boundaries. Do not retry transparently after any user-visible output or executed action. On disconnect, release local resources, attempt supported cancellation and retain uncertain upstream exposure. Choose full buffering only for workloads whose preventive policy requires it and whose latency budget permits it.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The client and gateway must coordinate richer failure states. Strict preventive inspection may reduce responsiveness. Preserving uncertainty can delay financial settlement, but avoids classifying truncated answers and unknown cost as successful free work.

Required validation

Test large and fragmented events, malformed trailers, missing usage and cancellation at multiple phases. Verify the effective event chain and latency/resource behavior during long-lived streams.

Acceptance gates: GC-T06, GC-T11, GC-T12, GC-T13. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when a new streaming protocol, safety mechanism or tool event type is introduced.

Dependencies GC-ADR-003, GC-ADR-012

decisions.title: Declare safety inspection coverage and fail behavior per route
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerApplication security leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Configuring a sanitation policy is not evidence that every relevant field was inspected. Extraction, partial results, remote timeouts and streamed delivery can leave gaps. Content checks cannot substitute for authorization or transactional correctness.

Options considered

  • Use a best-effort global sanitizer with implicit defaults.
  • Require full preventive inspection for every workload.
  • Define workload-specific inspected fields, enforcement timing and failure rules.

Proposed decision

Publish an inspection map for prompts, model output, tool arguments/results and selected metadata. Explicitly configure missing-variable behavior and handle clean, matched, partial, failed and uninspected states. High-assurance routes deny ambiguous or failed checks; any best-effort exception requires a named risk owner and visible evidence. Distinguish preventive checks from detection after delivery. Preserve independent object authorization and tool approval even when all content filters pass.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The policy becomes testable but requires fixtures for every endpoint and transformation. Remote safety services add latency, cost and data paths. Some stream contracts may need buffering or narrower supported payloads to meet preventive guarantees.

Required validation

Inject markers into mixed text/tools and nested fields, force extraction failures and service errors, and observe what reached the client. Verify failure decisions and auxiliary processing approval, not just HTTP status.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T11, GC-T13, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit on model/protocol changes, new tool structures or safety-service behavior changes.

Dependencies GC-ADR-003, GC-ADR-007, GC-ADR-010, GC-ADR-013

decisions.title: Disable exact response caching until eligibility and isolation are proven
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerApplication data ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Reusing a previous answer can reduce inference work but also return stale, unauthorized or personalized content. Authorization state and policy can change while a cache entry remains valid by TTL. Tool side effects are particularly unsafe to replay as cached answers.

Options considered

  • Cache all successful responses by prompt hash.
  • Disable response caching permanently.
  • Enable exact reuse only for approved deterministic-enough, nonpersonalized workloads.

Proposed decision

Disable gateway response caching by default. Approve specific workloads with an eligibility rule, tenant/scope partition, model/prompt/policy/corpus version and TTL/deletion owner. Reauthorize every hit before returning content. Exclude side-effecting tool results, unapproved personal data, uncertain streams and incomplete outputs. Treat a hit as a distinct reuse event with correct attribution rather than fabricating a fresh provider call.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Initial latency/cost savings are smaller, but isolation and correctness are easier to reason about. Cache invalidation becomes part of release and data-deletion workflows. The implementation may be an application-owned cache rather than a particular Apigee policy.

Required validation

Attempt cross-tenant hits and revoked access, change model/policy/corpus versions and force eviction. Verify allowed cache fallback still passes admission and does not leak data in telemetry.

Acceptance gates: GC-T10, GC-T14, GC-T15. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after measured repeated workload patterns justify a narrowly scoped cache.

decisions.title: Treat semantic caching as a separate quality and privacy experiment
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerRetrieval and evaluation leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Semantic proximity does not guarantee equivalent questions, permissions or business context. Embedding and vector services add processing destinations and cost. Provider context caching has different semantics and must not be included under the same approval.

Options considered

  • Enable semantic caching as a transparent optimization.
  • Use exact caching only.
  • Run a separate semantic-cache qualification on an approved workload.

Proposed decision

Keep semantic response caching off in the reference baseline. A later experiment must approve embedding/vector destinations, namespace isolation, corpus/model/policy versions, threshold and false-hit quality limits. Require authorization before and after candidate selection. Version changes invalidate eligibility unless equivalence is demonstrated. Inventory provider context caches separately with their owner, TTL and deletion behavior; do not count them as answer-cache hits.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The experiment can establish real savings but requires a labeled quality set and adversarial near-neighbor tests. Auxiliary processing may remove the cost benefit for low-hit workloads. Safety-sensitive and personalized tasks may remain ineligible.

Required validation

Measure false positive reuse, cross-scope collisions, privacy paths, failure behavior and total cost including embeddings/vector queries. Test permissions and corpus deletion while entries remain stored.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T14, GC-T15, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit only when quality evidence, workload repetition or service-control support materially changes.

decisions.title: Define durable authority for configuration, resources and customer state
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerData architecture leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A managed gateway does not need a customer PostgreSQL replica of its private control plane. However, application resource ownership, financial intents and job state remain durable customer concerns. Ambiguous authority produces inconsistent recovery and migration.

Options considered

  • Treat all state as gateway-managed.
  • Mirror every managed object in a generic customer database.
  • Assign one authoritative owner per state class and reconcile supported interfaces.

Proposed decision

Define an ownership inventory separating reviewed configuration, Apigee managed grants, hybrid runtime persistence, application resource mappings, financial reservations, retrieval indexes and telemetry. Keep customer state in an appropriately transactional durable store with schema/version ownership; do not imply a product-specific PostgreSQL requirement. Reconcile approved desired state to managed APIs without assuming access to proprietary storage. Preserve provider IDs only alongside verified application ownership and lifecycle metadata.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The design uses more than one store but makes their responsibilities explicit. Recovery and export are per state class rather than one mythical global backup. This adapts the original database concern to managed-service boundaries.

Required validation

Rebuild supported configuration and restore customer state in isolation. Test cross-owner access, missing mappings, schema compatibility and reconciliation after partial failure. Demonstrate which state cannot be recreated from logs.

Acceptance gates: GC-T16, GC-T18, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adopting stateful APIs, new stores, shared tenants or a different operating model.

Dependencies GC-ADR-001, GC-ADR-002, GC-ADR-007

Evidence informing this proposal [GP07] [GP53] [GP59] [GP63]

decisions.title: Qualify distributed coordination rather than assume a shared Redis design
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerDistributed systems ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Apigee policy counters and hybrid persistence are not the same architecture as LiteLLM Redis coordination. Distribution, synchronization, reset and outage semantics determine whether the service meets admission and revocation requirements.

Options considered

  • Assume platform counters are globally exact by default.
  • Replace all coordination with a customer service.
  • Use documented policy scope where sufficient and add an owned service for stronger invariants.

Proposed decision

For every counter or shared control, record authority, key scope, region, consistency, reset, expiry and loss-of-state behavior. Qualify the selected Apigee policy settings on the actual topology. Do not introduce Redis merely to mirror another product’s architecture, and do not treat generic Quota as equivalent to every token policy. Use a separately owned coordination service where a strict reservation or cross-region invariant cannot be met by the supported product contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This may produce different mechanisms for capacity, authorization freshness and money. The distinction is intentional and reduces false confidence. Stronger synchronization can cost latency and availability; business owners must approve the tradeoff.

Required validation

Test concurrent bursts, resets, partitions, stale restoration and recovery. Quantify admitted excess and stale decisions. Confirm dependency failure never silently changes a strict guarantee to unbounded local behavior.

Acceptance gates: GC-T04, GC-T07, GC-T09, GC-T20, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after topology growth, a policy implementation change or tighter consistency requirements.

Dependencies GC-ADR-002, GC-ADR-005, GC-ADR-017

Evidence informing this proposal [GP10] [GP08] [GP07]
