decisions.title: Use fail-closed monetary reservations only where a strict bound is required
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerFinOps and application platformDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Operational token counters and financial alerts do not establish an unconditional dispatch-time spending limit. Concurrent requests, late usage and unknown execution can create exposure beyond a nominal allowance. A stricter service must state its assumptions.

Options considered

  • Use alerts and post-call quotas as an approximate operating budget.
  • Qualify native preview spend cap budgets as a secondary project/service containment control.
  • Reject all uncertain-cost workloads.
  • Add a customer reservation authority for selected strict-budget workloads.

Proposed decision

Classify budgets as approximate operational guidance or strict admission policy. For strict classes, atomically reserve conservative maximum exposure before dispatch using trusted tenant, price version and bounded work. Unknown estimation fails closed or consumes a separately approved fixed allowance. Record each authorized attempt, retain uncertain exposure after dispatch and allocate bounded regional authority. Never describe this customer component as an Apigee built-in guarantee or an absolute invoice ceiling outside its workload assumptions. Evaluate the native preview spend cap first; use it where its documented scope and delayed enforcement are acceptable, alongside rather than as proof of a stronger tenant-level reservation guarantee.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Stricter controls can reject useful work and temporarily hold unused funds. They add a critical dependency and reconciliation workload. Approximate workloads can use simpler controls when their owners explicitly accept overshoot and evidence limits.

Required validation

Race calls at the allowance edge; inject duplicate dispatch, missing price, crash, timeout and partition. Verify reservation invariants and declared residual exposure, then compare observed settlement and billing aggregates. Where a native cap is selected, test its enforcement and restoration workflow, owner permissions, residual charges and rearming behavior without affecting unrelated production services.

Acceptance gates: GC-T07, GC-T09, GC-T10, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when pricing, modalities, maximum output, routing candidates or the business’s permitted exposure changes.

decisions.title: Separate operational usage, estimated cost and billed reconciliation
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerFinancial data ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

One logical request can create several billable attempts, auxiliary calls and a cached result. Missing usage or a delayed export cannot be treated as zero. The evidence available for exact billing joins differs from application tracing.

Options considered

  • Use gateway metrics as the invoice ledger.
  • Use billing export alone for operational attribution.
  • Maintain distinct attempt/usage and billing datasets with explicit reconciliation.

Proposed decision

Record logical calls, attempts, cache outcomes, tool/job work, observed token categories, price basis and confidence. Maintain a separate billing export analysis with supported dimensions and timing. Deduplicate only with reliable identity and preserve unmatched/uncertain records. Attribute auxiliary services and provider context caching separately where evidence permits. Publish reconciliation tolerance, adjustment authority and unresolved exposure; never fabricate precision unavailable in the billing data.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The system provides more honest accounting but requires reconciliation operations and carefully governed data access. Estimates can be useful before bills arrive without being presented as invoice truth. Retention should preserve evidence without unnecessarily storing content.

Required validation

Exercise retries, partial streams, cancellations, cache hits, safety callouts and batch work. Reconcile totals and explain mismatches within approved tolerances. Test loss/replay of usage events and controlled adjustments.

Acceptance gates: GC-T09, GC-T10, GC-T17, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when billing schemas, model pricing, usage metadata or internal chargeback rules change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-012, GC-ADR-017, GC-ADR-019

decisions.title: Give configuration one reviewed source of ownership
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerPlatform delivery leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Proxy bundles, shared flows, API products, grants, environment settings and external identities can change through different interfaces. Uncontrolled ownership makes the effective policy hard to reconstruct and can cause an emergency edit to disappear during the next deployment.

Options considered

  • Allow console and automation edits without reconciliation.
  • Force every entity into one configuration tool regardless of support.
  • Define authoritative reviewed artifacts and explicit delegated runtime workflows.

Proposed decision

Use reviewed versioned artifacts for security-sensitive proxy/shared-flow definitions, aliases and network/identity intent. Identify which managed entities are reconciled through supported APIs and which have delegated runtime workflows. Require effective permission and target diffs with every release. Detect drift; emergency changes need actor attribution, expiry/review and reconciliation before incident closure. Do not assume an administrative success response proves all runtime paths have converged.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The process limits ad hoc flexibility but improves explainability and repeatable recovery. Some managed objects may require specialized export/reconciliation rather than one universal tool. Configuration changes receive the same review rigor as privileged code.

Required validation

Promote a controlled change, compare repository/managed/effective state and detect an unauthorized edit. Reconcile an emergency grant and demonstrate an approved rollback without widening permissions.

Acceptance gates: GC-T04, GC-T18, GC-T19, GC-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when management APIs, automation tooling or delegated administration responsibilities change.

decisions.title: Release the complete service manifest, not just a proxy revision
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerRelease managerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Managed rollouts, hybrid artifacts, policy support, model versions, IAM bindings, SDKs and auxiliary services have independent lifecycles. A gateway-only version pin cannot freeze the complete application contract.

Options considered

  • Upgrade components independently with smoke tests.
  • Freeze indefinitely on a known revision.
  • Promote a versioned service manifest with impact-based qualification.

Proposed decision

Create a release manifest covering operating model, runtime/instance evidence, proxy/shared-flow revisions, model/API/location tuple, dependencies, identity/network diffs and acceptance results. Canary changes on approved workloads. Define the rollback boundary before deployment, including data compatibility and provider resource ownership. Track retirement and support dates; managed release announcements are inputs to observation and requalification, not proof of tenant rollout.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More dependencies enter change review, but this reduces accidental unsupported combinations. Managed components may not offer exact version pinning; the process must detect behavioral change and keep client contracts resilient rather than promise total control.

Required validation

Run impacted security, contract, quality, capacity and recovery tests. Verify canary metrics and effective revisions. Demonstrate a rollback or controlled roll-forward for the selected compatibility boundary.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T18, GC-T20, GC-T21, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when release cadence, product support, model retirement or managed rollout behavior changes.

decisions.title: Separate components by responsibility and failure behavior
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerPlatform architectureDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The platform can include ingress, managed or hybrid runtime, identity, adapters, safety, finance, retrieval and agent gateways. More services can reduce blast radius but also increase callouts, latency and operational ambiguity.

Options considered

  • Use one monolithic application/gateway boundary.
  • Split every function into an independent service.
  • Separate only responsibilities with different trust, scaling or lifecycle requirements.

Proposed decision

Keep caller admission and the public contract at one primary gateway boundary. Separate administration from runtime exposure and isolate privileged tool execution, retrieval authorization and any strict monetary service as their responsibilities require. Use an adapter service or another gateway only for demonstrated unsupported functionality with a clear deadline and failure contract. For hybrid, treat runtime and persistence placement explicitly. Agent Gateway remains an optional native identity/egress component, not a duplicate universal front door.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The reference is composable but avoids decomposition for its own sake. Each new service needs an owner, telemetry and failure policy. Dependency fan-out can outweigh any individual runtime performance advantage.

Required validation

Draw the actual dependency graph and inject independent failures. Verify each owner can identify which work must stop, which can continue and which evidence is needed to reconcile afterward.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T05, GC-T12, GC-T20, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when scaling, sensitivity, agent adoption or organizational ownership makes a current boundary ineffective.

Dependencies GC-ADR-001, GC-ADR-002, GC-ADR-008, GC-ADR-010, GC-ADR-017

Evidence informing this proposal [GP07] [GP19] [GP35]

decisions.title: Size for concurrent long-lived work and auxiliary bottlenecks
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerCapacity engineeringDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Requests per second alone do not characterize model workloads. Long streams, large multimodal inputs, safety callouts, vector lookups and slow clients can dominate memory, sockets and deadlines. Provider capacity is separate from gateway resource capacity.

Options considered

  • Scale only on CPU or average request count.
  • Provision for unbounded worst case.
  • Use workload classes, bounded admission and measured resource curves.

Proposed decision

Define workload classes with payload/output bounds, stream duration, callout fan-out and expected concurrency. Size pools, buffers, descriptors and queues from measured active work and tail behavior. Keep application quota, gateway protection and model capacity independent. Select capacity modes and overflow policy explicitly. Reject or defer work when limits are reached rather than hiding overload in unlimited queues. Scale hybrid persistence and egress dependencies with the runtime.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Capacity planning becomes more involved and may reject legitimate bursts, but prevents an apparently healthy gateway from accumulating unfinishable work. Managed hosting reduces some infrastructure tasks without eliminating workload-level admission decisions.

Required validation

Load-test realistic distributions, reduced backend capacity, long streams and slow clients. Observe pool wait, active work, memory, event-loop/runtime delay and completion; verify resources return to baseline after cancellation.

Acceptance gates: GC-T07, GC-T08, GC-T12, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when model latency, traffic mix, output bounds, capacity purchases or auxiliary services change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-012, GC-ADR-013, GC-ADR-018, GC-ADR-023

Evidence informing this proposal [GP46] [GP28] [GP34] [GP63]

decisions.title: Use metadata-first telemetry with explicit usage confidence
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerObservability leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Debugging AI traffic creates pressure to log full prompts and tool payloads. That can expose secrets and retrieved documents while still failing to distinguish user calls, attempts and incomplete streams. Sampling and sink outages can create invisible evidence gaps.

Options considered

  • Log complete request/response content by default.
  • Collect only coarse aggregate metrics.
  • Use a structured metadata schema with controlled exceptional content capture.

Proposed decision

Collect request/attempt/job/tool identifiers, verified scope, alias and concrete target, policy revision, stage latencies, outcome and observed/estimated/unknown usage. Exclude authorization headers, secrets and raw content by default. Permit exceptional content capture only with approved scope, reader access, expiry and redaction checks. Define bounded buffering/drop/fail behavior for each sink and expose telemetry gaps. Do not use operational metrics as the sole financial or administrative ledger.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Triage may require controlled reproduction rather than unrestricted historical prompts. The privacy surface is smaller and outcome attribution becomes clearer. High-assurance workloads may choose stricter evidence availability at an explicit availability cost.

Required validation

Inspect every sink using synthetic sensitive markers; force telemetry failures and validate gap reporting. Confirm incomplete streams and retries have distinct outcome and usage-confidence records.

Acceptance gates: GC-T10, GC-T11, GC-T17, GC-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when incident needs, telemetry vendors, data classifications or retention requirements change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-007, GC-ADR-013, GC-ADR-020

decisions.title: Make administrative changes attributable and audit coverage explicit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerSecurity operations ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Knowing that an API was called is different from knowing who changed the policy, identity grant or tool catalog that permitted it. Cloud administrative and data-access logs have different categories and enablement requirements.

Options considered

  • Rely on the request analytics dashboard.
  • Collect all available logs without a coverage plan.
  • Specify required administrative/data-access events and independent evidence custody.

Proposed decision

Define an audit matrix for policy publication, shared-flow change, role binding, product/app grant, key revocation, backend identity, catalog change and sensitive resource operations. Retain actor, approver, object, effective revision, timestamp and outcome where available. Separate audit readers/retention administration from ordinary runtime operators. Verify required data-access categories and export integrity; do not infer coverage from the presence of administrative logs.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Explicit auditing increases storage and operational work, and some categories need additional configuration. It improves incident reconstruction while discouraging unnecessary prompt retention. Missing required evidence becomes a visible acceptance failure.

Required validation

Execute representative changes and denied actions, then prove attribution, delivery lag, permissions and export continuity. Include a failure of the audit sink and a shared deployment identity in the test.

Acceptance gates: GC-T17, GC-T18, GC-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when event categories, roles, external sinks or regulatory evidence obligations change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-008, GC-ADR-021, GC-ADR-025

decisions.title: Treat runtime and datastore migrations as coordinated compatibility changes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerHybrid and data platform ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Hybrid persistence, customer schemas, proxy contracts and provider-owned resources do not all roll back with an image. A supported backup from one version may not be a supported restore input for another.

Options considered

  • Roll back containers independently of stored state.
  • Require a full outage for every change.
  • Use documented compatibility boundaries with rehearsed migration and recovery.

Proposed decision

Before upgrade, record runtime/platform, Cassandra arrangement, backup format, customer schema and key compatibility. Rehearse the supported target upgrade and recovery path in isolation. Drain within a qualified multi-cluster strategy where required; do not infer zero downtime from replica count. Treat managed-service configuration export, customer-store migration and hybrid datastore migration as separate workstreams. Preserve forward recovery when reverse migration is unsupported.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Migration planning consumes effort and can restrict emergency downgrade choices. It avoids turning a routine patch into data loss or restored stale authority. Version-specific official procedures take precedence over generic database advice.

Required validation

Restore a representative compatible backup, run application and revocation checks, and measure recovery. Attempt unsupported combinations in validation to ensure runbooks prevent accidental use; document point-of-no-return approvals.

Acceptance gates: GC-T18, GC-T20, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit with each runtime/storage major change, backup mechanism change or recovery-target revision.

Dependencies GC-ADR-017, GC-ADR-021, GC-ADR-022

decisions.title: Separate readiness, health and graceful draining
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSRE leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A process can answer a health endpoint while using stale configuration, lacking credentials or failing an essential safety/counter dependency. Conversely, a remote telemetry outage may not justify removing healthy serving capacity.

Options considered

  • Use one binary process health check for all dependencies.
  • Make readiness require every optional service.
  • Define layered health and dependency-specific readiness/draining.

Proposed decision

Distinguish process liveness, runtime readiness, effective policy freshness, credential availability, model-path health and optional integration health. Readiness gates only dependencies required by the admitted workload class. Bound stale operation and publish its status. Before planned removal, stop new admission, drain eligible in-flight work, record incomplete/cancelled outcomes and reconcile outstanding reservations. Health probes use safe low-cost contracts and never expose admin secrets.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The health model is more complex but prevents both false availability and unnecessary cascading outages. Draining long streams may require an explicit maximum wait and controlled interruption policy.

Required validation

Fail dependencies separately, drain under long streams and verify readiness decisions and capacity recovery. Confirm scaling/restart does not erase uncertain outcomes or silently broaden admission.

Acceptance gates: GC-T04, GC-T12, GC-T20, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adding a critical dependency, changing stream duration or adopting a different runtime topology.

Dependencies GC-ADR-012, GC-ADR-013, GC-ADR-021, GC-ADR-024

decisions.title: Prove resilient operation inside the approved geography before expanding regions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerResilience architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Region duplication can improve continuity but also duplicates state, cost and processing approvals. A second region is not useful if model capacity, safety, identity or retrieval cannot operate there under the required controls.

Options considered

  • Begin with global active-active routing.
  • Stay single-instance indefinitely.
  • Establish resilient primary operation, then add a fully qualified recovery region.

Proposed decision

First demonstrate resilient serving and recovery in the approved primary processing envelope. Add another region only for a concrete continuity or locality requirement with prequalified models, quotas, identities, safety/retrieval services and resource ownership. Failover must preserve capability and privacy constraints. Do not change to a global endpoint as an undocumented availability override. Stateful work needs an explicit owner/continuation plan rather than generic rerouting.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The first deployment is simpler and easier to validate, but may not satisfy stringent continuity targets until regional work is completed. Multi-region cost and operational complexity are justified by measured business needs.

Required validation

Fail the primary path and exercise only approved recovery routes. Confirm actual capacity, networking, credentials, geographic constraints and treatment of active sessions/jobs before production approval.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T12, GC-T21, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when continuity targets, model/service locations or residency obligations change.

decisions.title: Allocate bounded regional admission authority before partitions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerFinOps and distributed systemsDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A global budget or quota label does not guarantee a global atomic balance. If every disconnected region independently admits against the full allowance, business exposure can multiply precisely during an outage.

Options considered

  • Let each region consume the full global limit.
  • Require one always-online global authority for every call.
  • Allocate bounded regional authority with explicit reconciliation and rebalancing.

Proposed decision

For strict-budget workloads, assign bounded regional spending authority before isolated operation. Preserve reservation and attempt ownership locally under a durable supported mechanism. Rebalance only through an authenticated, audited transfer that prevents double allocation. During partition, exhaust only the assigned share; do not fall back to unlimited local counters. Approximate rate limits can use looser semantics only under a separately approved overshoot contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Unused allowance in a healthy region may not immediately rescue another region, reducing availability compared with unrestricted admission. The tradeoff makes financial exposure bounded and explainable during the most uncertain period.

Required validation

Partition regions while near limits, replay transfers, restore stale state and reconcile concurrent attempts. Demonstrate conservation of authority and the declared maximum residual exposure after recovery.

Acceptance gates: GC-T07, GC-T09, GC-T10, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when region count, business limits, counter semantics or admission-availability requirements change.

Dependencies GC-ADR-018, GC-ADR-019, GC-ADR-020, GC-ADR-029

decisions.title: Recover correct authority and unresolved work, not just running infrastructure
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerDisaster recovery ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Restoring a database can resurrect revoked credentials, lose ownership mappings or erase uncertain spending. Managed configuration, hybrid persistence, customer jobs and provider resources need different recovery evidence.

Options considered

  • Treat a successful database restore as complete recovery.
  • Recreate everything from deployment code alone.
  • Recover each authoritative state class and reconcile security/financial invariants.

Proposed decision

Maintain version-compatible backup and recovery procedures for customer-owned state, supported hybrid persistence and exported managed configuration. Preserve encryption keys, ownership mappings, pending jobs, reservations and revocation evidence. After restore, reconcile stale grants and unresolved attempts before reopening affected admission classes. Rebuild caches only after current authorization/policy state is established. Test managed instance recreation and provider resource continuity where relevant.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery may be slower than simply restarting infrastructure, but it restores a trustworthy service rather than a potentially overprivileged one. Some provider state may be unrecoverable; that limitation requires explicit user/workflow recovery behavior.

Required validation

Perform an isolated restore drill including expired keys, revoked grants, unrecorded job submission and an uncertain billed call. Measure recovery point/time and verify authority and ledger invariants.

Acceptance gates: GC-T16, GC-T20, GC-T21, GC-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after any state owner, key custody, backup format, topology or recovery objective changes.

Dependencies GC-ADR-017, GC-ADR-019, GC-ADR-020, GC-ADR-021, GC-ADR-027, GC-ADR-029, GC-ADR-030

decisions.title: Verify customer artifacts and track managed-service change evidence
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSupply-chain security ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The deployment includes customer proxy code, shared flows, callout libraries, containers, charts, SDKs and possibly model adapters. Managed runtime reduces some artifact ownership but does not validate customer code or freeze behavior.

Options considered

  • Install latest artifacts automatically without qualification.
  • Pin everything indefinitely.
  • Use approved provenance and supported versions with impact-based requalification.

Proposed decision

Pin and verify customer-controlled artifacts, dependencies and configuration through the approved supply-chain process. Separate build/publish privileges, retain digests and review third-party callouts. Track managed release notices and observed instance behavior as evidence rather than pretending managed binaries are customer-controlled. Include model and SDK lifecycle in vulnerability and compatibility triage. Never use an unqualified old sample package merely because it appears in a documentation snippet.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This adds release discipline and dependency review but reduces exposure to accidental or malicious artifact changes. Support and security may require updates before a preferred maintenance window; the test suite must make controlled patching feasible.

Required validation

Verify provenance, scan and rebuild customer artifacts, exercise a dependency update and demonstrate supported rollback/roll-forward. Confirm blocked artifacts cannot be deployed through alternate operator paths.

Acceptance gates: GC-T18, GC-T19, GC-T20, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit on supply-chain incidents, package migrations, runtime support changes or new third-party plugins.

Dependencies GC-ADR-008, GC-ADR-021, GC-ADR-022

decisions.title: Treat policy code, shared flows and adapters as privileged extensions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerPlatform security engineeringDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Policy configuration can choose destinations, acquire backend credentials, inspect content and alter authorization variables. Shared flows and external callouts increase the impact of one change beyond a single API.

Options considered

  • Allow teams to attach arbitrary policies/callouts.
  • Prohibit all extensibility.
  • Provide reviewed extension points with constrained privileges and execution budgets.

Proposed decision

Treat proxy policy changes, custom code, shared flows and adapter services as privileged software. Review identity, destination, data access, dependency and execution-time effects. Restrict dynamic URLs and credential access; use approved libraries and secrets mechanisms. Expose safe application-level configuration separately from privileged routing/authentication settings. A policy parser or a successful service call is not evidence of semantic correctness or authorization.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Extension review can slow customization but prevents a convenience feature from becoming an unrestricted credentialed egress path. Common reviewed patterns can reduce repeated effort while preserving a small trusted base.

Required validation

Attempt destination and variable injection, inspect permission diffs and run fault-path coverage. Test callout timeout, malformed responses, sensitive-data leakage and shared-flow changes affecting other APIs.

Acceptance gates: GC-T02, GC-T03, GC-T05, GC-T13, GC-T18, GC-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when new policy types, adapters, callout services or delegated publishing rights are introduced.

decisions.title: Default-deny tool and agent execution with backend authorization
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaIdentity & securitySuggested ownerAgent platform and business API ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A model can propose a tool call without having permission to execute it. Discovery, gateway method permission, native agent egress and business-object access are separate decisions. Side effects require stronger semantics than retryable text generation.

Options considered

  • Execute every model-requested registered tool.
  • Disable all tool access.
  • Approve tool/method/resource grants and validate each business action.

Proposed decision

Default-deny MCP and native agent actions until the specific transport, identity and tool contract is approved. Separate discover and invoke grants. Validate tool arguments, audience and destination, then require backend end-user/object authorization and any mandatory approval. Treat tool descriptions/results as untrusted input. Writes require business idempotency or a nonreplayable transaction policy. Explicitly distinguish dry-run from enforcement and qualify the exact Agent Gateway resource prerequisites.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This requires collaboration with tool owners and may limit autonomous operation. It prevents a registry entry or prompt instruction from becoming authority. Multiple gateways can provide complementary checks only when their relationship is documented and tested.

Required validation

Test hidden/unknown tools, stale catalogs, wrong audiences, unauthorized objects, injection, session reuse and duplicate actions. Correlate actual backend transactions with gateway decisions and approvals.

Acceptance gates: GC-T04, GC-T05, GC-T16, GC-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adding tools, changing transport or granting agents new side effects or external reach.

decisions.title: Bind provider state and identifiers to verified application owners
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerApplication data ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Context caches, files, conversations, interactions, sessions and jobs can be identified by provider-issued IDs. A privileged gateway may retrieve them across users unless it keeps an independent ownership map. Such IDs also constrain migration and fallback.

Options considered

  • Pass all provider IDs through without validation.
  • Avoid every stateful feature.
  • Support selected stateful resources with owner and lifecycle mappings.

Proposed decision

Create an application-owned record for each supported provider resource, including tenant/user, provider/project, location, type, creation/expiry, permitted operations and policy version. Authorize before read, continue, delete or cancel. Do not route a bound identifier to another provider or region unless an approved reconstruction mechanism exists. Exclude preview stateful interfaces from the initial contract unless retention/control limitations are explicitly accepted.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This adds durable mapping and cleanup work but avoids turning IDs into bearer capabilities. Migration must account for resources created before cutover, and some workflows may need to expire rather than transfer old state.

Required validation

Use foreign IDs, stale mappings, deleted owners and migrated aliases. Test read/delete/cancel authorization, TTL cleanup and failure between provider creation and local persistence.

Acceptance gates: GC-T05, GC-T15, GC-T16, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when enabling another stateful endpoint, changing retention or moving providers/projects.

decisions.title: Separate asynchronous and media workloads from interactive admission
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerJob platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Batch and media work can have large inputs, delayed billing, durable jobs and long completion times. An interactive timeout does not describe their lifecycle, and resubmitting after uncertainty can duplicate expensive work.

Options considered

  • Run all workloads through the chat request lifecycle.
  • Exclude asynchronous/media use entirely.
  • Use a dedicated job contract, owner store and allowance class.

Proposed decision

Add asynchronous/media endpoints only through a distinct job service contract. Authorize input/output storage, persist intent before submission, bind provider job IDs to owners, and use bounded polling/cancellation. Give jobs separate concurrency, payload, retention and financial limits. Treat ambiguous submission as unresolved rather than an automatic retry. Maintain durable progress and deletion evidence; client disconnect does not silently terminate ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The workflow is less convenient than a single blocking call but can recover safely and explain delayed expenditure. Some media costs need fixed conservative allowances when exact estimation is unavailable.

Required validation

Crash before/after submit and ID persistence, restart pollers, issue duplicate requests and revoke owners. Verify no unauthorized output access, unbounded reissue or lost financial exposure.

Acceptance gates: GC-T09, GC-T10, GC-T12, GC-T16, GC-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when adding new media types, batch APIs, scheduling guarantees or billing models.

Dependencies GC-ADR-012, GC-ADR-017, GC-ADR-019, GC-ADR-020, GC-ADR-031, GC-ADR-035

decisions.title: Keep quality and retrieval correctness under product ownership
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerApplication product and evaluation leadDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A compatible gateway response does not demonstrate a useful or safe answer. Model replacements, prompts, retrieval indexes and cache hits can all change task quality while infrastructure remains healthy.

Options considered

  • Accept a model based on generic provider benchmarks.
  • Freeze one model/prompt indefinitely.
  • Use application-specific quality and safety gates for every material change.

Proposed decision

Maintain task-specific golden and adversarial sets covering correctness, structured output, tool choice, citations, retrieval authorization and refusal behavior. Product owners accept quality tradeoffs; the gateway team owns faithful execution and evidence, not the business outcome by proxy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The organization must invest in evaluation data and review rather than rely on model reputation. This enables controlled replacement and exposes quality regressions caused by seemingly operational changes. Some fallbacks will remain ineligible despite good latency.

Required validation

Run blinded or reproducible comparisons with retained fixture versions, inspect failure categories and validate authorized citations. Require acceptance before alias, prompt, retrieval or caching changes reach production.

Acceptance gates: GC-T06, GC-T13, GC-T14, GC-T15, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when task requirements, model lifecycle, corpus content or acceptable risk changes.

decisions.title: Confirm entitlement, support and ownership cost for the exact composition
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerProcurement and platform sponsorDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A broad product license or cloud account does not establish access to every policy, environment, region or preview feature. Managed and hybrid operations have different customer obligations. Published list prices do not capture auxiliary services or negotiated terms.

Options considered

  • Select using a generic feature list and gateway unit price.
  • Assume existing enterprise contracts cover the extension.
  • Confirm required entitlements, lifecycle/support and full ownership-cost assumptions.

Proposed decision

Obtain explicit confirmation of the environment/policy packaging, model availability, capacity, regions, support response, preview acceptance and deployment rights needed by the selected design. Confirm the current hybrid support matrix rather than resolving conflicting prose/table dates by assumption. Price inference, policies, auxiliary services, networking, storage, customer infrastructure, labor and migration separately. Assign owners for model and gateway incidents and document where supplier guarantees stop.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Procurement becomes an architecture input and may change the preferred deployment. The result is a realistic operating commitment instead of a low headline price that excludes required controls. Unresolved mandatory entitlements block production approval.

Required validation

Review the signed scope and cost model against the manifest, contact support through the intended path and verify support/lifecycle ownership. No invented quote or benchmark substitutes for evidence.

Acceptance gates: GC-T01, GC-T12, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit at renewal, feature expansion, price/capacity changes or altered support/preview terms.

decisions.title: Benchmark the whole governed workload and its failure modes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerPerformance and reliability engineeringDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Gateway latency claims can omit authentication, safety, routing, long streams, logging and upstream variability. A high throughput number is not useful if completion, isolation or accounting correctness fails at load.

Options considered

  • Use vendor synthetic throughput as the selection criterion.
  • Measure only average proxy latency.
  • Run an equivalent governed workload with staged dependency and failure tests.

Proposed decision

Benchmark native, managed gateway and any hybrid alternative under the same client contract, model quality, policy chain and privacy controls. Measure acceptance, first usable output, completion, rejection, cancellation, resource use and usage-record lag separately. Include overload, dependency failure and recovery. State workload distribution, warmup, duration, sample count and confidence limits. No production performance or reliability claim is approved from this documentation review alone.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Tests cost real inference and engineering time, but make tradeoffs comparable. Controlled upstreams help isolate overhead while live selected models reveal integration behavior. Neither alone is a complete production qualification.

Required validation

Execute the defined harness with realistic payloads and concurrency, verify tail behavior and correctness invariants, and retain raw sanitized results. Repeat after material runtime, policy, capacity or model changes.

Acceptance gates: GC-T06, GC-T07, GC-T09, GC-T11, GC-T12, GC-T20, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when traffic shape, service objectives, policy chain or supplier capacity changes.

Dependencies GC-ADR-003, GC-ADR-012, GC-ADR-013, GC-ADR-019, GC-ADR-024, GC-ADR-025, GC-ADR-037

decisions.title: Preserve an exit path and review the architecture on evidence triggers
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & contractsSuggested ownerArchitecture review boardDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A managed platform and its surrounding policies can create useful integration and lock-in at the same time. Model retirement, control gaps, economics and organizational strategy can change faster than a long procurement cycle.

Options considered

  • Accept unrestricted coupling to the current platform.
  • Abstract every provider feature at excessive implementation cost.
  • Preserve a bounded portable client contract with explicit nonportable extensions.

Proposed decision

Maintain a replacement fixture for the public application contract, exportable reviewed configuration and owner-bound resource inventory. Label provider-native/stateful features that cannot move transparently. Keep a native or alternative-gateway baseline for measuring incremental value, without requiring all production traffic to be dual-run. Revisit on lifecycle, security, cost, quality or mandatory-control triggers. Retire obsolete routes and resources deliberately, retaining necessary audit and financial evidence under policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Portability remains selective rather than pretending all features are identical. The organization pays for some duplicate testing but gains a credible negotiation and recovery option. Exit plans must address application data and permissions as well as endpoint changes.

Required validation

Demonstrate the same client fixture on a qualified alternative route, inventory nonportable resources and test cutover/rollback without cross-owner access or uncontrolled replay. Obtain owner acceptance of any continuity limits.

Acceptance gates: GC-T06, GC-T16, GC-T18, GC-T21, GC-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Review at least at major architecture or contract renewal and immediately on a material unsupported requirement or retirement event.

decisions.title: Adopt shared commercial mediation only for explicit requirements
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerPlatform architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The reference organization needs accountable model access across teams but has not demonstrated that one additional gateway is necessary for every application. Commercial administration can replace engineering work while introducing a vendor dependency and another privileged execution layer. The choice must be based on the complete operating service.

Options considered

  • Retain direct provider access with application controls.
  • Adopt Portkey/SCM as the shared commercial gateway.
  • Retain an incumbent gateway or compose narrowly separated services.

Proposed decision

Establish a native or incumbent control group, then qualify Portkey for the requirements it demonstrably improves: shared provider access, governed configuration, administration or security integration. Start with a bounded LLM contract and an accountable service owner. Keep task authorization, quality and any strict monetary service explicitly assigned. Do not make adoption of MCP, agents, prompt hosting or additional security products implicit in the gateway decision.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This can preserve more than one approved integration pattern and requires a clear rule for when shared mediation is mandatory. It avoids paying for duplicated controls and makes the commercial benefit measurable, but adds upfront comparison work.

Required validation

Run the same capability, policy, failure and cost fixtures through both paths. Demonstrate the additional controls and attempted bypasses. Approval requires a documented requirement and benefit, not a broad feature score.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T02, PK-T03, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Provider scope, team count, operating capacity or a mandatory governance requirement changes.

Dependencies Reference assumptions and an approved business requirement.

decisions.title: Qualify OSS, Enterprise, SCM and special modes separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerPlatform security architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Public source visibility, a commercial runtime and a managed administration experience are different evidence boundaries. A shared name or ancestry cannot prove matching controls. The retrieved release channels also use different version numbers and may not represent the current tenant rollout.

Options considered

  • Treat all Portkey-branded distributions as equivalent.
  • Standardize on one exact qualified distribution and release set.
  • Support several distributions with separate capability and assurance records.

Proposed decision

Maintain a distribution manifest identifying the management product, tenant, runtime image, chart, support channel, endpoint set and enabled flags. Evaluate OSS source only as evidence for the selected OSS artifact. Require vendor confirmation for commercial runtime and SCM capability parity. Keep beta or body-forwarding modes outside the default governed contract until separately qualified. Do not prescribe the latest publicly observed changelog entry as automatically supported production software.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The manifest prevents false parity assumptions but increases qualification effort across multiple deployment variants. Fewer approved variants reduce maintenance cost. Customers depend on vendor-provided release evidence where source is private.

Required validation

Compare declared and deployed versions and flags, run the negative-control suite on each supported variant, and obtain a current compatibility/support statement. Demonstrate that an unqualified mode cannot be enabled by ordinary callers.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T02, PK-T03, PK-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new distribution, management migration, image channel or beta execution path is introduced.

Dependencies PK-ADR-001

decisions.title: Publish a bounded endpoint and execution-mode contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerApplication platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A unified URL can conceal native and translated paths with different persistence, tools, errors and event semantics. Applications need a stable contract stronger than request acceptance. Security-sensitive options must never disappear unnoticed during adaptation.

Options considered

  • Expose every documented route and pass through new parameters.
  • Publish a minimal tested contract and expand through acceptance gates.
  • Use provider-native APIs exclusively.

Proposed decision

Publish approved API/provider/mode combinations with required fields, unsupported-field disposition, resource semantics and denial classification. Start with bounded chat and separately qualified streaming. Distinguish native Responses from stateless adapted Responses. Forbid client-selected Nitro, beta, custom-destination and debugging modes unless explicitly allowed by a dedicated contract. Reject or deliberately classify unsupported security/retention options rather than treating successful parsing as compatibility.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some provider features will remain inaccessible through the shared route until tested. The restriction reduces accidental behavior changes and makes migration feasible. Application teams must own fixtures for their semantic and quality requirements.

Required validation

Test required fields, tools, structured output, native errors, ignored options, streaming events and stored-resource methods against native and proxied control groups. Include client libraries that discard unknown events.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T03, PK-T11, PK-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new endpoint, SDK, provider feature or translation path enters the supported service.

Dependencies PK-ADR-001, PK-ADR-002

decisions.title: Version model contracts independently of provider references
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerModel platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Applications benefit from a stable model promise, but a provider slug or catalog listing is only an address and access reference. Changing the selected deployment can alter context limits, tools, quality, location, state and price without changing the application request shape.

Options considered

  • Let applications select arbitrary catalog models.
  • Publish reviewed model contracts mapped to approved targets.
  • Hardcode one physical provider deployment in every application.

Proposed decision

Maintain an organization-owned catalog of model contracts, mapping each to approved physical targets, provider accounts, locations, capabilities and evaluation evidence. Define who can change that mapping and when a new contract version is required. Use catalog provisioning and locked configs to enforce access, but retain the contract outside the vendor UI. Require explicit requalification for embedding-model or stateful-provider changes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The abstraction improves portability only when the mapping is governed. It adds evaluation and release work, and an application may need more than one contract rather than a universal alias. Broad provider access remains a deliberate exception.

Required validation

Prove forbidden model and newly added integration access is denied. Replace a target in a canary and verify schema, semantic quality, location, usage and resource compatibility before promotion.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T06, PK-T09, PK-T21, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Model retirement, pricing, location, quality or capability changes affect an approved contract.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-010, PK-ADR-021

decisions.title: Issue distinct least-privilege workload keys
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerIdentity platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Shared keys erase attribution and make revocation disruptive. A key with valid authentication can still carry more authority than the workload needs. Human development, unattended services and administration have different accountability and lifecycle requirements.

Options considered

  • Share a workspace or organization credential.
  • Create distinct scoped service identities per application/environment.
  • Use short-lived delegated assertions for all traffic where supported.

Proposed decision

Assign each workload and environment a named, owned credential with the smallest verified operation scope, explicit workspace/model grants and a documented expiry/rotation process. Keep human and automation identities separate. Deny policy, provider, prompt, log and key administration unless separately justified. Attach and lock the required request policy. Preserve service attribution even when user identity is propagated for business authorization.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More credentials require provisioning automation and lifecycle ownership, but compromise and revocation can be contained. A workload key remains a service authority rather than proof of the current end user; applications need a separate user authorization mechanism.

Required validation

Exercise every forbidden management method and another workspace, then rotate and revoke through all serving nodes. Measure the actual revocation window, including warm operation under management outage.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T04, PK-T06, PK-T14. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

A new workload, shared credential, delegated user model or ownership change appears.

Dependencies PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-008, PK-ADR-021

decisions.title: Validate JWT trust, intended use and revocation explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerIdentity security ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Token signatures establish a signer, not the correct tenant, audience, policy or business permission. Local validation and caches introduce lifecycle behavior that differs from database-backed key lookup. Gateway access assertions and downstream tool assertions are separate trust relationships.

Options considered

  • Accept any token signed by a configured key.
  • Validate a constrained claim contract at the gateway and supporting identity broker.
  • Use scoped opaque keys until required JWT behavior is proven.

Proposed decision

Approve exact signer/algorithm, issuer, intended recipient, expiry, organization, workspace and scope mappings. Test the gateway behavior rather than assuming omitted controls are enforced. Ensure missing or unresolved required policy context fails closed through a demonstrated mechanism. Use bounded token lifetimes and a measured emergency revocation path. For tool forwarding, verify the downstream trust and business-object permissions separately from gateway authentication.

Consequences and tradeoffs

An identity broker or backend validation layer may be needed when native claims behavior does not satisfy the contract. Short lifetimes increase identity-service dependency, while long lifetimes increase stale-authority exposure. Neither tradeoff should be hidden behind an SSO checkbox.

Required validation

Use validly signed but wrongly scoped tokens, stale signing keys, wrong tenants and missing config claims. Test cold and warm nodes during rotation and management loss. Record the last accepted revoked assertion.

Acceptance gates: PK-T05, PK-T07, PK-T14, PK-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Trust provider, claim schema, validation mode, token lifetime or tool delegation changes.

decisions.title: Make tenant and resource isolation a tested invariant
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerSecurity architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Workspaces organize policy but do not prove every resource method is tenant-safe. Cache results, provider files, task identifiers, logs and future model provisioning create additional access surfaces. Client-supplied metadata cannot authenticate ownership.

Options considered

  • Rely on workspace labels alone.
  • Prove logical isolation across all resource and execution surfaces.
  • Use separate organizations/runtime stacks for stronger boundaries.

Proposed decision

Derive tenant identity from verified credentials or an approved mapping and intersect it with model, tool and resource grants. Bind every stored handle to owner, workspace, provider account and location. Test read/list/delete as rigorously as invocation. Namespace caches from trusted context. Use separate organizations, credentials or runtimes where logical tests or contractual guarantees do not meet the required isolation strength.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Owner indexes and negative tests add application work, but they expose gaps that feature checklists miss. Physical separation costs more and does not remove the need for resource authorization. New-workspace and inherited-access behavior must be reviewed continuously.

Required validation

Run a cross-tenant corpus across model calls, metadata spoofing, cache hits, logs, files, jobs, MCP tools and A2A tasks. Create new integrations/workspaces and verify no accidental privilege expansion.

Acceptance gates: PK-T04, PK-T05, PK-T06, PK-T13, PK-T19, PK-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New tenancy, sharing, resource method, inheritance rule or external customer access is added.

decisions.title: Separate management authority from inference traffic
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerSecurity operations ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Policy writers and administrators can change destinations, credentials, safety behavior and retained data. They therefore hold a stronger authority than an ordinary inference caller. Private networking helps reduce exposure but does not establish least privilege or attributable changes.

Options considered

  • Use one administration credential and common public route.
  • Separate named management roles, automation and network exposure.
  • Delegate all configuration to application workspaces.

Proposed decision

Restrict managed administration and customer management endpoints to approved operators and automation. Separate policy approval, credential administration and runtime operation where feasible. Use named service accounts, time-bounded emergency access and protected audit export. Do not expose log retrieval, registration or diagnostics through inference wildcards. Review workspace delegation for changes that alter organizational security or privacy requirements.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Administrative work may require review and slower promotion. That cost buys attributable changes and smaller compromise scope. Managed-console availability and vendor administrator controls remain contractual dependencies requiring explicit evidence.

Required validation

Attempt management operations with application credentials and from the application network. Execute representative approved and denied UI/API changes and reconstruct who changed what, when and with which effective result.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T04, PK-T18, PK-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Administrative API, SSO, delegation, support access or emergency procedure changes.

decisions.title: Separate provider secrets, encryption and registration authority
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerSecrets platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The runtime may hold provider credentials, vault permissions, scan-service keys and signed-identity material. Encryption protects stored objects but does not remove the runtime permission to decrypt or use them. Credential caching and workspace scoping affect rotation and recovery.

Options considered

  • Store shared secrets directly in broad configuration.
  • Use scoped secret references and separately managed encryption/signing material.
  • Use provider workload identities wherever the integration supports them.

Proposed decision

Prefer constrained workload identities or runtime secret resolution, with explicit workspace access and audited vault permissions. Keep provider, scan, management, registration, encryption and MCP signing authorities distinct. Define cache-aware rotation and emergency revocation at the source provider as well as the gateway. Confirm actual KMS principals for the deployment; never copy a hosted example blindly. Exclude plaintext secrets from manifests, logs and diagnostic exports.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More identities and key lifecycles increase operational complexity. Vault or KMS availability can become a request dependency, and cached secrets can outlive a central change. Those dependencies must be measured rather than hidden by an encrypted-at-rest claim.

Required validation

Rotate and revoke under load, deny fetch/decrypt access, cold-start nodes and exercise failover. Confirm no unrelated workspace can resolve a secret and no secret values appear in configured sinks.

Acceptance gates: PK-T07, PK-T08, PK-T17, PK-T22, PK-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Credential source, encryption authority, runtime cache, workspace scope or signing method changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-006, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-008, PK-ADR-031

decisions.title: Bind egress and processing location to the complete route
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture & trustSuggested ownerNetwork and privacy ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

An approved model destination is only one recipient in a composed gateway request. Scanners, tools, metadata, log viewing and secret services add paths. Hybrid runtime placement alone cannot establish end-to-end residency or prevent credential forwarding to an unintended host.

Options considered

  • Allow arbitrary provider URLs and rely on application discipline.
  • Allowlist the complete execution graph and credential recipient.
  • Use fully isolated single-provider stacks for constrained workloads.

Proposed decision

Approve model, scanner, tool, secret, management and telemetry destinations by workload and data class. Restrict custom hosts, redirects, DNS/private-address changes and forwarded credential headers through tested gateway and network controls. Apply the same policy to retries and fallbacks. Record processing and retention requirements separately. Do not route a required scan or tool call to another region merely to recover availability without an approved exception.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Explicit egress can slow provider onboarding and requires maintenance as service endpoints change. It makes data movement explainable and limits SSRF/credential leakage exposure. Network controls alone cannot authorize a business object or prove provider retention behavior.

Required validation

Use controlled destination tests, redirect chains and unexpected provider headers; observe actual traffic and credentials. Verify the full graph for native, adapted, cached, tool and failure paths.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T08, PK-T09, PK-T12, PK-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Provider, auxiliary integration, processing geography, redirect behavior or private connectivity changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-004, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-009, PK-ADR-033

decisions.title: Route only among approved equivalent targets
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerRuntime platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Pooling capacity and changing the model contract are different decisions. A router can return a valid response while violating required capabilities, quality, processing location or resource ownership. Adaptive behavior is harder to explain than a small static target set.

Options considered

  • Expose arbitrary provider fallback.
  • Begin with explicit weighted/equivalent targets and bounded fallback.
  • Adopt adaptive optimization immediately.

Proposed decision

Start with a small reviewed target graph and deterministic eligibility rules. Each primary and backup must meet the same approved workload contract, including model capability, credentials, location, quality and output limits. Use circuit state as a health signal, not an authorization bypass. Promote adaptive or conditional policies only with separate failure-distribution and task-quality evidence. Record the actual target per attempt.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The eligible pool may be smaller and more expensive than every technically callable model. The restriction reduces surprising substitutions and makes incidents explainable. Stateful resources may remain pinned even when stateless inference can move.

Required validation

Simulate every failure branch, throttling, cooldown and recovery. Confirm that denied, incompatible or location-prohibited targets receive no work. Compare application quality on all permitted alternatives.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T08, PK-T09, PK-T10, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Capacity strategy, target set, conditional routing or model contract changes.

decisions.title: Give one layer ownership of retries and deadlines
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerApplication reliability ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Client, gateway and provider libraries can all retry. Their combined behavior may exceed the intended duration or financial exposure. A network failure after dispatch is ambiguous, and replaying tool or job operations can duplicate side effects.

Options considered

  • Leave retries enabled independently at each layer.
  • Assign one retry owner with bounded total attempts and wall time.
  • Disable all retries and rely on caller recovery.

Proposed decision

Define the single retry owner per workload, the retryable failure classes, maximum total attempts and end-to-end deadline. Account for upstream/client hidden retries and Retry-After behavior. Stop on authentication or terminal policy denial. Preserve the remaining deadline through fallback. Treat ambiguous dispatch as potentially completed and billable. Require domain idempotency or explicit reconciliation before replaying side-effecting operations.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some failures surface to users rather than being hidden by another attempt. The policy reduces amplification and makes cost/exposure predictable. Applications need clear incomplete/unknown outcomes and recovery guidance instead of a generic retry-on-error wrapper.

Required validation

Trace all actual attempts under connection drops, timeouts, throttling and fallback. Prove no replay after partial disclosure or unverified side effects, and verify the full deadline at the client boundary.

Acceptance gates: PK-T09, PK-T10, PK-T11, PK-T15, PK-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Client SDK, provider behavior, fallback graph or transaction semantics changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-011, PK-ADR-013, PK-ADR-019, PK-ADR-036

decisions.title: Specify streaming, cancellation and disclosure explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerApplication ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A stream creates an irreversible disclosure boundary before final usage or safety results may arrive. Client libraries differ in handling gateway-added events. Closing a connection cannot be assumed to stop provider computation or remove financial exposure.

Options considered

  • Treat streaming like an ordinary successful HTTP response.
  • Publish a stream lifecycle with bounded timing and explicit incomplete outcomes.
  • Use non-streaming buffered responses for the initial supported contract.

Proposed decision

Define first-byte, idle and absolute-duration limits, supported events, partial tool handling, final usage and terminal outcome classification. Verify client-visible denials independently of HTTP status. Do not retry after emitted content as a transparent continuation. Record cancellation attempts and unknown upstream completion. Use buffered delivery or disallow the workload when preventive output inspection is required but not demonstrated on the streaming path.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Buffering may reduce interactivity and increase memory. Explicit incomplete outcomes require application UX and accounting work. The design prevents a late diagnostic event from being misrepresented as prevention and separates transport success from task completion.

Required validation

Interrupt before dispatch, before first chunk, during content/tool arguments and before final usage. Test each supported SDK and raw protocol client; compare what was delivered with recorded policy and usage outcomes.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T10, PK-T11, PK-T12, PK-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Streaming API, client parser, timeout policy, output inspection or tool protocol changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-012, PK-ADR-014, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-025

decisions.title: Require preventive controls by route and execution phase
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerAI safety and security ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Input checks, output checks, asynchronous observation and external security scans protect different boundaries. A configured hook may be optional, overridden, late or unavailable in a special mode. Marketing descriptions cannot establish the exact prevention guarantee.

Options considered

  • Attach generic guardrails and accept defaults.
  • Define required preventive checks and qualify their execution per route.
  • Use detective monitoring only with explicit residual-risk acceptance.

Proposed decision

Version each required check with its phase, covered content, verdict/action schema, permitted data recipient and timeout/failure policy. Lock mandatory policy against caller and workspace bypass. Prevent upstream dispatch or client disclosure only through a demonstrated synchronous/buffering mechanism. Label asynchronous or post-stream checks detective. Treat denial as a distinct terminal application outcome, including compatibility-oriented successful-status responses. Qualify external AIRS scanning separately from gateway activation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Stronger prevention can add latency, vendor dependence and processing recipients. Some endpoint/mode combinations must be excluded or protected in an application service. Detective controls remain useful, but their limitations and incident response must be visible.

Required validation

Place synthetic markers in every admitted input/output channel, force scanner errors and bypass attempts, and observe actual dispatch/disclosure. Verify both positive and negative behavior with supported clients.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T08, PK-T11, PK-T12, PK-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Guardrail mode, scan service, policy version, client behavior or admitted protocol changes.

decisions.title: Keep exact response caching opt-in and tenant-safe
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerData platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Answer reuse can reduce work but also disclose data or preserve obsolete policy outcomes. Authentication, namespace partitioning and content key construction are separate mechanisms. Provider-owned resources and side effects are not ordinary reusable answers.

Options considered

  • Cache all successful completions by default.
  • Enable exact caching only for explicitly eligible workloads.
  • Avoid gateway response caching entirely.

Proposed decision

Default response caching off. For an approved workload, authenticate and resolve policy before reuse; derive a trusted namespace including tenant and relevant model/policy/data version; bound TTL and content retention. Do not accept arbitrary caller namespaces. Exclude secrets, personalized authorization-sensitive results, provider-owned handles and side effects. Define invalidation and cost reporting for hits independently of control-object caching.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Hit rate may be lower than broad shared caching and some workloads receive no benefit. This preserves confidentiality and traceability. Namespace/version changes are part of release management, and cache deletion does not erase other recipients or historical logs.

Required validation

Use identical prompts across tenants and changing permissions/model versions. Verify no cross-owner hits, correct expiry and invalidation, reauthorization and cost interpretation. Test unsupported streaming combinations explicitly.

Acceptance gates: PK-T06, PK-T13, PK-T16, PK-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Eligibility, key namespace, policy/data freshness or cache backend changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-014, PK-ADR-018, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-021

Evidence informing this proposal [PK18]
