decisions.title: Approve semantic caching as a separate quality decision
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerApplication product ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Similarity-based answer reuse can return a plausible but task-inappropriate result. It may also introduce an embedding service and another data store. A good exact-cache result provides no evidence that semantic matching preserves correctness for a regulated or transactional task.

Options considered

  • Enable semantic caching wherever exact caching is available.
  • Evaluate it per task against a versioned corpus and explicit risk threshold.
  • Limit the service to exact or no caching.

Proposed decision

Keep semantic caching out of the initial shared contract. Admit it only for a named workload after testing task correctness, tenant isolation, sensitivity, freshness and the additional embedding/storage recipients. Set acceptance thresholds from business consequences rather than generic similarity scores. Exclude authorization decisions, exact extraction obligations and side-effecting tasks unless a separate authoritative validation step makes reuse safe.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Potential savings are deferred and a task-specific evaluation is required. Semantic cache operation becomes part of the product, with drift, invalidation and quality ownership. The organization can decline it even when the gateway supports the feature.

Required validation

Compare against an uncached control using near-duplicate, contradictory, stale and cross-tenant prompts. Measure false reuse and downstream corrections as well as hit rate, latency and total cost.

Acceptance gates: PK-T06, PK-T13, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Task, corpus, embedding model, similarity settings or error tolerance changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-004, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-015, PK-ADR-037

Evidence informing this proposal [PK18]

decisions.title: Preserve managed desired state and customer recovery evidence
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerPlatform architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The original reference concern required a durable governance authority. In commercial Portkey/SCM, that authority is a managed service rather than a customer PostgreSQL deployment. Cached runtime objects are not a sufficient backup, and private vendor persistence internals are not public evidence.

Options considered

  • Treat runtime cache as the configuration system of record.
  • Use managed desired state with controlled customer exports and release evidence.
  • Adopt a fully customer-operated distribution under a separate contract.

Proposed decision

Recognize the selected managed control plane as the serving configuration authority while retaining customer-owned approved declarations, dependency maps and export evidence. Define conflict and drift ownership between reviewed source and managed objects. Contract for export, recovery, deletion and incident support. Keep business resource ownership and any strict monetary ledger in explicitly owned durable systems. Do not invent an unsupported customer database layer to emulate the managed product.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Managed persistence reduces infrastructure work but introduces vendor recovery dependence and export limitations. Customer evidence supports reconstruction and exit but must not silently override emergency changes. Cache continuity remains a separate operational feature.

Required validation

Reconstruct a test tenant/runtime from approved exports, verify dependency order and effective policy, and document objects or histories that require vendor action. Test loss of local caches without losing authoritative declarations.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T14, PK-T21, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Management product, export completeness, configuration authority or recovery contract changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-001, PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-021, PK-ADR-031, PK-ADR-038

Evidence informing this proposal [PK03] [PK07] [PK08] [PK04]

decisions.title: Separate coordination and configuration from answer caching
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerSRE ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Runtime caches may hold governance objects, pending usage and optional answer data with very different failure consequences. Configuring one Redis endpoint does not prove that all clients share the needed state or that multiple enforcement domains have globally consistent counters.

Options considered

  • Use one undifferentiated cache and accept defaults.
  • Document logical state classes and qualify the supported shared topology.
  • Use isolated runtimes with explicit independent allowances.

Proposed decision

Inventory each cache/counter client, key namespace, TTL, eviction policy, acknowledgement and failure response. Keep response-cache eligibility separate from coordination and configuration availability. Use vendor-supported shared state and capacity, with isolation where justified. Test stale restoration and local fallback rather than assuming limits remain correct. Specify maximum authorization/configuration age independently of cache retention and ensure pending accounting state has an explicit loss/replay contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Extra state isolation or capacity can add cost. The documentation burden exposes hidden dependencies and allows security, availability and financial tradeoffs to be reviewed separately. No global atomicity claim is made from a common Redis label.

Required validation

Inject memory pressure, partitions, cache loss, stale snapshots, new nodes and restarts during usage flush. Measure admitted work, revocation convergence, duplicates, gaps and cold-object behavior.

Acceptance gates: PK-T13, PK-T14, PK-T15, PK-T16, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Cache topology, scaling domain, TTL, eviction, resync or failure policy changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-019, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-028, PK-ADR-030

Evidence informing this proposal [PK07] [PK08] [PK18]

decisions.title: Distinguish native allowances from strict monetary admission
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerFinOps and service ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Operational rate/budget policies can be valuable without constituting an exact dispatch-time spending ceiling. Concurrency, delayed usage, retries, tool work, unknown prices and regional separation create exposure. Financial correctness must be specified before selecting a mechanism.

Options considered

  • Treat configured usage budgets as an unconditional cap.
  • Accept native approximate allowances with a documented exposure bound.
  • Add a separately qualified reservation/admission service for strict requirements.

Proposed decision

Classify each workload as ordinary allowance or strict monetary authorization. Use native policies where their tested contract is sufficient. For strict scope, reserve a conservative approved maximum before dispatch using idempotent request/attempt records, bound unknown exposure and fail closed when authority is unverifiable. Include retries, auxiliary services and asynchronous work. Do not release a reservation solely on client disconnect or absence of usage. Keep the stronger mechanism explicitly customer-owned unless vendor evidence establishes it.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Strict admission adds state, estimation and availability costs and may reject useful work. Native limits remain useful defense in depth. Exact invoice matching may still be impossible when upstream billing is delayed or nondeterministic, so the accepted guarantee must be precisely bounded.

Required validation

Run parallel near-limit requests, regional partitions, unknown-price routes, crashes and partial streams. Demonstrate reservation settlement, exception ownership and the maximum accepted overshoot/exposure.

Acceptance gates: PK-T10, PK-T14, PK-T15, PK-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Financial requirement, pricing basis, concurrency, regions or chargeable feature set changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-012, PK-ADR-018, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-030, PK-ADR-036, PK-ADR-038

decisions.title: Reconcile application, provider and gateway ledgers separately
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution & stateSuggested ownerFinOps ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

An application request can create several model attempts, scan calls and tool transactions. Provider usage and gateway commercial metering are different units, while control-plane reporting may arrive later. Collapsing them hides discrepancies and can double charge internal users.

Options considered

  • Use the gateway dashboard as the sole ledger.
  • Maintain a customer attempt ledger and reconcile each billing authority.
  • Accept aggregate organizational billing without request chargeback.

Proposed decision

Record logical request and actual attempt identifiers, tenant, target, policy/pricing revision, measured or estimated usage, result class and uncertainty. Reconcile application reservations against attempts, attempts against provider billing dimensions, and gateway-metered usage against the commercial invoice. Use idempotent ingestion and exception queues for missing/duplicate events. Label character-derived tool metering distinctly from tokenizer output. Do not invent an exact request-ID invoice join where the supplier does not provide one.

Consequences and tradeoffs

A separate ledger adds retention and data-engineering responsibility. It improves explainability and internal chargeback but cannot manufacture missing upstream facts. Metadata should be minimized and access restricted to legitimate finance/operations roles.

Required validation

Reconcile known fixtures containing cache hits, retries, partial streams, errors, scans, batches and agent/tool calls. Simulate failed flushes and duplicate events, then resolve each discrepancy with preserved evidence.

Acceptance gates: PK-T15, PK-T16, PK-T17, PK-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Billing unit, price model, event schema, attribution policy or provider invoice granularity changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-018, PK-ADR-019, PK-ADR-025, PK-ADR-026, PK-ADR-036, PK-ADR-038

decisions.title: Make effective configuration ownership explicit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerRelease engineering ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A saved config, a key default, workspace delegation and caller parameters can all influence one request. A reviewed object name does not prove which effective policy executed. Managed UI convenience should not create an untracked second source of security-sensitive changes.

Options considered

  • Allow free runtime edits and caller overrides.
  • Assign reviewed ownership with limited delegation and effective-policy verification.
  • Make all configuration immutable and prohibit emergency changes.

Proposed decision

Assign an owner to every security-sensitive field and object. Promote reviewed configs, model mappings, guards, logging and egress rules through a controlled process, with exact content/version evidence. Disable unapproved caller overrides and restrict workspace delegation. Permit audited emergency changes under a defined reconciliation procedure. Verify the effective configuration on serving nodes; do not infer it from a successful UI save or a mutable config slug.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Changes require review and may converge asynchronously. Emergency operations need a clear reconciliation owner. The approach preserves developer flexibility for explicitly delegated settings while preventing policy drift from being mistaken for intended behavior.

Required validation

Change defaults, workspace rules and explicit request fields in conflicting combinations. Verify the accepted precedence, denied bypasses, effective revisions and exported change evidence across all runtimes.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T18, PK-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Configuration schema, precedence, default settings, delegation or management product changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-004, PK-ADR-008, PK-ADR-014, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-022, PK-ADR-026

Evidence informing this proposal [PK09] [PK04] [PK47]

Make all configuration immutable and prohibit emergency changes. Proposed decision Assign an owner to every security-sensitive field and object. Promote reviewed configs, model mappings, guards, logging and egress rules through a controlled process, with exact content/version evidence. Disable unapproved caller overrides and restrict workspace delegation. Permit audited emergency changes under a defined reconciliation procedure. Verify the effective configuration on serving nodes; do not infer it from a successful UI save or a mutable config slug. Consequences and tradeoffs Changes require review and may converge asynchronously. Emergency operations need a clear reconciliation owner. The approach preserves developer flexibility for explicitly delegated settings while preventing policy drift from being mistaken for intended behavior. Required validation Change defaults, workspace rules and explicit request fields in conflicting combinations. Verify the accepted precedence, denied bypasses, effective revisions and exported change evidence across all runtimes. Acceptance gates: PK-T03 , PK-T18 , PK-T21 . Status: not executed. Revisit trigger Configuration schema, precedence, default settings, delegation or management product changes. decisions.title: Promote coherent releases with a bounded rollback path
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerRelease managerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Gateway binaries, managed objects, model APIs, client libraries and feature flags evolve independently. A container rollback alone may not restore the accepted contract, and it cannot undo provider billing, retained data or tool side effects.

Options considered

  • Upgrade runtime images independently whenever available.
  • Release a tested artifact/configuration/client contract set with canary and rollback.
  • Freeze indefinitely on an observed version.

Proposed decision

Record the vendor-confirmed runtime/chart support set, image digests, managed policy revisions, model mappings, credentials by reference, client contracts and feature flags as one release. Test in isolation, canary bounded workloads, compare actual behavior and drain before broader promotion. Keep compatible prior artifacts and owner mappings until the rollback window closes. Define which managed changes are reversible and which require forward repair or vendor assistance.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Qualification takes effort and may delay optional features. It reduces accidental version skew and makes incident recovery deliberate. Freezing is not a security strategy; patch intake and model/API lifecycle events still require active review.

Required validation

Rehearse a failed canary, configuration rollback, key rotation during upgrade and interrupted jobs/streams. Verify no permission broadening, stranded resources or unaccounted work when returning to the accepted state.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T21, PK-T22, PK-T23, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Runtime, chart, managed schema, beta flag, provider API or client contract changes.

decisions.title: Choose deployment separation for explicit failure and trust boundaries
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerPlatform architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

SaaS, hybrid and separated protocol pools allocate different responsibilities. More services can isolate resource pressure and credentials, but also add costs, licensing questions and operational interfaces. The management product remains a distinct dependency even when runtimes are customer-operated.

Options considered

  • One shared deployment for all protocols and environments.
  • Separate only the pools needed for security or workload isolation.
  • Fully isolate every application and dependency.

Proposed decision

Select SaaS or hybrid based on contractual management, network and runtime-placement requirements. Within customer-operated scope, separate production from development and isolate LLM, tool or agent pools when their credentials, egress or long-lived resource demands justify it. Document shared control-plane, cache and telemetry dependencies. Do not describe a physical split as complete independence without tests. Obtain explicit entitlement for the intended number and topology of deployments.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Separation can reduce blast radius and noisy-neighbor effects but increases infrastructure, upgrades and support complexity. A shared managed plane can remain a correlated failure/security domain. Simpler deployments are preferable when they meet the requirements.

Required validation

Saturate or compromise a simulated protocol pool and verify other workloads remain within their contract. Map all shared dependencies and test the management outage behavior of each pool.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T06, PK-T14, PK-T22, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Workload mix, credential sensitivity, tenancy, network placement or deployment terms changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-001, PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-018, PK-ADR-024, PK-ADR-038

decisions.title: Bound concurrency, connection pools and autoscaling together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSRE capacity ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Requests-per-second alone does not size long streams, media, scans and agent tasks. Scaling runtimes also changes connections to providers, caches and secret services. Unbounded queues hide overload until deadlines expire and retries multiply the work.

Options considered

  • Scale on CPU alone with large queues.
  • Use workload-specific concurrency and dependency-aware scaling.
  • Provision fixed peak capacity and reject excess traffic.

Proposed decision

Define workload classes with maximum bytes, output size, active requests, queue delay and lifetime. Bound connection pools and auxiliary calls, then scale within tested provider/cache/vault capacity. Use client-observed latency and rejection metrics alongside CPU/memory. Shed or reject overload early with a documented recovery signal. Keep retry and financial admission limits in effect during autoscaling and avoid admitting more work simply because another pod starts.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Early rejection is visible to clients and requires retry guidance. Capacity headroom and isolation cost money, but uncontrolled buffering and provider amplification are less predictable. Per-class metrics and realistic burst tests are necessary operational work.

Required validation

Load-test mixed short calls, long streams, slow scans, large inputs and jobs. Observe queue age, pool wait, memory, sockets, dependency saturation and policy correctness during scaling and draining.

Acceptance gates: PK-T10, PK-T11, PK-T14, PK-T15, PK-T22, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Workload duration, payload size, provider quotas, scan latency or scaling topology changes.

decisions.title: Default to minimized telemetry and qualify every failure path
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerPrivacy and observability ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Observability is valuable, but prompts, transformed output, URLs, metadata and error bodies can contain sensitive data. A setting named metrics-only is not evidence that all protocols and failures exclude content. Local log storage may still be remotely viewable.

Options considered

  • Capture complete payloads for all requests.
  • Use minimized metadata by default with approved time-bounded content capture.
  • Disable all telemetry, including accounting and operational evidence.

Proposed decision

Define an allowed telemetry schema per sink and protocol. Default to bounded metadata, protect tenant identifiers and lock organizational logging controls where required. Allow content capture only for named purposes, restricted access and retention. Test errors, tool outputs and transformed/original content separately. Bound exporter queues and distinguish optional diagnostics from required audit/accounting evidence. Record dashboard access paths and verify historical deletion independently of future capture settings.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some incidents will be harder to debug without payloads and require controlled synthetic reproduction. Minimized metadata still needs privacy review. Telemetry outages need explicit degraded behavior so performance is not protected by silently losing required evidence.

Required validation

Inject synthetic secrets into successful and failed model/tool calls, inspect every sink and UI path, then test collector saturation, duplicate delivery, retention expiry and historical purge.

Acceptance gates: PK-T11, PK-T16, PK-T17, PK-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Logging mode, sink, protocol, error handling, retention or remote viewing behavior changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-010, PK-ADR-013, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-026, PK-ADR-031

decisions.title: Preserve independent attributable administrative audit
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSecurity operations ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

An inference trace cannot explain every grant, credential, model, plugin or logging change. Administrative audit is needed to reconstruct authority during incidents. Vendor retention language is not equivalent to customer-controlled tamper resistance or an approved retention schedule.

Options considered

  • Rely on inference logs and dashboard history.
  • Export administrative evidence to a protected customer audit boundary.
  • Use only manual change tickets without runtime evidence.

Proposed decision

Capture named human and automation actions on all security-relevant objects, including denied changes and emergency access. Export to an independently controlled retention/access boundary where supported, and document gaps requiring vendor evidence. Preserve correlation to approved changes and effective runtime revisions without storing secrets. Keep administrative audit retention separate from inference payload logs and do not erase necessary audit by changing a debugging setting.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Audit storage, export monitoring and access review add operating work. Some managed actions may require vendor support evidence. A protected export improves incident reconstruction but still needs completeness and clock/correlation testing.

Required validation

Execute a representative UI/API change sequence and reconstruct actor, target, change, approval and effective outcome. Test export interruption, deletion permissions and retention behavior independently of inference logs.

Acceptance gates: PK-T04, PK-T18, PK-T21, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Management APIs, audit schema, delegated roles, export capability or retention obligations change.

Dependencies PK-ADR-008, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-021, PK-ADR-025, PK-ADR-031

Evidence informing this proposal [PK04] [PK32]

decisions.title: Treat configuration and customer-store migrations as controlled changes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerRelease and data ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The original reference database-migration concern changes under managed administration: customers do not control undisclosed vendor schemas, but still migrate configs, catalogs, log storage, resource indexes and financial ledgers. A successful object import does not prove permission or ownership continuity.

Options considered

  • Assume managed migrations require no customer qualification.
  • Control customer schema/object migrations and verify managed compatibility.
  • Recreate the environment and abandon old resource state.

Proposed decision

Identify every customer-owned schema and every managed object/API version used by the release. Apply customer-store changes through one controlled migration authority with compatibility and recovery plans. Diff legacy-to-catalog grants and config semantics. Obtain vendor compatibility guidance for managed upgrades. Preserve old provider-owned resource mappings during transition. Never run ad hoc concurrent migrations from every serving pod or assume a cache snapshot restores managed state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Migration ownership is explicit but spans vendor and customer teams. Backward-compatible transitions may require temporary dual schemas or routing, adding complexity. Some changes need forward repair rather than rollback and must be flagged before cutover.

Required validation

Rehearse migration with representative grants, jobs, logs and cost records. Interrupt it, recover, verify no broadened access and confirm both old/new clients behave according to the transition contract.

Acceptance gates: PK-T06, PK-T20, PK-T21, PK-T22, PK-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Catalog model, API schema, customer ledger, storage format or management upgrade changes.

decisions.title: Separate health, readiness, freshness and graceful draining
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSRE ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A running process can lack usable credentials or configuration for a cold route. A healthy cached route can still violate the accepted authorization freshness. Long streams and jobs also outlive ordinary HTTP health checks and deployment shutdown windows.

Options considered

  • Use one process-health endpoint for every readiness decision.
  • Define separate liveness, contract readiness, freshness and drain states.
  • Probe all downstream services synchronously on every health request.

Proposed decision

Keep liveness simple and non-destructive. Define readiness for the supported workload class, including required config/secret availability and accepted freshness. Avoid probes that consume billable inference or create cascading outages without need. On shutdown, stop admitting new work, retain completion/accounting paths for accepted work and drain within a bounded period. Classify interrupted streams and durable jobs explicitly rather than treating pod termination as successful cancellation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Readiness is more nuanced than an HTTP 200 and can differ for warm and cold paths. Conservative admission may reduce availability during management incidents. Clear drain and freshness metrics improve safe rollout and prevent silent stale-authority operation.

Required validation

Cold-start with unavailable management/vault/cache, then test warm state, expired objects and a revoked key. Terminate under streams/jobs and prove outcomes, usage and resource ownership remain explainable.

Acceptance gates: PK-T11, PK-T14, PK-T20, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Health checks, configuration cache behavior, workload duration or orchestration lifecycle changes.

decisions.title: Establish multi-zone resilience before regional expansion
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerSRE and platform architectsDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Additional regions introduce new model capacity, credentials, configuration paths, policy propagation and financial domains. A global traffic switch can mask unresolved state and location constraints. Most initial resilience work should establish a dependable single-region service first.

Options considered

  • Deploy globally from the first pilot.
  • Prove multi-zone operation, then add regions for explicit requirements.
  • Run one instance and rely on vendor/provider availability.

Proposed decision

For customer-operated scope, qualify multi-zone runtime and supported state dependencies before adding a second region. Document correlated managed-plane, secret, provider and telemetry failures. Add a region only for an approved continuity or processing-location need, with compatible targets and owner-bound resource recovery. Failover destinations must satisfy the original policy and capacity contract. Test warm and cold recovery, not only load-balancer health switching.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Regional rollout is delayed and some rare outages remain initially out of scope. The staged approach avoids multiplying untested dependencies. Vendor SaaS resilience must be established by contract and observable evidence rather than inferred from a customer topology diagram.

Required validation

Lose a zone, node pool and dependency independently, then perform a region-level exercise after prerequisites pass. Verify authorization, routing location, usage and retained-resource continuity throughout.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T08, PK-T14, PK-T22, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Continuity objective, permitted geography, vendor region support or correlated-failure analysis changes.

decisions.title: Allocate quotas and monetary exposure by enforcement domain
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery & operationsSuggested ownerFinOps and reliability ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A policy named global may be enforced through distributed runtime state whose partition behavior must be verified. Regional failure can lead both regions to accept work against stale totals. Restoring an old counter snapshot can also lower apparent usage without lowering the bill.

Options considered

  • Assume all replicas share an instantaneous global counter.
  • Allocate bounded regional allowances and reconcile them.
  • Use a separately qualified strongly coordinated admission service.

Proposed decision

Identify each native enforcement domain and test its consistency. For strict scope, either use an approved global reservation service or allocate bounded regional exposure with controlled reallocation. Never increase available allowance merely by restoring stale state or adding a region. Define reset windows, currency/pricing assumptions and partition behavior. Treat native counters and reports as evidence inputs rather than proof of a stronger global guarantee.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Regional allocation can leave capacity unused while another region is constrained. Strong coordination adds latency and availability dependencies. Both are legitimate tradeoffs when the accepted financial and continuity contracts are explicit.

Required validation

Submit synchronized requests in multiple regions, partition their coordination, reset periods and restore old state. Show total admitted exposure remains within the agreed bound and all discrepancies reconcile afterward.

Acceptance gates: PK-T14, PK-T15, PK-T16, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Enforcement topology, region count, financial bound, resets or counter recovery changes.

decisions.title: Recover configuration, ownership, accounting and keys together
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerRecovery service ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A runtime can be recreated yet still lack valid policy, provider resource ownership or the ability to decrypt stored state. Restoring obsolete grants or credentials can turn disaster recovery into a security regression. Managed persistence also limits what customers can restore independently.

Options considered

  • Restore only containers and Redis snapshots.
  • Recover an approved dependency-ordered service bundle.
  • Rely solely on vendor support with no customer reconstruction evidence.

Proposed decision

Define recovery bundles for approved declarations, managed exports, runtime artifacts, secret/encryption references, protected audit, resource-owner indexes and required financial state. Record vendor-managed recovery dependencies and acceptable loss/recovery objectives. Restore authority and mappings before reopening ingress; do not resurrect revoked credentials. Reconcile uncertain in-flight work and stale counters. Verify data deletion and retention requirements still hold after recovery.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Complete recovery requires coordination across security, application, finance, SRE and vendor teams. Backup scope and encryption-key availability create operational cost. A successful infrastructure restore is intentionally insufficient evidence of a recovered service.

Required validation

Perform a cold rebuild after key rotation and policy changes, recover jobs and logs, and verify negative permissions before allowing traffic. Demonstrate which components cannot be restored without vendor action and test that escalation.

Acceptance gates: PK-T07, PK-T14, PK-T18, PK-T20, PK-T21, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

State ownership, encryption, export format, retention or continuity objectives change.

Dependencies PK-ADR-009, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-021, PK-ADR-026, PK-ADR-027, PK-ADR-028, PK-ADR-035

decisions.title: Verify artifact provenance and maintain an active patch process
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerPlatform security ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Gateways process provider secrets and untrusted payloads, so dependency and image changes carry security impact. OSS tags, commercial releases and managed tenant updates provide different evidence. An old stable-looking installation example is not a current support or vulnerability guarantee.

Options considered

  • Use moving image tags and trust upstream packaging.
  • Pin approved artifacts and verify available provenance/security evidence.
  • Fork and maintain all runtime dependencies internally.

Proposed decision

Record exact image and chart digests, source/release identity where available, supported platform matrix, available signatures/attestations/SBOMs and accepted exceptions. Verify commercial evidence with the vendor rather than substituting OSS source. Maintain vulnerability and release intake with emergency qualification focused on authentication, destination validation, credentials, tools and resource methods. Avoid unsupported freezes; keep a tested rollback or forward-repair plan.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Verification and patch qualification consume engineering effort and may reveal gaps in vendor evidence. The response to missing attestations must be an explicit risk decision. A private image does not remove responsibility to evaluate its deployment and supported lifecycle.

Required validation

Prove deployed digest matches approval, scan the actual artifact, rehearse an urgent update and verify the controls did not regress. Test that deployment automation refuses an unapproved artifact or reports a governed exception.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T21, PK-T22, PK-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Runtime, dependency, packaging channel, vulnerability or supported platform changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-009, PK-ADR-022, PK-ADR-023, PK-ADR-027, PK-ADR-033, PK-ADR-038

decisions.title: Control plugins, callbacks and custom routes as privileged code
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerPlatform security architectDrafted7 October 2026

Context

An integration can inspect content, invoke networks, access secrets or alter execution even when described as logging or a guardrail. Configuration can also create fan-out or redirect provider credentials. Extensibility therefore expands both the trusted computing base and the data-flow graph.

Options considered

  • Allow workspace-defined plugins and custom hosts freely.
  • Approve a constrained extension catalog with bounded authority.
  • Prohibit all non-core integrations.

Proposed decision

Maintain an approved inventory of callbacks, plugins, custom destinations and beta execution paths. Assign each an owner, purpose, credential scope, permitted data, egress, timeout, resource budget and failure policy. Review executable changes as code, and configuration changes as policy programs. Prevent ordinary workloads from registering arbitrary extensions. Validate output from external services rather than trusting it as control instructions. Require independent release and rollback evidence for security integrations.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Onboarding integrations becomes slower but auditable. Some desired features may need a separate service with stronger isolation. The gateway still depends on its core implementation; restricting extensions reduces rather than eliminates that trust.

Required validation

Cause an integration to stall, return malformed decisions, request forbidden destinations, leak a synthetic credential or fan out excessively. Prove containment and correct request/audit outcomes without broad permission grants.

Acceptance gates: PK-T03, PK-T08, PK-T12, PK-T17, PK-T19, PK-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Plugin code, external service, custom route, feature flag or data recipient changes.

decisions.title: Default-deny MCP and authorize tools at the business boundary
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerTool platform ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Registry access, workspace provisioning, tool enablement, user permission and transaction authorization are distinct. Some retrieved MCP control pages describe forthcoming capabilities. A model-generated tool call cannot be treated as a grant to execute a business action.

Options considered

  • Trust every tool exposed by a provisioned server.
  • Use explicit tool grants plus verified identity and backend authorization.
  • Keep MCP outside the shared gateway until required controls are available.

Proposed decision

Begin with an approved server/tool subset and deny unqualified capabilities. Test both discovery and direct invocation. Forward identity only through an approved verifiable trust path, and require the tool backend to authorize the actual user, resource and action. Bind high-risk approval to exact arguments and enforce domain idempotency. Supply required limits/guardrails independently when not demonstrated by the selected gateway release; do not credit roadmap promises as deployed protection.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Tool services retain meaningful security responsibility and may need an authorization/approval layer. The design limits convenience but prevents registry membership from becoming unrestricted execution. New tool schemas or server behavior require requalification even without gateway changes.

Required validation

Attempt hidden tools directly, forged identity headers, cross-owner objects, replayed writes and chained delegation. Verify missing approvals, limits and invalid arguments stop the action at the backend business boundary.

Acceptance gates: PK-T05, PK-T06, PK-T08, PK-T19, PK-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Tool server, schema, identity forwarding, native control maturity or side-effect permission changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-006, PK-ADR-007, PK-ADR-010, PK-ADR-012, PK-ADR-033, PK-ADR-035, PK-ADR-036

decisions.title: Preserve provider and agent ownership for stateful resources
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerApplication data ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Files, stored responses, batch jobs and A2A tasks belong to an upstream account or service context. A generic resource identifier is not sufficient to route or authorize retrieval. Native and adapted API paths may also provide different persistence behavior.

Options considered

  • Route all resource methods through whichever provider is currently selected.
  • Maintain explicit owner/upstream bindings and lifecycle policy.
  • Expose only stateless inference.

Proposed decision

Bind each retained resource to authenticated owner, workspace, provider/agent endpoint, account, region, creation policy and retention deadline in a durable customer index where needed. Authorize list/read/download/delete independently from inference. Preserve the correct route through credential rotation and migration. Disallow generic cross-provider fallback for owner-bound resources. Specify how to resolve ambiguous creation and how deletion is verified in every actual store.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications acquire lifecycle and recovery responsibilities that a unified API cannot remove. Resource portability may be limited and migration may require draining rather than copying. Stateless workloads remain simpler and should not inherit unnecessary retained state.

Required validation

Test wrong-owner methods, guessed IDs, key rotation, provider changes, lost callbacks and interrupted create/delete operations. Demonstrate recovery of stranded resources without broadening access or duplicating jobs.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T06, PK-T16, PK-T20, PK-T21, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New resource API, persistence feature, credential ownership, migration or retention requirement changes.

decisions.title: Govern batch, media and agent work with separate admission
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerWorkflow service ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Large uploads, asynchronous jobs and agent loops have different resource and financial profiles from short chat requests. Completion can outlive the gateway connection or rollout. Blind retries and unclear ownership create duplicate work and unbounded side effects.

Options considered

  • Apply ordinary chat limits to every workload.
  • Use separate admission classes and durable orchestration.
  • Keep all long-running work outside the gateway.

Proposed decision

Define byte/object, concurrent job, duration, output, tool-call and financial limits per workload class. Persist owner and upstream IDs before treating submission as complete. Resolve ambiguous submission before retrying; verify callbacks and use idempotent settlement. Keep application-owned job state, cancellation policy and business approvals. Admit server-side tool execution or agent recursion only with separately proven bounds and explicit delegation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Durable orchestration and reconciliation add implementation cost. Some workloads remain native/provider-specific rather than fully normalized. Separate pools can protect interactive inference but introduce more deployment and quota allocation work.

Required validation

Crash at upload, submission and completion; repeat notifications; cancel late; rotate credentials and lose a region. Verify no unauthorized resource access, unbounded attempts, hidden charges or duplicate business actions.

Acceptance gates: PK-T06, PK-T10, PK-T15, PK-T16, PK-T19, PK-T20, PK-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Workload size, asynchronous API, agent delegation, provider retention or charging basis changes.

Context

Routing, translation, prompt edits and semantic caching can alter results even when infrastructure is healthy. A gateway cannot establish that an answer is correct for the business or that retrieved documents are authorized for the current user. Quality and safety are application-specific contracts.

Options considered

  • Use transport success as quality acceptance.
  • Maintain versioned task, retrieval and policy evaluations.
  • Delegate all quality judgment to the provider or gateway vendor.

Proposed decision

Assign each application an owner for a representative evaluation corpus, output schema, retrieval permissions, tool behavior and acceptable error classes. Evaluate every approved model/fallback, adapter, prompt and cache change against that corpus. Keep document filtering and business authorization at an authoritative application/service boundary. Use gateway observability as evidence, not a substitute for task outcomes. Promote changes only with recorded quality and operational tradeoffs.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Evaluation requires labeled examples, protected datasets and ongoing maintenance. A technically faster or cheaper route may be rejected for business error risk. Product teams retain responsibility even when configuration is centrally administered.

Required validation

Run candidate and control paths on common fixtures with adversarial, multilingual, malformed, stale and authorization-sensitive cases. Measure downstream corrections and task failures, not only latency, tokens or syntactic validity.

Acceptance gates: PK-T02, PK-T09, PK-T12, PK-T13, PK-T21, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Model, prompt, schema, retrieval corpus, tools, routing or semantic cache changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-004, PK-ADR-011, PK-ADR-014, PK-ADR-016, PK-ADR-021, PK-ADR-022

decisions.title: Contract for exact entitlements, metering and shared responsibility
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerProcurement and service ownersDrafted7 October 2026

Context

Commercial value depends on purchased capabilities, deployment rights, regions and recovery commitments. The current public offering excludes new fully air-gapped Enterprise deployments while supporting existing installations. Gateway charges still differ from provider and inspection costs. [RV01] [RV02]

Options considered

  • Procure from a generic feature checklist and marketing price.
  • Contract against the approved architecture and measurable obligations.
  • Use OSS or native services to avoid the commercial dependency.

Proposed decision

Obtain written confirmation of management product, tenant regions, SaaS/hybrid rights, supported runtime/channel, identity/governance features, log/export/retention behavior, support response and recovery responsibilities. Treat disconnected operation as legacy-contract support, not an assumed new-customer option; a hard new air-gap requirement blocks adoption absent an actually contracted exception. Define gateway metering, retry/cache/error treatment, auxiliary licensing and provider-charge separation. Include termination/export assistance and incident obligations. Make unresolved mandatory terms deployment blockers.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Procurement may take longer and produce a narrower entitlement than the broad product page suggests. The resulting agreement makes total cost and operational dependence explicit. OSS avoids some license fees but does not erase engineering or security ownership costs.

Required validation

Reconcile the contractual bill of capabilities with the runtime acceptance manifest and an example invoice. Test access to support/export paths and obtain confirmation for every hard requirement before production approval.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T15, PK-T16, PK-T21, PK-T23, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Product packaging, acquisition integration, licensing units, region availability, support or deployment terms change.

Amended 8 October 2026 — review R01. Corrects the earlier ambiguous air-gap interpretation using the explicit current deployment restriction. Status remains Proposed; no runtime or procurement acceptance is implied. [RV01] [RV02]

Dependencies PK-ADR-001, PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-020, PK-ADR-023, PK-ADR-031, PK-ADR-040

decisions.title: Qualify performance and SLOs with the actual controls enabled
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerService reliability ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

A proxy microbenchmark does not represent a shared service with authentication, config misses, scans, streaming and usage reporting. Native inference latency can dominate measurements and obscure gateway overhead. Vendor figures are not results for the reference workload.

Options considered

  • Adopt vendor latency/throughput claims as the capacity plan.
  • Run controlled and live comparative tests with full policy enabled.
  • Overprovision without establishing a baseline.

Proposed decision

Use a controlled upstream to measure gateway overhead and failure behavior, then approved live providers for semantic and end-to-end timing. Keep payloads, concurrency, clients, provider targets and policies comparable to the incumbent baseline. Measure tails, completion correctness, rejection, cancellations, resource use, state freshness and operational cost. Test cache misses and degraded dependencies as well as warm happy paths. Treat Nitro as a different contract, not an equivalent benchmark shortcut.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Benchmarks take effort and results apply only to their recorded configuration and workload. They may show no meaningful speed advantage but still reveal administrative or reliability benefits. Capacity targets must be revisited as workloads and features change.

Required validation

Retain load generators, fixture versions, artifact digests, raw timing and failure classifications. Demonstrate sustained mixed traffic, scaling, drain and dependency faults while security and financial gates remain valid.

Acceptance gates: PK-T10, PK-T11, PK-T14, PK-T17, PK-T22, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Runtime, policy stack, workload distribution, provider, cluster size or optimization mode changes.

Dependencies PK-ADR-002, PK-ADR-012, PK-ADR-013, PK-ADR-018, PK-ADR-023, PK-ADR-024, PK-ADR-037

Evidence informing this proposal [PK15] [PK20] [PK39]

decisions.title: Maintain an exit path and an evidence-based decision lifecycle
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaAssurance & exitSuggested ownerArchitecture review ownerDrafted7 October 2026

Context

The organization should be able to replace mediation without losing its application contract, resource ownership, audit or financial history. Managed configuration and provider-specific resources can create practical lock-in even when request syntax is compatible. Proposed decisions need explicit acceptance and review.

Options considered

  • Treat adoption as permanent and leave configuration only in the vendor UI.
  • Preserve portable contracts, artifacts and an exercised replacement path.
  • Avoid all managed capabilities regardless of benefit.

Proposed decision

Retain customer-owned application contracts, config/prompt declarations, identity/grant mappings, evaluation fixtures, owner indexes and required audit/financial exports. Document which vendor features cannot be ported directly and the native fallback or drain strategy for stateful resources. Exercise a bounded alternate gateway/native path periodically. Accept, revise or reject each ADR with named evidence and review dates; do not inherit approval from an earlier product evaluation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Portability work has a continuing cost and cannot make every provider feature interchangeable. It protects negotiation and continuity, while allowing valuable managed capabilities when their exit cost is consciously accepted. Decommissioning must revoke old authority and reconcile retained work, not merely change DNS.

Required validation

Rebuild one approved workload on an alternate path using retained artifacts, verify security/quality behavior, export required histories and demonstrate resource drain/deletion. Confirm the decision register reflects actual accepted scope and unresolved risks.

Acceptance gates: PK-T01, PK-T02, PK-T20, PK-T21, PK-T22, PK-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Contract renewal, service suitability, lifecycle status, export capability or organizational requirements change.

Dependencies PK-ADR-001, PK-ADR-003, PK-ADR-017, PK-ADR-021, PK-ADR-022, PK-ADR-027, PK-ADR-031, PK-ADR-035, PK-ADR-037, PK-ADR-038, PK-ADR-039

decisions.title: Operate a shared Kubernetes gateway only for explicit platform requirements
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerPlatform architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A shared gateway can reduce repeated provider integration, but it adds another production dependency and moves policy authority into a platform service. Existing Kubernetes/Envoy capability makes that composition more plausible; it does not eliminate the need to justify it.

Options considered

  • Direct provider integration per application
  • An AI-native application gateway
  • Agent Router integrated with the existing Kubernetes platform

Proposed decision

Adopt Agent Router only through a bounded pilot tied to named requirements: declarative policy, multi-provider contracts or private inference routing. Keep a direct-provider baseline. Assign service ownership across networking, identity, model operations and application quality before opening access. Do not insert it merely to standardize a URL.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This preserves a clear value test and avoids an unnecessary dependency. It also delays broad self-service until the underlying operating contract is demonstrable; some applications may appropriately remain direct.

Required validation

Compare the same approved workload and policy tests against direct access and one feasible gateway alternative. Account for on-call, integration and release work as well as infrastructure. Record the requirements that cannot be satisfied by the simpler option.

Acceptance gates: AR-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

No measurable incremental value, a new mandatory requirement, or a change in platform ownership.

DependenciesReference requirements and approved ownership.

Evidence informing this proposal[AR04] [AR05]

decisions.title: Qualify the complete runtime and API bundle
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerRelease engineeringDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Agent Router behavior depends on Envoy Gateway, Envoy Proxy, CRDs, processor configuration and optional inference extensions. A stable project tag alone cannot prove the assembled service is compatible or secure.

Options considered

  • Float each dependency independently
  • Pin only the Agent Router image
  • Promote an immutable tested dependency bundle

Proposed decision

Pin chart versions, image digests, CRD schemas, cluster compatibility, runtime flags and client contracts together. Use v1.2.0 as this evaluation’s release baseline, then choose the current approved patch at deployment qualification. Record stable, alpha and preview surfaces separately. Do not import Next documentation into the supported scope without release evidence and tests.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Changes become auditable and reproducible, at the cost of maintaining a cross-project release matrix. Emergency patches still need focused regression tests; an old pinned image is not a long-term security strategy.

Required validation

Render and validate the bundle, inspect actual running images and schemas, verify processor injection and execute representative negative/streaming cases. Record artifact provenance checks as completed evidence only after they actually run.

Acceptance gates: AR-T01 · AR-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Any chart/image/CRD change, security advisory, provider API change or unsupported cluster version.

DependenciesAR-ADR-001

Evidence informing this proposal[AR01] [AR02] [AR10]

decisions.title: Publish a bounded endpoint and capability contract
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerApplication platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

The common client interface spans multiple provider schemas. A path can exist while a required field, event or lifecycle operation remains unsupported on a particular backend. Generic passthrough can also evade assumed processing.

Options considered

  • Expose every accepted path
  • Promise broad client-SDK compatibility
  • Publish a tested endpoint/backend capability matrix

Proposed decision

Expose only approved tuples of endpoint, provider schema/version, model alias and policy mode. Define request limits, unsupported-field behavior, error classification, stream events and retained-resource ownership. Require explicit rejection for unsupported combinations. Treat new modalities, Responses lifecycle and native passthrough as separately reviewed capabilities.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The initial service is narrower but explainable. Applications gain a stable contract; the platform must maintain fixtures rather than relying on a provider-count claim or a single successful chat example.

Required validation

Run positive and negative transformation tests with deterministic upstream fixtures and selected live providers. Verify tool arguments, structured output, reasoning metadata, unsupported fields and provider errors on every approved tuple.

Acceptance gates: AR-T02 · AR-T08 · AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New endpoint/model capability, client SDK assumptions or a provider schema change.

DependenciesAR-ADR-002

Evidence informing this proposal[AR12] [AR13]

decisions.title: Version aliases as application promises
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerModel platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A logical alias hides the physical provider name, but task quality, tokenization, tools, context limits and data location remain observable application properties. A fallback can change those properties without changing the caller’s URL.

Options considered

  • Provider names exposed directly
  • Mutable aliases with no compatibility rule
  • Versioned aliases with eligible target sets

Proposed decision

Define each alias by its intended task, capabilities, limits, location and quality thresholds. Store the approved physical targets with explicit priorities and model overrides. Require a contract revision or compatible canary evidence before changing those targets. Bind provider-owned resources to their original owner rather than routing them through an unconstrained alias.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Applications become less coupled to infrastructure while semantic changes remain visible. Maintaining quality baselines and resource affinity adds work; an inexpensive model is not automatically an eligible replacement.

Required validation

Execute the same task corpus and schema tests on primary and fallback targets. Attempt hidden-alias invocation and cross-provider resource retrieval. Verify actual destination/model labels, not just the requested alias.

Acceptance gates: AR-T02 · AR-T07 · AR-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Model retirement, fallback expansion, embedding-index change or quality regression.

DependenciesAR-ADR-003

decisions.title: Use distinct accountable workload identities
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerIdentity platformDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Sharing a gateway or provider credential across unrelated applications prevents reliable revocation and attribution. Routing headers and model names are not authenticators; a provider key proves backend authority, not the identity of the original caller.

Options considered

  • One shared gateway token
  • Application-supplied tenant metadata
  • Verified per-workload identities with accountable owners

Proposed decision

Give each application/environment a distinct authenticated identity and an owner. Derive tenant and cost descriptors from that identity through controlled mapping. Keep administrative credentials out of runtime clients. Define expiry, rotation, decommissioning and emergency revocation, and use separate break-glass administration with auditing.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Attribution and containment improve, but the organization must operate an identity lifecycle and mapping service. Identity outages now require a deliberate service failure policy rather than implicit anonymous operation.

Required validation

Test expired, revoked and wrong-environment credentials; forged tenant headers; and attempts to use a workload identity for management. Confirm all replicas attribute and deny consistently.

Acceptance gates: AR-T03 · AR-T05. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New tenant type, external users, workload federation or identity-provider migration.

DependenciesAR-ADR-001

Evidence informing this proposal[AR19] [AR34]

Original concernADR-005. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

Options considered One shared gateway token Application-supplied tenant metadata Verified per-workload identities with accountable owners Proposed decision Give each application/environment a distinct authenticated identity and an owner. decisions.title: Separate caller validation from backend delegation
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerSecurity architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A correctly signed token may have the wrong issuer or audience. A delegated credential may be absent, malformed or intended for another backend; fallback to a configured shared key can silently change who authorizes the action.

Options considered

  • Forward incoming credentials generically
  • Allow shared-key fallback everywhere
  • Validate each authority and forbid implicit delegation fallback

Proposed decision

Validate issuer, audience, lifetime and required claims at the caller boundary. Forward only specifically approved backend credentials, preferably through trusted metadata, and deny missing delegated authority on delegation-required routes. Configure metadata forwarding deliberately. Treat MCP issuer and session identity rules as part of the same reviewed authority model, not as optional decorations.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This prevents convenience fallback from escalating privilege. It requires separate client/provider token lifecycles and can reject requests that previously worked using a shared service account.

Required validation

Use wrong-audience/issuer tokens, duplicate headers, missing metadata and partial credentials. Record the credential fingerprint observed by a controlled backend. Verify unverified claims never influence policy.

Acceptance gates: AR-T03 · AR-T05 · AR-T14. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Identity configuration change, new provider delegation method or token-exchange feature adoption.

DependenciesAR-ADR-005

Evidence informing this proposal[AR20] [AR22]

decisions.title: Enforce tenant isolation across configuration and resources
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerPlatform securityDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Tenant separation includes who may change routes, reference credentials, invoke models and access retained objects. Namespaces and hostnames help organize resources but are not sufficient end-to-end security boundaries.

Options considered

  • Hostname-only tenant separation
  • Namespaces without route/reference restrictions
  • Layered identity, RBAC, grants and resource authorization

Proposed decision

Use namespace ownership, restricted route-writing RBAC, receiver-controlled named grants and verified caller policy together. Disallow arbitrary tenant-supplied backend destinations and privileged filters. Check ownership on files, sessions, tools and tasks independently. Escalate to separate gateways or clusters when shared-controller or credential blast radius exceeds accepted risk.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Isolation becomes explicit rather than inferred. More restrictive permissions and separate environments can reduce operational convenience and increase cost; those tradeoffs should be accepted by the risk owner.

Required validation

Test same-name secrets across namespaces, unauthorized reference creation, grant removal, direct hidden-resource access and configuration-write escalation. Verify denied references are absent from effective data-plane authority.

Acceptance gates: AR-T03 · AR-T04 · AR-T18 · AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New trust domain, externally managed tenant, stronger isolation requirement or reference-permission defect.

DependenciesAR-ADR-005 · AR-ADR-006

Evidence informing this proposal[AR07] [AR21]

Original concernADR-007. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Keep administrative authority private and narrowly delegated
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerCluster security ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Kubernetes, controller endpoints, debug configuration and proxy administration can reveal or alter provider access. Sharing an inference hostname with management or granting broad patch rights creates avoidable exposure.

Options considered

  • One combined public administrative surface
  • Network isolation without permission design
  • Private administration plus least-privilege change authority

Proposed decision

Expose only approved runtime routes to application networks. Restrict Kubernetes, webhook, controller, metrics/debug and Envoy administration according to their purpose. Require strong operator identity and audited changes; keep generated configuration within the secret boundary. Separate emergency access from routine route authoring and prevent application teams from changing mandatory security policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Troubleshooting requires approved access paths and sanitized support bundles. The added friction is justified because administrative access can exercise broad provider and tenant authority even without reading a raw key.

Required validation

Probe administrative paths from application networks and test least-privilege roles. Review exported diagnostics for credentials and ensure emergency actions are attributable and reconciled.

Acceptance gates: AR-T04 · AR-T22 · AR-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New management endpoint, support integration, external operator or debug facility.

DependenciesAR-ADR-007

Evidence informing this proposal[AR07] [AR34]

Original concernADR-008. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Manage independent key material and MCP session lifecycle
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerSecret-management ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Provider keys, webhook certificates, telemetry credentials and MCP session-encryption material have different purposes and rotation effects. Restoring an old key or generating a new session seed on every render can undermine safe recovery.

Options considered

  • One shared secret and ad-hoc rotation
  • Chart-generated material without recovery ownership
  • Purpose-specific managed secrets with explicit rotation semantics

Proposed decision

Keep each authority class separate and referenced through the approved secret system. Use stable, non-public MCP session material with controlled rotation; accept session reinitialization rather than retain known-insecure historical material. Define which credentials must rotate after compromise and which resources become invalid. Keep values out of Git, support archives and client logs.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Rotation and restoration require coordination, especially for live MCP sessions. This avoids silently restoring old authority and permits independent containment of provider, telemetry or session compromise.

Required validation

Render twice, restart replicas, rotate the session key and simulate restore with revoked material. Verify intended reconnect behavior, denial of foreign sessions and successful authorized fresh sessions.

Acceptance gates: AR-T05 · AR-T14 · AR-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Credential compromise, key-store migration, rotation-policy change or session protocol update.

DependenciesAR-ADR-006 · AR-ADR-008

Evidence informing this proposal[AR02] [AR22]

Original concernADR-009. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Approve actual egress and processing locations
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaArchitecture and trustSuggested ownerCloud network/security architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Self-operated gateways still contact model providers, identity services, inspectors, tools and telemetry endpoints. A private ingress or CONNECT proxy proves only part of the data path.

Options considered

  • Unrestricted outbound access
  • Provider hostname allowlist only
  • Per-component destination and processing-policy inventory

Proposed decision

Approve destinations for every originating component, including controller identity discovery and credential exchange. Restrict caller-controlled URLs and backend changes. Bind fallback and region selection to data policy; qualify private endpoints and forward-proxy limitations independently. Do not infer provider retention or location guarantees from gateway placement.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Egress policies and new-provider onboarding need coordinated review. Explicit auxiliary-service inventory reduces hidden disclosures, but some features may be excluded when their processing boundaries cannot be accepted.

Required validation

Record destination/SNI/host and identity during normal, fallback, rotation and tooling flows. Probe redirect and arbitrary-backend attempts; test each component in a deny-by-default network.

Acceptance gates: AR-T05 · AR-T07 · AR-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New region/provider/tool, identity-discovery change or data-classification requirement.

DependenciesAR-ADR-007 · AR-ADR-009

Evidence informing this proposal[AR26] [AR32]

Original concernADR-010. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Start with equivalent explicit-priority routing
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerTraffic platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Network health, quota availability and application suitability are different selection inputs. Aggressive routing optimization can send work to an incompatible target or concentrate it beyond safe capacity.

Options considered

  • Cheapest/fastest target without capability constraints
  • Implicit backend ordering
  • Explicit eligible groups with tested priorities and weights

Proposed decision

Route within a prequalified equivalent target set using explicit priorities and bounded distribution. Keep eligibility decisions separate from health and optimization. Evaluate quota exhaustion at the selected backend as its own result; do not assume native quota-aware alternate selection. Integrate an endpoint picker only for a qualified serving pool with verified model identity.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The first design favors predictability over maximal cost optimization. More advanced routing can be added after measuring behavior, but must preserve quality, security and state-affinity constraints.

Required validation

Inject provider failures and quota exhaustion; record actual targets and distribution. Test stale picker metrics, wrong model versions and retained-resource affinity.

Acceptance gates: AR-T07 · AR-T09 · AR-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Need for adaptive placement, changed capacity model or an expanded model contract.

DependenciesAR-ADR-003 · AR-ADR-004 · AR-ADR-010

Evidence informing this proposal[AR15] [AR24]

Original concernADR-011. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.
