decisions.title: Assign one retry owner and a total attempt deadline
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerApplication reliability ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Retries may exist in the SDK, gateway and provider client. Their multiplication creates excess cost, latency and duplicated side effects, particularly after a request has already reached an upstream service.

Options considered

  • Retry independently at every layer
  • Disable all retries
  • One declared owner with bounded recoverable attempts

Proposed decision

Choose one retry owner for inference and propagate a total deadline. Classify failures before retry, cap attempts and re-check each destination’s authority. Do not retry policy denials, unsupported requests, emitted output or ambiguous business actions automatically. Use separate domain idempotency and reconciliation for side effects and asynchronous submissions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some failures reach callers earlier, but duplicate execution and hidden cost are controlled. Integrations must disable or account for lower-level retries rather than relying on unrelated defaults.

Required validation

Count actual upstream calls under every injected failure. Test timeouts after provider acceptance and verify attempt-specific translation, credential use and remaining exposure.

Acceptance gates: AR-T07 · AR-T08 · AR-T11. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New client library, provider retry behavior, routing layer or side-effecting endpoint.

DependenciesAR-ADR-011

Evidence informing this proposal[AR08] [AR15]

Original concernADR-012. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Treat streaming completion as a first-class outcome
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerApplication platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

An initial HTTP success does not establish a complete model response. Streams can carry partial tools, usage at termination and late errors; once content is sent it cannot be retracted.

Options considered

  • Count initial HTTP status only
  • Buffer every response without distinction
  • Explicit streaming state machine and cancellation contract

Proposed decision

Define admitted, started, content-emitted, terminal, canceled and uncertain outcomes per endpoint. Bound idle and total time separately. Do not switch providers after delivering content as though continuing the same generation. Preserve partial-usage uncertainty and release connections deliberately. Buffer only where a preventive policy requires it and the latency/memory cost is accepted.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Clients and telemetry need richer outcome handling. Streaming responsiveness may conflict with preventive output inspection; the application owner must choose the correct service contract.

Required validation

Exercise malformed chunks, LF/CRLF framing, incomplete tools, slow readers and cancellation around terminal usage. Confirm no duplicated content and no assumption that a client timeout cancels upstream billing.

Acceptance gates: AR-T08 · AR-T12. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New stream protocol, output guardrail mode, client behavior or provider usage format.

DependenciesAR-ADR-012

Evidence informing this proposal[AR08] [AR16]

Original concernADR-013. Conceptual coverage; no previous implementation acceptance is inherited.

decisions.title: Qualify preventive checks at exact protocol phases
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerApplication security ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A generic external processor or logging callback is not automatically a complete guardrail service. Endpoint paths, passthrough and streaming can expose different data and different opportunities to block.

Options considered

  • Assume one filter covers all traffic
  • Post-call detection only
  • Named preventive and detective controls by route/phase

Proposed decision

Document each required check’s inputs, position, result contract, timeout and failure behavior. Fail closed where prevention is mandatory. Separate content redaction for telemetry from input/output enforcement. Do not expose an alternate path that bypasses required checks; evaluate inspection egress and buffer limits as part of the design.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Coverage is auditable but requires protocol-specific testing and may add latency. Some routes should stay disabled until enforcement can be demonstrated rather than advertised as universally protected.

Required validation

Use detectable fixtures in model input, output, tool arguments and errors. Stall or corrupt inspector replies and verify exactly which bytes reach provider and caller.

Acceptance gates: AR-T06 · AR-T08 · AR-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New endpoint, inspector integration, policy requirement or streaming enforcement change.

DependenciesAR-ADR-003 · AR-ADR-007 · AR-ADR-013

decisions.title: Keep gateway response caching disabled until isolated
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerApplication data ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

An exact response cache can expose a result created under another tenant’s permissions or an older policy. Provider prompt caching is a different mechanism and does not establish a customer response-reuse contract.

Options considered

  • Cache all successful responses
  • Trust request text as the cache key
  • Disable by default; explicit tenant/policy-bound eligibility

Proposed decision

Leave response caching out of the initial service. Any later cache must include authenticated scope, policy/model version and relevant retrieval authority in its key and eligibility decision. Reauthorize hits, define TTL/invalidation and exclude personalized, confidential or side-effecting requests unless their reuse is explicitly safe. Keep counter Redis separate from payload storage policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The pilot forgoes possible latency/cost savings but avoids a new isolation and retention subsystem. Application-specific caches may remain preferable to a shared gateway cache.

Required validation

Test cross-tenant lookups, revocation, alias updates, retrieval ACL changes, expired data and tool results. Demonstrate privacy and task correctness on hits as well as misses.

Acceptance gates: AR-T13 · AR-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Measured reuse opportunity with a defensible eligibility rule.

DependenciesAR-ADR-007 · AR-ADR-014

Evidence informing this proposal[AR12] [AR16]

decisions.title: Treat semantic reuse as a separate quality-sensitive service
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerApplication quality ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Semantic similarity is not equality of intent, authorization or factual context. A plausible reused answer can be wrong even when its embedding is near the new request.

Options considered

  • Enable a global similarity cache
  • Avoid semantic reuse entirely
  • Application-specific evaluated semantic reuse

Proposed decision

Keep semantic reuse disabled in the reference baseline. Approve it only for a bounded application with a defined false-hit tolerance, tenant isolation, freshness policy and independent quality evaluation. Include embedding-model/version changes and retrieval permissions in invalidation. Never treat a semantic-cache hit as evidence that a provider or gateway answered the current request.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Potential savings are conditional and an additional model/store must be operated. Clear provenance and quality metrics are needed to prevent silent degradation hidden by lower token use.

Required validation

Build adversarial near-neighbor and stale-context examples. Evaluate false hits and task errors separately from hit ratio and latency, including cross-tenant negative tests.

Acceptance gates: AR-T13 · AR-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New domain, changed embedding model, privacy rule or unacceptable false-hit rate.

decisions.title: Use Kubernetes for desired state, not as an invented billing database
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerPlatform data architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

The gateway’s configuration authority is Kubernetes and generated runtime state. Durable application conversations, resource ownership and financial settlements are separate responsibilities that should not be forced into CRDs merely to avoid a database.

Options considered

  • Store all application state in gateway resources
  • Assume stateless gateway means no durable state
  • Separate desired configuration from application/accounting stores

Proposed decision

Keep reviewed gateway configuration in Git and the Kubernetes API, with protected secret references. Define application databases, outboxes and financial records separately where required. Do not claim Agent Router provides a turnkey durable organizational ledger. Regenerate derived proxy/processor artifacts from trusted inputs rather than treating them as the only backup.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Persistence matches each consistency and retention requirement. The organization may need additional stores, but their purpose, authority and failure semantics become explicit.

Required validation

Delete/rebuild generated artifacts and prove reconstruction. Exercise application resource ownership and financial deduplication independently of controller restarts.

Acceptance gates: AR-T15 · AR-T17 · AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New durable resource type, accounting requirement or configuration authority change.

decisions.title: Operate separate allowance and quota coordination contracts
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerUsage governance ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Client allowances and backend/model quotas use different scopes and service configuration. A running Redis instance or enabled addon does not establish that both enforcement paths are active or share one atomic guarantee.

Options considered

  • One assumed universal counter service
  • Local counters per replica
  • Explicitly configured independent RLS responsibilities

Proposed decision

Provision the required client and quota services separately, with reviewed domains, descriptors, Redis clients and failure modes. Bind mandatory quota checks to denial on service loss. Exclude unsupported fields and non-enforcing shadow rules from production control claims. Define counter reset, eviction and failover policies independently of response-cache policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The deployment has more components and monitoring needs. In exchange, the team can explain which service enforces each requirement and detect missing enforcement rather than relying on configuration appearance.

Required validation

Exhaust both scopes, remove each service, mismatch model names and inject Redis failure. Verify effective counter ownership and admitted traffic on every replica.

Acceptance gates: AR-T09 · AR-T10. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Quota API graduation, changed RLS topology, selector/window requirement or region expansion.

decisions.title: Add strict money reservation only for a defined exposure guarantee
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerFinOps architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Completion-time token counters can provide useful operating limits without being a strict pre-dispatch financial ceiling. Prices, retries, media and tool work complicate a monetary guarantee.

Options considered

  • Treat token counters as a hard invoice cap
  • Accept documented operating-budget overshoot
  • Separate conservative reservation for strict workloads

Proposed decision

Classify workloads by required containment. For strict workloads, require a separately owned atomic reservation covering approved prices and attempt envelopes before dispatch, with fail-closed behavior and explicit unknown-cost handling. Use native/provider containment as an additional layer where applicable. Do not invent a built-in gateway guarantee or a precision the provider data cannot support.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The strict path adds state, latency and engineering cost. Workloads with acceptable bounded operational exposure may use simpler allowances, but their risk acceptance must be explicit.

Required validation

Test concurrent near-limit calls, extra attempts, delayed billing after timeout and missing price/usage. Demonstrate the agreed maximum exposure under partition and recovery.

Acceptance gates: AR-T11 · AR-T12. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Changed financial risk tolerance, new billing units, price source or provider containment capability.

DependenciesAR-ADR-003 · AR-ADR-018

decisions.title: Reconcile request, attempt and provider usage independently
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExecution and governanceSuggested ownerFinOps engineeringDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Token usage is an observation, not always a complete bill. Retries, cancellations, cache categories, tools and missing terminal events can create differences between application calls and provider charges.

Options considered

  • Use success counters as billing truth
  • Trust one gateway spend total
  • Deduplicated event model plus independent reconciliation

Proposed decision

Maintain distinct call, attempt, usage and settlement identifiers and explicit outcome confidence. Preserve price versions and units. Reconcile at the strongest supported provider granularity; keep unknown usage visible and investigate material variance. Do not fabricate per-request invoice joins or count a missing event as zero charge.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Accounting becomes explainable at the cost of a reconciliation pipeline and operational ownership. Historical changes remain attributable instead of silently rewriting past estimates with current prices.

Required validation

Compare deterministic fixture truth with events, then provider aggregates with estimates. Inject duplicates, delayed events and partial streams; verify idempotent settlement and bounded backlog.

Acceptance gates: AR-T08 · AR-T12 · AR-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New provider cost category, changed telemetry schema, unacceptable variance or finance reporting requirement.

DependenciesAR-ADR-019

decisions.title: Declare one owner for each configuration layer
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerPlatform configuration ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Input manifests, generated HTTP routes, processor bundles and accepted xDS form different layers. Manual edits to derived objects can disappear or create drift while desired state looks correct.

Options considered

  • Allow edits at any layer
  • Git-only edits without runtime verification
  • Declared input ownership with observed-generation checks

Proposed decision

Git owns reviewed desired resources; controllers own generated configuration. Record effective policy and bundle generations at promotion. Restrict manual changes to an audited emergency process that reconciles back to the source. Do not treat accepted status or a Helm success as proof that every proxy enforces the new rules.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Configuration is more reproducible but runtime observation becomes part of delivery. Emergency repair may require an explicit temporary fork rather than silently changing generated state.

Required validation

Create drift deliberately, reconcile it and compare all runtime replicas. Test rejected updates and prove that the resulting state is the last-known-safe policy rather than a broadened default.

Acceptance gates: AR-T04 · AR-T15. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New controller ownership, configuration source, emergency procedure or policy merge behavior.

DependenciesAR-ADR-008 · AR-ADR-017

decisions.title: Promote releases with a recorded rollback boundary
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerRelease managerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

An image rollback may not reverse CRD, policy or secret changes. Reverting a security-sensitive version can also restore an unsafe behavior even when the old application requests begin succeeding again.

Options considered

  • Automatic image rollback on any error
  • Upgrade all components without staging
  • Versioned promotion with safe rollback and roll-forward options

Proposed decision

Qualify installation, supported upgrade and isolated restoration separately. Promote the dependency bundle through schema, negative-control, failure and canary gates. Record which state can be rolled back, which requires migration and which must be invalidated. Prefer roll-forward or scoped isolation when reverting would restore unsafe authority.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Releases require more evidence and owner coordination. The benefit is an honest recovery plan instead of an assumed inverse operation for every schema or key change.

Required validation

Rehearse the actual version path with representative stored resources, credentials and sessions. Verify both old and new services against current security requirements before authorizing traffic rollback.

Acceptance gates: AR-T01 · AR-T15 · AR-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Security fix, schema conversion, runtime dependency change or failed recovery rehearsal.

decisions.title: Separate runtime blast radius while preserving the processor pair
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerInfrastructure architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Envoy and the external processor cooperate on each request, while different protocols and trust domains have different lifetime and authorization requirements. Sharing everything can spread policy or resource failures.

Options considered

  • One gateway for all protocols and tenants
  • Independent processor farm without qualifying state assumptions
  • Paired runtime units with separate gateways where justified

Proposed decision

Scale Envoy with its qualified external processor as a coupled data-plane unit. Separate LLM, MCP and experimental A2A gateways when filter semantics, trust or resource lifetimes differ. Keep control-plane exposure private. Use stronger cluster separation for untrusted configuration authors rather than relying on hostname rules alone.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More gateways consume resources and require consistent release management. They also make protocol-specific failure, preview experimentation and tenant isolation easier to reason about.

Required validation

Kill one processor, exhaust one protocol’s resources and reject a preview listener update. Demonstrate that unaffected gateway contracts remain valid and no runtime instance bypasses mandatory processing.

Acceptance gates: AR-T06 · AR-T15 · AR-T16. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New protocol, materially different tenant risk, resource contention or processor deployment architecture.

decisions.title: Size pools and autoscaling from observed concurrent work
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerPerformance ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Long-lived streams, large JSON bodies and tool sessions consume resources differently from short requests. Controller churn, proxy workload and inference scheduling also stress separate components.

Options considered

  • Scale on request rate only
  • Reuse demonstration resource values
  • Measure each bottleneck and reserve failure capacity

Proposed decision

Build a workload model from arrival rate, lifetime, payload size and protocol mix. Measure Envoy, extproc, controllers, RLS, Redis and endpoint picker separately. Bound connection pools and queues, set resource requests, and qualify autoscaling plus zone-loss capacity. Do not convert vendor demo throughput or example Helm resources into production sizing.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The team needs representative workloads and performance ownership. Conservative capacity can increase cost but prevents hidden overload caused by independent component ceilings.

Required validation

Run reproducible direct/proxy/full-stack tests, then combined traffic and rolling updates. Report queueing, tail latency, memory, errors and fairness with machine/artifact specifications.

Acceptance gates: AR-T16 · AR-T19. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Workload distribution change, new modality, fleet size increase or capacity incident.

decisions.title: Make metadata-only observability the default
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerObservability and privacy ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Tracing can capture sensitive content and different semantic conventions use different defaults. Caller-controlled labels can also create excessive cardinality or encode private identifiers.

Options considered

  • Export full prompts and results by default
  • Disable observability entirely
  • Approved metadata with explicit content opt-in

Proposed decision

Select and pin one tracing convention, disable message-content capture by default, and allow only approved low-cardinality identity/model attributes. Keep reusable credentials and opaque session material out of every sink. Add content capture only for a separately approved, retained and access-controlled dataset. Bound exporter queues and expose data-loss counters.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Debugging and quality investigation may need controlled sampling rather than full production capture. This reduces privacy exposure and prevents telemetry costs or outages from silently dominating the gateway.

Required validation

Inject synthetic sensitive markers into all protocol paths and search every sink, including errors, retries and MCP. Switch conventions in a test environment and validate both privacy and dashboards.

Acceptance gates: AR-T22. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New exporter, tracing convention, content-capture use case or retention policy.

decisions.title: Keep administrative audit distinct from usage telemetry
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerSecurity operationsDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Operational traces may be sampled, delayed or dropped. They do not replace an attributable record of route, grant, credential and policy changes that determine who can access a provider or tool.

Options considered

  • Infer audit from request logs
  • Keep only deployment commit history
  • Separate change audit tied to effective configuration

Proposed decision

Collect administrative changes from Git/deployment and Kubernetes audit paths with operator identity, change intent and release generation. Preserve security incident evidence in a separately controlled store. Define retention and tamper-resistance requirements independently of model telemetry and provider billing records. Ensure emergency changes are attributable and later reconciled.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The design introduces a dedicated audit lifecycle and storage cost. In exchange, investigators can distinguish a malicious or erroneous policy change from an ordinary inference failure.

Required validation

Perform approved and denied route/grant/secret changes, emergency modifications and rollback. Demonstrate a complete chronology without exposing raw secret values.

decisions.title: Treat CRD evolution as a controlled state migration
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerPlatform release engineerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

CRDs define both accepted input and stored resources. Validation tightening, ownership transfer or version conversion can break updates to existing objects even when data-plane images roll successfully.

Options considered

  • Overwrite CRDs with latest manifests
  • Assume a chart rollback restores all schemas
  • Inventory and qualify storage/validation migrations

Proposed decision

Record served and storage versions, existing objects, conversion behavior and chart ownership before change. Validate representative stored resources against the target schema. Review ownership-transfer and conflict-forcing operations rather than copying them blindly. Keep alpha quota/preview resources outside the stable-core compatibility assumption.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Schema changes need coordination with resource owners and backups. This avoids turning an apparently harmless chart upgrade into a cluster-wide editing or reconciliation failure.

Required validation

Rehearse the supported upgrade path and restoration in isolation, including objects that become invalid under tighter security validation. Document whether rollback can safely read and modify the resulting state.

Acceptance gates: AR-T01 · AR-T15 · AR-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New CRD version, validation change, conversion webhook or resource ownership migration.

decisions.title: Differentiate liveness, readiness and graceful draining
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerReliability engineeringDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A running process can lack current credentials, processing configuration or mandatory admission services. Terminating a ready pod can also truncate long streams or leave uncertain upstream work.

Options considered

  • Use process health as readiness
  • Gate every request on every dependency indiscriminately
  • Role-specific readiness and bounded draining

Proposed decision

Define health by component role. New runtime instances must have trusted configuration and required processing before serving; existing instances follow a qualified dependency-outage policy. Drain long-lived connections within an approved bound, record unfinished calls and do not treat pod termination as proof of provider cancellation. Keep control-plane cache readiness separate from proxy readiness.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Health policies are more complex than one HTTP endpoint and can reduce availability when governance is unavailable. They prevent deceptively healthy but incorrectly configured capacity from receiving traffic.

Required validation

Restart controllers and processors, rotate certificates, scale down with active streams and remove RLS. Verify ingress admission, graceful completion and explicit uncertain outcomes.

Acceptance gates: AR-T08 · AR-T15 · AR-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New dependency, stream lifetime, health contract or orchestration behavior.

decisions.title: Establish multi-zone resilience before adding regions
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerInfrastructure reliability ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Region expansion multiplies policy, identity, counter and retained-resource complexity. Many availability requirements can first be addressed by eliminating single points of failure inside the approved primary region.

Options considered

  • Single-node production
  • Active-active multi-region immediately
  • Qualified multi-zone primary with explicit dependencies

Proposed decision

Spread paired runtimes and critical services across zones; size surviving capacity and test disruption. Include Kubernetes, identity, both RLS roles, Redis and customer stores in the availability design. Prove controller failover, fresh runtime admission and restore procedures before introducing cross-region routing.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This prioritizes simpler, testable continuity but does not cover complete regional loss. The business owner must explicitly accept that boundary until a second-region design is justified and qualified.

Required validation

Remove a zone during representative mixed load and a rolling deployment. Measure correct admission, stream outcomes, counter behavior, recovery and remaining capacity.

Acceptance gates: AR-T10 · AR-T16 · AR-T17. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Regional continuity requirement, data-location split or failure evidence exceeding the accepted boundary.

decisions.title: Allocate regional authority and exposure explicitly
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerRegional platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A second region can continue serving while the first is partitioned, but shared names do not create global atomic budgets or portable sessions. Provider state and processing permissions may differ by location.

Options considered

  • Assume shared aliases imply global state
  • Use a synchronous global dependency for every call
  • Explicit regional allowances and resource affinity

Proposed decision

Define which identities, model targets, quotas and financial allowances each region may exercise during partition. Bind provider resources and sessions to their owners; use reconstruction only where application contracts allow it. Approve regional data flows and failover targets separately. Do not promise both independent operation and globally strict counters without a proven mechanism.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Capacity and budget may be temporarily stranded by conservative partitioning. The benefit is a bounded exposure and understandable continuity contract instead of an unmeasured global-consistency claim.

Required validation

Partition regions, revoke access in one region and fail over stateful operations. Measure combined admission exposure and verify no data/location boundary is crossed.

Acceptance gates: AR-T10 · AR-T11 · AR-T17 · AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New region, change in global financial guarantee or provider state portability.

decisions.title: Restore trusted authority, not every historical session
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerDisaster-recovery ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Backup completeness is not the same as safe restoration. Old manifests, grants, session keys or counters can re-enable revoked access or erase recently consumed allowance.

Options considered

  • Restore all snapshots verbatim
  • Rely on stateless pod replacement
  • Reconstruct trusted configuration and reconcile uncertain state

Proposed decision

Back up desired manifests, schemas, protected key references and customer-owned records as a coordinated inventory. Restore in isolation, regenerate derived artifacts and re-run negative controls. Rotate compromised material and force reauthentication/reinitialization when needed. Record counter-reset exposure and unresolved usage rather than asserting continuity the restored data cannot prove.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Recovery may deliberately sacrifice old sessions or require manual reconciliation. This is preferable to resurrecting unsafe authority under the appearance of a complete restore.

Required validation

Perform a timed restore with revoked keys, stale counters and incomplete application records. Demonstrate current authorization, accepted data-loss boundaries and a traceable exposure estimate.

Acceptance gates: AR-T17 · AR-T21 · AR-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Key-store/schema change, new durable component or failed restoration exercise.

DependenciesAR-ADR-009 · AR-ADR-017 · AR-ADR-027 · AR-ADR-030

decisions.title: Verify release provenance and respond to security changes
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaDelivery and operationsSuggested ownerSoftware supply-chain ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

An AI gateway handles powerful credentials and sensitive content. A familiar project name, registry tag or dependency on Envoy does not prove the provenance or safety of the deployed artifact.

Options considered

  • Trust mutable registry tags
  • Build forks without documented provenance
  • Approved artifacts, dependency inventory and patch process

Proposed decision

Pin and verify artifacts using available publisher evidence and organizational controls; record build/source relationship, dependencies and SBOM where available. Mirror approved artifacts as needed without losing provenance. Monitor supported release/security channels and qualify fixes promptly. Keep custom forks documented and owned; do not assume a security advisory on one component applies identically to every packaging variant.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Verification and patch response require sustained engineering. The organization gains traceability and an explicit risk decision when upstream evidence or support is incomplete.

Required validation

Validate checksums/digests and available signatures, scan the selected bundle, review privileged permissions and rehearse a security-sensitive upgrade with current negative tests.

Acceptance gates: AR-T01 · AR-T23. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Advisory, artifact publisher change, new dependency or internal build process.

DependenciesAR-ADR-022 · AR-ADR-031

decisions.title: Treat runtime extensions and proxy patches as privileged code
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerPlatform security architectDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Envoy patches, custom authorization, body mutation and external processing can change destinations, identities or content. Their placement can bypass a mandatory check even when the route looks valid.

Options considered

  • Allow application-authored arbitrary patches
  • Ban all extension mechanisms
  • Review extensions as privileged platform code

Proposed decision

Limit extension and patch creation to approved operators, with code review, provenance and endpoint-specific failure tests. Document filter order and metadata trust. Separate experimental A2A or other alpha filters from stable traffic. Do not enable runtime optimizations that change backend identity or bypass required processing without integration evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Customization becomes slower but safer. Some desired integrations may require an application-side implementation rather than a broad proxy patch with hard-to-bound effects.

Required validation

Inspect generated filter chains, inject extension failures and demonstrate that an application team cannot disable mandatory identity/guardrails. Test unrelated listener traffic when enabling protocol-specific filters.

Acceptance gates: AR-T06 · AR-T15 · AR-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New plugin/filter, Envoy runtime option, patch API or mandatory policy.

decisions.title: Expose MCP through explicit capabilities and business authorization
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerTool platform ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

MCP aggregation can concentrate many tools and credentials behind one endpoint. A permitted catalog entry or model-generated argument does not establish permission to perform a business transaction.

Options considered

  • Aggregate all backend tools by default
  • Gate discovery but trust invocation
  • Explicit catalog, current identity and independent action authorization

Proposed decision

Approve named backends and capabilities, validate session identity and re-check each invocation. Restrict forwarded headers and credential origin per backend. Treat tools, prompts and resources separately. Keep business-object authorization, approvals and idempotency at the tool service. Review catalog/prefix changes as API changes and do not infer forthcoming protocol features are delivered.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Tool onboarding and catalog drift require ownership. The design avoids granting an agent the full power of every aggregated service and keeps recovery from uncertain side effects in the responsible domain.

Required validation

Test foreign sessions, hidden-tool direct calls, duplicate bare names, wrong audience, revoked grants, unauthorized object arguments and repeated actions. Prove allowed operations still work after key rotation.

Acceptance gates: AR-T14 · AR-T18. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New MCP server, tool schema, protocol version, delegation mechanism or sensitive action.

decisions.title: Bind provider-owned resources to an authenticated owner
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerApplication state ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Responses, files, jobs and sessions may be owned by a provider account or deployment. An opaque ID can be guessed, leaked or supplied by a different tenant; a shared provider key can otherwise expose more than the caller owns.

Options considered

  • Proxy all IDs under a shared credential
  • Force all state into the gateway
  • Application-managed owner and location mapping

Proposed decision

Maintain authenticated owner, provider/account, region, lifecycle and retention mappings for every retained resource exposed to callers. Authorize read/delete/continue separately from initial creation. Preserve affinity through failover or explicitly reconstruct using an approved application workflow. Do not promise cross-provider portability of opaque native state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The application retains a durable mapping service and migration responsibility. This avoids treating a provider object ID as an authorization token or silently orphaning state during gateway replacement.

Required validation

Attempt cross-owner retrieval and deletion, changed-region continuation, duplicate creation after timeout and expired-object access. Verify rollback can still identify the owner of live resources.

Acceptance gates: AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New stateful API, provider retention change, regional failover or data deletion requirement.

decisions.title: Qualify asynchronous and media work independently
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerApplication workload ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Batch jobs, files, images and audio have different payload sizes, cost units and completion times from chat. A successful synchronous gateway test says little about durable submission or delayed financial exposure.

Options considered

  • Expose through generic chat policy
  • Disable all non-chat work permanently
  • Separate workload contracts and durable ownership

Proposed decision

Add each non-chat family through a separate qualification gate. Bound payload and output size, reserve appropriate exposure where required, retain a durable submission/outbox record and reconcile ambiguous acknowledgements. Define cancellation, retention, polling/callback security and result ownership. Keep native passthrough restricted until equivalent controls are demonstrated.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Feature rollout is slower and may need application-side orchestration. It prevents a chat-oriented quota and timeout policy from creating unbounded or untraceable asynchronous work.

Required validation

Submit large/malformed media, interrupt acknowledgements, replay completion events and cancel after dispatch. Confirm ownership, idempotency, billing units and recoverable job state.

Acceptance gates: AR-T02 · AR-T11 · AR-T21. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New modality, provider batch interface, callback mechanism or output-cost category.

Define cancellation, retention, polling/callback security and result ownership. Keep native passthrough restricted until equivalent controls are demonstrated. It prevents a chat-oriented quota and timeout policy from creating unbounded or untraceable asynchronous work. Confirm ownership, idempotency, billing units and recoverable job state. Acceptance gates: AR-T02 · AR-T11 · AR-T21 . Status: not executed. decisions.title: Keep task quality and retrieval permission with the application
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerApplication quality ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A gateway can normalize schemas and route traffic without knowing whether an answer is correct or whether retrieved documents are visible to the end user. Model equivalence is application-specific.

Options considered

  • Approve models from transport tests only
  • Let routing optimize cost without task evaluation
  • Application-owned quality and retrieval contract

Proposed decision

Maintain representative task datasets, retrieval authorization and quality/safety thresholds per alias. Evaluate every fallback and local-serving revision before admission to the eligible set. Treat retrieved content and tool output as untrusted data. Record prompt, model and evaluation versions so regressions can be traced independently of gateway releases.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The platform cannot claim quality from infrastructure conformance alone. Applications retain evaluation work, but avoid discovering semantic incompatibility only after a cost-optimized failover.

Required validation

Run fixed task and adversarial retrieval/tool suites on all eligible models. Separate syntax validity, factual/task success, safety and latency; require owner approval of tradeoffs.

Acceptance gates: AR-T18 · AR-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Model/prompt/retrieval change, new task domain or quality regression.

DependenciesAR-ADR-003 · AR-ADR-004 · AR-ADR-011

Evidence informing this proposal[AR12] [AR24]

decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerPlatform procurement ownerDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Open-source availability and commercial support are different contracts. A similarly named hosted service or enterprise derivative can have another control plane, feature set, license or migration path.

Options considered

  • Assume community software includes an SLA
  • Assume every commercial feature belongs to OSS
  • Explicit distribution, support and responsibility matrix

Proposed decision

Record the exact project, artifacts, deployment model and license in the service inventory. Where support is purchased, obtain coverage for the assembled runtime, dependencies, environments and incident response. Separate provider, Kubernetes and gateway responsibilities. Do not transfer Enterprise/SaaS feature claims into the OSS evaluation without evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Procurement and escalation become more detailed. The organization may choose paid support or a different platform if it cannot own cross-layer incidents; license cost alone does not settle that decision.

Required validation

Run a cross-team incident exercise and confirm escalation ownership. Review support scope, update obligations, offline requirements and exit rights against the actual topology.

Acceptance gates: AR-T23 · AR-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

New vendor contract, derivative distribution, support model or ownership gap.

DependenciesAR-ADR-001 · AR-ADR-002 · AR-ADR-023

Evidence informing this proposal[AR03] [AR04]

decisions.title: Base performance claims on reproducible end-to-end evidence
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerPerformance engineering leadDrafted8 October 2026

Context

Proxy efficiency is only one contributor to user experience. Model latency, streaming duration, policies, retries and serving queues can dominate or hide gateway overhead.

Options considered

  • Rank by implementation language or vendor peak throughput
  • Measure only a single happy-path request
  • Controlled baselines plus representative end-to-end workloads

Proposed decision

Use comparable direct, Envoy-only and full-stack experiments with declared payloads, connection reuse, hardware and retries. Report correctness, tail latency, resource usage, stream completion, fairness and cost together. Qualify private-pool scheduling separately. Do not publish invented performance numbers or infer Agent Router maturity from Envoy deployment history.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The benchmark requires realistic fixtures and workload selection. It produces evidence that informs sizing and selection rather than a flattering but operationally irrelevant maximum throughput.

Required validation

Retain scripts, artifacts, environment and raw aggregates. Repeat with mandatory controls enabled, dependency failures and one-zone loss; inspect whether improvements sacrifice correctness or privacy.

Acceptance gates: AR-T16 · AR-T19 · AR-T20. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Major workload/runtime change, SLO failure or a competing design with measured benefit.

DependenciesAR-ADR-024 · AR-ADR-037

Evidence informing this proposal[AR08] [AR28]

decisions.title: Maintain an exit path and review decisions individually
decisions.disposition: Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
decisions.body:
AreaExtensions and decision lifecycleSuggested ownerArchitecture boardDrafted8 October 2026

Context

A large ADR register is useful only if decisions remain owned and revisited. A shared gateway can become difficult to replace when applications depend on undocumented headers, state IDs or administration workflows.

Options considered

  • Accept all ADRs by publishing the report
  • Treat gateway choice as permanent
  • Evidence-based acceptance with portable client contracts

Proposed decision

Keep every record Proposed until its accountable owner accepts the evidence or explicitly narrows scope. Maintain an organizational endpoint contract, exportable policy inventory and resource-owner mapping. Rehearse one alternative path with the same fixture corpus. Review lifecycle, support, economics and unresolved risks at scheduled architecture checkpoints and after material incidents.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The platform retains some portability engineering and decision administration. That cost limits accidental lock-in and prevents draft documentation from being mistaken for production certification.

Required validation

Run the client contract against another feasible gateway/direct provider path, inventory nonportable features and estimate migration effort. Verify every accepted ADR links to current evidence and an owner.

Acceptance gates: AR-T23 · AR-T24. Status: not executed.

Revisit trigger

Contract renewal, major platform change, security incident, ownership shift or materially better alternative.

sections.title: 1. The authoritative baseline
sections.intro: Use this matrix before following an example or making an implementation claim. “Current” means the most recent delivered artifact in this body of work , not the latest market release or an accepted production system.

sections.title: 2. Coverage, preservation and version precedence
sections.intro: The inventory covers 74 delivered files and 627 archive-member occurrences , representing 510 unique byte-identical artifacts . It includes 42 distinct HTML artifacts , of which 30 are documentation and 12 are applications, plus contracts, evidence, source, tests, screenshots, patches and the original packages. Every available source occurrence maps to a preserved object and SHA-256 in the inventory. Exact duplicate bytes are stored once in the preservation collection; original package bytes and runnable current distributions retain their original context.

sections.title: 3. Product goal and bounded pilot
sections.intro: Aperture should expose a coherent service journey: describe intent, validate constraints, obtain independent approval, activate the approved contract, execute within authority, and explain the resulting evidence . The same conceptual resources should be visible in the UI, automation interfaces, request evidence and financial attribution. The viewing filter is a convenience; it is never an authorization grant.

sections.title: 4. Architecture: current reference versus proposed destination
sections.intro: The target design separates Control API, Control Worker, Execution Kernel and Admission Service roles. It places service contracts, policy compilation, governed releases and financial authority under explicit ownership. It originally proposed a small Go kernel with build-time adapters and PostgreSQL/RLS defense in depth. These remain proposals , not descriptions of the current R14 distribution. Architecture , AP-ADR-003 , AP-ADR-004

sections.title: 5. Component and capability alignment
sections.intro: The table distinguishes an implemented local capability from a demonstration, candidate or proposal. “Implemented reference” does not mean production-qualified.

sections.title: 6. Identity, tenancy and authority
sections.intro: In server mode, the browser does not select its effective role. Current server-side membership defines tenant/workspace visibility and command authority. A workload credential is a separately approved, single-service authority; revoking a creator’s human session does not automatically revoke every independently approved workload. Reads, exports, commands and eligible replay require current scope rather than trusting an earlier cached UI state. Identity guide , current security source

sections.title: 7. One change grammar, distinct states
sections.intro: The user-facing progression is Draft → Validate → Review → Approve → Activate → Observe . Those words describe distinct events. An approved change can still be stale, fail activation or lack runtime health evidence. A local content fingerprint binds what was reviewed; it is not a cryptographic signature, independent attestation or immutable external audit.

sections.title: 8. Execution, uncertainty and cancellation
sections.intro: A logical request intent, durable dispatch record, execution attempt and receipt are different identifiers and states. The local reference can queue synthetic work transactionally with its reservation. Before dispatch, current authority is rechecked. Once durable dispatch intent exists, a crash or uncertain outcome must not become a fresh automatic execution. Persistent core guide , current domain implementation

sections.title: 9. Financial semantics and optimization
sections.intro: Rate allowance, spending reservation, accrued liability and provider billing are separate contracts. The local reference tracks tenant-level financial authority with integer micro-units, held exposure and journal adjustments. Pending/unknown exposure reduces available allowance. A known request-total settlement does not invent missing attempt-level attribution. An acknowledged overrun records liability and restricts further admission; it does not discard the excess to keep a dashboard below budget. Current finance schema , domain implementation

sections.title: 10. Operating continuity, readiness and restore
sections.intro: Installation mode does not activate a service, restore a credential or settle money. Pausing inference is not a notification kill switch. Reviewed route disable or process stop provides separate delivery containment. A restored branch must not automatically send historical notifications. Operations guide , current notification guide

sections.title: 11. Durable signals and governed delivery
sections.intro: The server-side observer evaluates three fixed rules on its own schedule: unknown financial exposure aged at least 60 seconds, queued work aged at least 120 seconds, and at least five denied receipts in a workspace within five minutes. Its nominal interval is ten seconds. Those are reference rules, not accepted enterprise response-time commitments or a general user-programmable automation engine. Signals guide , source

sections.title: 12. LiteLLM correction and qualification boundary
sections.intro: The pinned source correction addresses two duration behaviors. Multi-day hour/minute/second reset paths dropped whole elapsed days during rollover. Prefix parsing accepted malformed input such as 1ms as one minute and 1h30m as one hour. The patch preserves day quotient/remainder and requires complete matching. Its scheduler still preserves the legacy invalid-input fallback; it does not provide a new universal fail-closed scheduling API. Code review , patch

sections.title: 13. Contracts and source-of-truth map
sections.intro: The current persistent OpenAPI contains 37 HTTP operations and 52 schemas . The mock catalogs, public target sketches and Python candidate interface are different surfaces. Never generate a production client from the mock API or publish a target sketch as an implemented endpoint.

sections.title: 14. User experience and research continuity
sections.intro: The nine server-backed views are My work, AI services, Change center, Workload access, Request lab, Request explorer, Spend & allowances, Audit trail, and Runtime & scope . They implement a constrained reference journey rather than every feature visible in the fifteen-screen mock. Server console source

sections.title: 15. Safe package use and migration
sections.intro: From the extracted consolidation package, enter the unchanged R14 distribution , not the candidate or an archived older package:

sections.title: 16. Evidence ledger: retained versus newly checked
sections.intro: Evidence is attached to a source/version and a test mode. Do not add these counts across releases. Suites overlap; source versions differ; assertions, parametrized tests, subtests, document checks and participant outcomes are different units.

sections.title: 17. Decision register and alignment dispositions
sections.intro: The consolidated register contains 352 full records : 304 product-specific comparative ADRs, 40 Aperture ADRs and eight LiteLLM review amendments. It keeps original IDs, full content, ownership suggestions, rationale and source links. All remain Proposed . Counts refer to canonical records, not repeated copies of the same ADR in successive reports.

sections.title: 18. One roadmap and one promotion decision
sections.intro: The earlier milestone sequence and successive release-specific “next steps” now resolve to the following gated plan. Receiver qualification remains necessary before meaningful-data webhook egress, but is not the sole platform-wide next step after the separate LiteLLM candidate appeared.

sections.title: 19. Terminology and ownership
sections.intro: Owner roles are suggestions, not assigned people. The platform owner approves scope; security/identity owners qualify authority; finance owners accept reservation and reconciliation semantics; operations owners accept failure/recovery; product/research owners accept usability evidence; application owners define acceptable outcomes. None of those approvals is fabricated in this collection.

sections.title: 20. Corrections, integrity and maintenance
sections.intro: The alignment register records actual corrections and boundary clarifications with affected sources, current wording, evidence and remaining work. It includes the stale R10-current evidence pointer in R14 architecture, the receiver-first immediate roadmap, proposed Go runtime versus reuse, browser/server feature parity, distinct API surfaces, separate egress rules, legacy state names, non-additive test counts and historical comparison freshness.

sections.title: 21. Complete operational review and SOP library
sections.intro: Open the self-contained operational review . It is the current operational supplement to this handbook. The underlying runtime remains R14, with synthetic inference and no installed unified telemetry exporter.

testing_method.runtime: Unmodified preserved R14 Store/Application, temporary SQLite fixtures and synthetic data. No model calls or actual receiver delivery.
testing_method.read_only_assurance: Diagnostic tool uses mode=ro, query_only, bound scope, allowlisted query IDs, BEGIN snapshot and bounded execution. Fixture database hashes unchanged by read diagnostics. Input-state preparation is restricted to temporary test files.
testing_method.financial_cases: Exact independent ledger aggregates, null cost with retained Unknown exposure, separate actual mocked settlement preserving response_observed=false, and valid Unknown job history after reconciliation.
testing_method.scope_cases: Cross-tenant/workspace refusals; no credential/hash/body columns returned; changed and revoked queued identity bindings; explicit row truncation; counts beyond 200 recent UI rows.
testing_method.browser: Native file navigation was attempted and blocked with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR. Unchanged HTML was injected into fresh Chromium about:blank pages; no application transport bridge or script rewriting was used.
testing_method.rendering: No external asset requests and no JavaScript page errors on the exercised document paths. DOM print expansion checked; physical pagination was not certified.

not_executed: promtool rule parsing/evaluation and native rule fixtures
amtool routing validation and receiver dispatch
